69557.e: The year 1447 began at the end of June 2025. Because the lunar year is about 11 days shorter, 1448 began around mid-June 2026.
69557.m: In summer 2026 the Islamic year 1448 began.

69558.q: Which festival ends the fasting month of Ramadan?
a: The Festival of Breaking the Fast
69558.e: The Festival of Breaking the Fast (Eid al-Fitr) is celebrated on 1 Shawwal. In Turkey and the Balkans it is also called Ramazan Bayramı or the Sugar Festival.
69558.m: Ramadan ends with the Festival of Breaking the Fast.

69559.q: On which day of the month of Dhu al-Hijjah does the Festival of Sacrifice begin?
69559.e: The Festival of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha) commemorates Abraham’s willingness to sacrifice his son. It begins on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah and lasts several days.
69559.m: The Festival of Sacrifice begins on the tenth day of the last Islamic month.

69560.q: Why do Islamic festivals such as Ramadan shift each year compared with our calendar?
a: Because the Islamic lunar year is about 11 days shorter
Because the Islamic lunar year is about 11 days longer
Because each country chooses the date freely
Because they are calculated from the solstice
69560.e: The Islamic year has twelve lunar months with about 354 days altogether. That is why festivals such as Ramadan move through all the seasons.
69560.m: Islamic festivals move because the lunar year is shorter.

69561.q: Which calendar does Saudi Arabia follow for religious purposes such as Ramadan?
69561.e: The Islamic lunar calendar applies for religious purposes. Since 2016, however, Saudi Arabia has paid civil service salaries according to the Gregorian calendar.
69561.m: In Saudi Arabia, religious dates follow the lunar calendar.

69562.q: Which festival begins the year in the official Iranian solar calendar?
69562.e: Iran uses a solar calendar that also starts from the Hijra. The New Year, Nowruz, falls on the spring equinox around 20 or 21 March.
69562.m: The Iranian year begins with Nowruz in spring.

69563.q: What traditionally determines the start of a month in the Islamic calendar?
69563.e: A month begins when, after the new moon, the first thin crescent (hilal) is seen in the evening sky. Some countries now also use astronomical calculations.
69563.m: An Islamic month begins with the new crescent moon.

69564.q: Which state was created in 1947 as a homeland for the Muslims of British India?
69564.e: Pakistan was created when British India was partitioned. The poet and philosopher Muhammad Iqbal, who wanted to renew religious thought in Islam, is regarded as its spiritual father.
69564.m: Pakistan was created in 1947 as a state for India’s Muslims.

a: The idea of uniting all Muslims politically
The teaching of God as the only God
The separation of state and religion
The spread of Islam to America
69565.e: In the 19th century Jamal al-Din al-Afghani called on Muslims to unite against European colonialism. He is regarded as the founder of pan-Islamism.
69565.m: Pan-Islamism aimed to unite Muslims against colonialism.

69566.q: What did 19th-century Islamic modernists such as Muhammad Abduh mainly want to show?
a: That Islam and reason are compatible
That the Quran should be abolished
69566.e: The modernists wanted to combine Islam with reason and modern science. To this end Muhammad Abduh also reformed teaching at Al-Azhar.
69566.m: Islamic modernism combined faith and reason.

69567.q: How did the Indian reformer Sayyid Ahmad Khan want to strengthen Muslims in the 19th century?
a: With modern education on the British model
With an uprising against the British
By returning to the Mughal Empire
69567.e: In 1875 Sayyid Ahmad Khan founded a college in Aligarh on the British model. It became Aligarh Muslim University.
69567.m: Sayyid Ahmad Khan relied on modern education for Muslims.

69568.q: Why did the Egyptian Quran scholar Nasr Hamid Abu Zayd have to go into exile in 1995?
a: A court declared him an apostate because of his interpretation of the Quran
He had been convicted of tax fraud
He had lost his Egyptian citizenship
69568.e: Abu Zayd also saw the Quran as a text that must be interpreted in the context of its time and language. After the ruling he went to Leiden University in the Netherlands.
69568.m: Nasr Hamid Abu Zayd interpreted the Quran with methods of literary studies.

69569.q: With which methods did the thinker Mohammed Arkoun want to study Islamic traditions?
a: With methods of history and linguistics
Only with the rulings of earlier scholars
69569.e: Mohammed Arkoun taught at the Sorbonne and developed a “critique of Islamic reason”. For this he used history, linguistics and anthropology.
69569.m: Mohammed Arkoun called for a critical study of Islamic thought.

69570.q: How did Ali Shariati, a leading thinker of the Iranian Revolution, interpret Shiism?
a: As a religion of resistance against oppression
As a teaching of withdrawal from politics
As a support of the Shah’s monarchy
69570.e: Ali Shariati studied in Paris and inspired many young Iranians before 1979. He died in England in 1977, shortly before the revolution.
69570.m: Ali Shariati is regarded as a leading thinker of the Iranian Revolution.

69571.q: When interpreting the Quran, what did the Pakistani scholar Fazlur Rahman want to understand first?
a: The historical context of the verses
The numerical values of the letters
69571.e: Fazlur Rahman wanted to work out the basic principles of the Quran from their historical context. They were then to be applied to the present.
69571.m: Fazlur Rahman combined Quran interpretation with historical thinking.

69572.q: Under whose rule did Islam spread in Bosnia from the 15th century?
69572.e: The Ottomans conquered Bosnia in 1463. In the following decades many local people converted to Islam.
69572.m: Islam came to Bosnia with the Ottomans.

69573.q: What is a traditional Islamic school called, such as the one that has existed in Sarajevo since 1537?
69573.e: The Gazi Husrev-beg Madrasa was endowed by Gazi Husrev-beg and has educated pupils for almost 500 years. The mihrab is the prayer niche and the minbar the pulpit of a mosque.
69573.m: A madrasa is an Islamic school.

69574.q: Which religions mainly shape Bosnia and Herzegovina?
69574.e: The Bosniaks are mostly Muslims, the Serbs Orthodox and the Croats Catholic. The Muslims have their own head, the Reis-ul-Ulema.
69574.m: Bosnia is home to Muslims and Orthodox and Catholic Christians.

69575.q: Which state recognised Islam as a religious community with an Islam Act in 1912, after annexing Bosnia?
69575.e: Austria-Hungary had annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1908. The Islam Act of 1912 is still a basis for the recognition of Islam in Austria today.
69575.m: Because of Bosnia, Austria recognised Islam as early as 1912.

69576.q: What share of the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina described themselves as Muslim in the 2013 census?
69576.e: According to the 2013 census, 50.7 per cent were Muslims. There are also mainly Orthodox Serbs and Catholic Croats.
69576.m: About half the people in Bosnia and Herzegovina are Muslim.

69577.q: What is the Arabic script called in which Bosnian was also once written?
69577.e: Arebica is an Arabic script adapted to Slavic sounds. From the 15th to the early 20th century it was used mainly for religious and popular texts.
69577.m: With Arebica, Bosnian was written in Arabic letters.

69578.q: What happened to many mosques during the Bosnian War from 1992 to 1995?
a: They were sold by the state
They were dismantled and moved abroad
69578.e: Many mosques were blown up during the war, such as the 16th-century Ferhadija in Banja Luka. It was rebuilt using recovered original stones and reopened in 2016.
69578.m: Many mosques in Bosnia destroyed in the war have been rebuilt.

69579.q: Which crime does the Potočari memorial near Srebrenica commemorate?
a: The burning of the National Library
The destruction of the Mostar bridge
69579.e: In July 1995 Bosnian Serb troops killed about 8,000 Bosniak men and boys. International courts classified the crime as genocide.
69579.m: Srebrenica stands for the 1995 genocide of Bosniaks.

69580.q: What is the Chinese-speaking Muslim ethnic group of China called?
69580.e: The Hui speak Chinese and live in many parts of the country. Some are descended from Arab, Persian and Central Asian traders who married Chinese women.

69581.q: What is an “autonomous region” in China, such as Ningxia or Xinjiang?
a: An area with certain special rights for a minority
69581.e: Autonomous regions are named after minorities, for example Ningxia after the Hui. In practice, however, the central government in Beijing decides.
69581.m: Ningxia is the autonomous region of the Hui.

69582.q: What is typical of the Great Mosque of Xi’an?
a: It is built in the style of a Chinese temple.
It is built entirely of mud.
It stands on an island in the river.
69582.e: The mosque has curved roofs, courtyards and a pagoda instead of a minaret. It shows how Islam in China adapted to local architecture.
69582.m: Many old mosques in China look like Chinese temples.

69583.q: Which Muslim ethnic group shapes the city of Kashgar in Xinjiang?
69583.e: Kashgar was for a long time the religious and cultural centre of the Uyghurs. It is home to the Id Kah Mosque, the largest mosque in China.
69583.m: Kashgar is an important Uyghur city.

69584.q: In which southern Chinese port city is the Huaisheng Mosque, one of the oldest mosques in China?
69584.e: Arab and Persian sea traders reached Guangzhou early by sea. According to tradition, the Huaisheng Mosque dates back to the Tang period.
69584.m: One of China’s oldest mosques is in Guangzhou.

69585.q: Which two Muslim ethnic groups are the largest in China?
69585.e: China recognises ten mainly Muslim ethnic groups, together more than 20 million people. The Hui and the Uyghurs make up the largest part.
69585.m: The Hui and Uyghurs are China’s largest Muslim ethnic groups.

69586.q: From roughly which year have the media and UN bodies reported on internment camps for Uyghurs in Xinjiang?
69586.e: China calls the camps vocational training centres. A 2022 report by the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights spoke of possible crimes against humanity.
69586.m: Since 2017 there have been reports of camps for Uyghurs in Xinjiang.

69587.q: What is the policy called with which the Chinese government wants to adapt religions to Chinese culture?
69587.e: Since 2015 the government under Xi Jinping has called for the sinicisation of religions. As a result, domes and minarets have been removed or rebuilt on many mosques.
69587.m: Sinicisation is meant to make religions in China more Chinese.

69588.q: Who chairs the meetings of the municipal council?
69588.e: The mayor (Gemeindepräsident or Gemeindepräsidentin) is the head of the municipal council and chairs its meetings.
69588.m: The mayor leads the municipal council.

69589.q: Who often speaks for the whole municipality when guests come?
a: A child in the first class
69589.e: The mayor represents the municipality to the outside world. For example, he welcomes guests from other municipalities.
69589.m: The mayor represents the municipality to others.

69590.q: What does the mayor get for their work?
69590.e: Mayors get money for their work for the municipality. In large municipalities it is a salary, in small ones often an allowance.
69590.m: The mayor is paid for their work.

69592.e: Usually the voters elect the mayor. Nobody is simply given this office or inherits it.

69593.q: What does a mayor do if they are not re-elected?
69593.e: In a democracy the people decide. Anyone who is not re-elected hands the office over peacefully to the new person.
69593.m: In a democracy, you hand over an office peacefully after losing an election.

69594.q: Where does the mayor usually have her office?
69594.e: The administration and the leadership of the municipality work in the town hall. The mayor's office is there too.
69594.m: The mayor works in the town hall.

69595.q: Can you write a letter with an idea to the mayor?
69595.e: Everyone may tell the municipality their ideas and wishes, including children. The mayor is often happy to read such letters.
69595.m: Children may also write to the municipality with their ideas.

69596.q: What is the municipal council in a village?
69596.e: In most villages, the municipal council runs the municipality. It is like a small government for the village.
69596.m: The municipal council is the village's government.

69597.q: Does the municipal council also have to obey the laws?
a: No, it is above the law
Only when the police are watching
69597.e: Under the rule of law, the laws apply to everyone, including the government of a municipality.
69597.m: The municipal council must obey the laws too.

69599.q: How does the municipal council decide if not everyone agrees?
69599.e: The members of the municipal council vote. What the majority wants then applies to everyone.
69599.m: In the municipal council, the majority decides.

69600.q: Who often gives a club permission for a festival on the village square?
69600.e: Public squares usually belong to the municipality. That is why a club needs a permit from the municipality for a festival there.
69600.m: For a festival on a public square you need a permit from the municipality.

69601.q: In small municipalities, do municipal councillors usually do the job only on the side?
a: No, they work day and night
No, they still go to school
They do not work at all
69601.e: In small municipalities, councillors usually have another job. They do the office on the side, which is called the militia system.
69601.m: Many municipal councillors have a normal job alongside the office.

69602.q: Who belongs to the municipal council together with the mayor?
a: All the children in the village
69602.e: The municipal council is made up of several elected people. The mayor is one of them and leads it.
69602.m: The municipal council has several elected members.

69603.q: Does the municipal council have to do what the municipal assembly has decided?
a: Yes, it has to carry it out
69603.e: The municipal assembly decides, and the municipal council carries out the decision. The people have the final say.
69603.m: The municipal council carries out what the people have decided.

69604.q: What is a municipal assembly called that takes place in addition for an urgent topic?
69604.e: Normally there are fixed dates in the year, the ordinary municipal assemblies. If something important cannot wait, the municipal council calls an extraordinary municipal assembly.
69604.m: For urgent business there is an extraordinary municipal assembly.

69605.q: The municipal assembly votes against a new village fountain. What happens?
a: The fountain is made twice as big
The municipal council builds it secretly
69605.e: If the majority says no, the proposal is rejected. The municipal council has to keep to this decision.
69605.m: What the municipal assembly rejects is not done.

69606.q: Why do some playgrounds have a fence?
a: So that small children do not run into the road
So that the birds stay outside
69606.e: A fence with a gate protects small children, especially if the playground is next to a road. It often keeps dogs out too.
69606.m: A fence protects children on the playground from the road.

69607.q: At a municipal assembly, how do you show that you want to say something?
69607.e: Anyone who wants to say something asks to speak. The chair then gives them the floor, and they often speak at a microphone at the front.
69607.m: At the assembly you only speak once you have been given the floor.

69608.q: What is often held after a municipal assembly?
69608.e: In many municipalities the municipality invites people to an apéro after the assembly. There people stay and chat together.
69608.m: After the municipal assembly people often meet for an apéro.

69609.q: What kind of democracy is a municipal assembly?
69609.e: At the municipal assembly the voters decide for themselves. This is called direct democracy.
69609.m: At the municipal assembly the people decide directly.

69610.q: Who often clears branches from the municipal roads after a storm?
69610.e: After a storm there are often branches and stones on the roads. The people from the works department clear them away so that everyone can drive safely again.
69610.m: After a storm the works department clears the roads.

69611.q: At a municipal assembly, may you have a different opinion from the municipal council?
69611.e: In a democracy you may say your opinion freely. At the assembly you can speak and vote against a proposal.
69611.m: At the municipal assembly you may say your opinion freely.

69612.q: In a municipality, who pays for the school building with their taxes?
69612.e: The money for the school building comes from the taxes paid by residents and companies. So everyone pays for the school together.
69612.m: With taxes, everyone pays for the school together.

69613.q: Do parents have to pay for exercise books at a state school?
a: No, the school pays for them
Yes, the children pay with their pocket money
69613.e: State schools in Switzerland are free of charge. School materials are paid for with taxes.
69613.m: At a state school you get school materials for free.

69614.q: What does a municipality often spend the most money on?
69614.e: School buildings, materials and salaries cost a lot. That is why the school is the biggest expense in many municipalities.
69614.m: The school often costs a municipality the most money.

69615.e: Teachers’ salaries are paid with tax money. Depending on the canton, the canton and the municipalities share the costs.
69615.m: Teachers’ salaries are paid with tax money.

69616.q: Do companies also pay taxes to the municipality?
69616.e: Not only people but also companies pay taxes. This money helps the municipality pay for things like schools.
69616.m: Companies also pay taxes to the municipality.

69617.q: What does a municipality buy with tax money for PE lessons?
69617.e: The municipality equips the gym with apparatus. This is paid for with tax money.
69617.m: Gym equipment at school is bought with tax money.

69618.q: Why do people without children also pay taxes for schools?
a: Because they don’t buy exercise books
Because they live in the school building
69618.e: Well-educated people later help the whole community. That is why everyone contributes to schools.
69618.m: Good schools help the whole community.

69619.q: What do you call money you pay to the state for shared tasks?
69619.e: Taxes are money for shared tasks such as schools, roads and the fire brigade. The Confederation, cantons and municipalities collect taxes.
69619.m: Taxes pay for shared tasks like schools.

69620.q: What does the fire brigade use to free people trapped in a car after an accident?
69620.e: With the strong rescue cutters the fire brigade can cut through car doors and metal. This way trapped people can be safely got out.
69620.m: The fire brigade frees trapped people with rescue cutters.

69621.q: What is the person who leads a fire brigade called?
69621.e: The fire brigade is led by the commander. They lead the call-outs and the training exercises.
69621.m: The fire brigade is led by a commander.

69622.q: What does the fire brigade use to reach a window on the top floor?
69622.e: The turntable ladder can be extended a long way and turned. This way the fire brigade rescues people from high floors.
69622.m: With the turntable ladder the fire brigade reaches high windows.

69623.q: Why do firefighters wear breathing apparatus in smoke?
69623.e: Smoke contains poisonous gases. With breathing apparatus firefighters get clean air from a cylinder.
69623.m: Smoke is poisonous, so firefighters wear breathing apparatus.

69624.q: What do firefighters wear on their heads for protection?
69624.e: The fire helmet protects against falling objects and heat. It often has a visor for the eyes.
69624.m: Firefighters protect their heads with a helmet.

69625.q: What can you use to quickly put out a small fire in the kitchen?
69625.e: You lay a fire blanket over a burning pan. The fire then gets no more air and goes out. You must never pour water on burning oil.
69625.m: A fire blanket smothers a small fire.

69626.q: Why does the fire brigade train regularly?
a: So that everything works in an emergency
69626.e: In a real fire every move has to be right. That is why firefighters train regularly.
69626.m: The fire brigade trains so it can help quickly in an emergency.

69627.q: What does the fire brigade use to bring water to the fire?
69627.e: The hose carries water from the hydrant or the fire engine to the fire. At the end there is a nozzle.
69627.m: The fire hose brings water to the fire.

69628.q: Where must you never park a car, so the fire brigade can always get water?
a: In front of your own house
69628.e: In an emergency the fire brigade must be able to reach the hydrant at once. That is why parking in front of one is forbidden.
69628.m: You must not park in front of a hydrant.

69629.q: Who puts up new road signs in many municipalities?
69629.e: The works department looks after the municipal roads. This includes signs and road markings.
69629.m: The works department takes care of signs on municipal roads.

69630.q: In Switzerland, what is a place called where you can borrow games and toys?
69630.e: At a ludothek you can borrow board games, ride-on toys and other toys for a few weeks. The word comes from the Latin ludus, which means game.
69630.m: At the ludothek you borrow games and toys.

69631.q: Who puts up the Christmas lights in many villages?
69631.e: Using tall ladders and lifting platforms, the works department hangs the Christmas lights in the streets.
69631.m: The works department often decorates the village for Christmas.

69632.q: Who cleans the village fountain in many municipalities?
69632.e: Village fountains usually belong to the municipality. The works department cleans them regularly so they stay nice and clean.
69632.m: The works department keeps the village fountains clean.

69633.q: Who trims the hedges along municipal paths in many municipalities?
69633.e: Hedges along public paths must not grow into the way. The works department cuts them back regularly.
69633.m: The works department trims hedges along public paths.

69634.q: Who plants the flower beds in the village in many municipalities?
69634.e: The works department looks after the public green spaces. This includes planting flowers in beds and planters.
69634.m: The works department plants the flowers in the public beds.

69635.q: What vehicle does the works department often use for many jobs?
69635.e: The works department has small, powerful vehicles. A snowplough, a brush or a mower can be fitted to the front.
69635.m: The works department often works with small, powerful vehicles.

69636.q: What does the head of the works department do?
69636.e: The head of the works department plans who mows, cleans or clears snow and when. He hands out the work to the people in the department.
69636.m: The head of the works department runs the department.

69637.q: Where do you take empty PET drinks bottles?
69637.e: You put empty PET bottles in the PET collection point, for example at the shop. They are made into new bottles.
69637.m: PET bottles go in the PET collection.

69638.q: Where are empty food tins collected?
a: At the aluminium and tin collection
69638.e: Tins made of steel or aluminium can be collected separately. The metal is melted down again.
69638.m: Tins go in the metal collection.

69639.q: Where do you take old medicines?
69639.e: Old medicines can harm nature. That is why you return them to the pharmacy or chemist’s.
69639.m: You take old medicines back to the pharmacy.

69640.q: Where can you find the collection days for rubbish and paper?
69640.e: Many municipalities publish a waste calendar. It shows when each type of waste is collected.
69640.m: The waste calendar shows the collection days.

69641.q: Where do you take a broken hairdryer?
69641.e: Electrical appliances contain valuable and poisonous materials. You can return them free of charge to shops that sell such appliances.
69641.m: You take old electrical appliances back to the shop.

69642.q: Where does a flattened cardboard box belong?
69642.e: Cardboard is collected separately and made into new cardboard. Flattened, it takes up less space.
69642.m: Cardboard belongs in the cardboard collection.

69643.q: Who collects the waste paper in many municipalities?
69643.e: In many municipalities school classes or clubs help with the paper collection. In return they often get some money for the class fund.
69643.m: School classes often collect the waste paper.

69644.q: Where do you take old clothes that are still in good condition?
69644.e: You can put old clothes in collection bins or bags. They are worn again or recycled.
69644.m: You give old clothes to the clothes collection.

69645.q: Where do empty paint tins with leftovers belong?
69645.e: Leftover paint can be poisonous. That is why you hand it in at a collection point for hazardous waste.
69645.m: Poisonous leftovers belong in the hazardous waste collection.

69646.q: What is it better to take off at the playground?
69646.e: A bike helmet can get caught on play equipment. That is dangerous, so you play at the playground without a helmet.
69646.m: At the playground you play without a bike helmet.

69649.q: On which piece of play equipment do you slide from top to bottom?
69649.e: On the slide you climb up and slide down. You slide feet first.
69649.m: On the slide you go down feet first.

69650.q: What does a sign at the entrance to a playground often show?
69650.e: At the entrance it often says which rules apply and what age the playground is meant for.
69650.m: A sign at the playground shows the rules.

69651.q: Why shouldn’t you wear jackets with drawstrings on play equipment?
69651.e: Drawstrings and cords can get tangled on equipment. That can be dangerous.
69651.m: Drawstrings can get caught on play equipment.

69652.q: What do you do at the playground if another child is already on the swing?
69652.e: At the playground everyone shares the equipment. If you wait, your turn will come.
69652.m: At the playground you wait until it is your turn.

69653.q: What do some playgrounds have for a picnic with sausages?
69653.e: Many playgrounds in the countryside have a fire pit. There you can grill a sausage with adults.
69653.m: At the fire pit you can grill sausages with adults.

69654.q: Where do you have PE lessons at school?
69654.e: For PE there is a gym with equipment such as parallel bars, a high bar and mats.
69654.m: PE takes place in the gym.

69655.q: Where do the teachers meet during break?
69655.e: The staffroom is a room for the teachers. There they talk things over and take a break.
69655.m: The teachers meet in the staffroom.

69656.q: What makes a sound at school to show that break is starting?
69656.e: In many schools a bell or gong rings. That way everyone knows when break begins and ends.
69656.m: The school bell shows that break is starting.

69657.q: What colour are the signs in a school that show the emergency exit?
69657.e: Emergency exit signs are green with a white running figure. They show the safe way outside.
69657.m: Green signs show the way to the emergency exit.

69658.q: Where do children hang up their jackets at school?
69658.e: In front of the classroom there are hooks in the cloakroom. Jackets and bags hang there.

69659.q: Where do children work with wood and saws at school?
69659.e: The workshop has workbenches and tools. There children make things out of wood and other materials.
69659.m: You work with wood in the workshop.

69660.q: What does a school practise so that everyone gets out quickly in a fire?
69660.e: In a fire drill all classes leave the school calmly and quickly. Outside everyone meets at the assembly point.
69660.m: In a fire drill everyone goes calmly to the assembly point.

69661.q: Where do pupils learn to cook in some schools?
69661.e: Many schools have a school kitchen with cookers and sinks. There older children learn to cook and eat healthily.
69661.m: You learn to cook in the school kitchen.

69662.q: Where can children borrow books in many schools?
69662.e: Many schools have their own school library. There children can borrow books for school and for reading.
69662.m: Many schools have their own school library.

69663.q: What can you do if you want to read a book for longer?
69663.e: At the library you can often renew a loan, at the desk or online. Then you may keep the book longer.
69663.m: You can often renew a loan.

69664.q: Apart from books, what can you also borrow in many libraries?
69664.e: Many libraries have audiobooks, films, magazines and games. That is why they are also called media libraries.
69664.m: At the library there are also audiobooks and games.

69665.q: What do you do if a book you want is currently on loan?
a: You buy it from the library
You take it away from someone
69665.e: You can reserve a book that is on loan. When it comes back, it is put aside for you.
69665.m: You can reserve a book that is on loan.

69666.q: Which books with lots of pictures are made for small children?
69666.e: Picture books tell stories with big pictures and little text. They are ideal for small children.
69666.m: Picture books tell stories in pictures for small children.

69668.q: What can you also borrow online from many libraries today?
69668.e: Many libraries offer e-books. You read them on a tablet or e-reader.

69669.q: How should you treat a borrowed book?
a: Draw on it with felt-tip pens
Leave it out in the rain
69669.e: Many other people will read a library book after you. That is why you handle it carefully.

69670.q: What does the library often scan when you borrow a book?
69670.e: Every book has a barcode stuck on it. When it is scanned, the computer knows who has borrowed which book.
69670.m: The library scans the barcode on the book.

69671.q: What do you practise in a children’s and youth parliament?
69671.e: You learn to present ideas, discuss them and vote. This is how you practise democracy.
69671.m: In a children’s and youth parliament you practise democracy.

69672.q: How does a children’s parliament decide on an idea?
69672.e: In the children’s parliament there is a vote. The idea with the most votes wins.
69672.m: In the children’s parliament the majority decides.

69673.q: Which idea might a youth parliament suggest to the municipality?
69673.e: Youth parliaments stand up for things that matter to young people. A skatepark is a typical example.
69673.m: A youth parliament suggests ideas for young people.

69674.q: What is important when someone else is speaking in the children’s parliament?
69674.e: In a parliament people listen to each other. Only then can good decisions be made.
69674.m: In parliament people listen carefully to each other.

69675.q: What do members of a children’s parliament do when they disagree?
69675.e: Different opinions are normal. You exchange arguments and look for a good solution.
69675.m: In the children’s parliament different opinions are discussed.

69676.q: Where can a town’s children’s parliament often meet?
69676.e: Some children’s parliaments may meet in the town’s real council chamber. That makes them feel like real politicians.
69676.m: Children’s parliaments often meet in the real council chamber.

69677.q: What is a written proposal that a youth parliament submits to the municipality called?
69677.e: With a motion the youth parliament asks the municipality to look into something or do something. Whether anything comes of it is then decided by the authorities.
69677.m: A motion is a proposal to the municipality.

69678.q: What does the coat of arms of the town of Olten show?
69678.e: The coat of arms of Olten shows three green fir trees on a green triple hill. It has been used since 1653 at the latest.
69678.m: The coat of arms of Olten shows three fir trees.

69679.q: In the coat of arms of the town of Frauenfeld, what is the woman leading on a chain?
69679.e: In the Frauenfeld coat of arms a woman holds a red lion on a golden chain. The woman matches the name of the town (Frau means woman).
69679.m: In the coat of arms of Frauenfeld a woman holds a lion.

69680.q: Which bird is in the coat of arms of the town of Aarau?
69680.e: The Aarau coat of arms shows a black eagle on white below a red stripe.
69680.m: The coat of arms of Aarau has a black eagle.

69681.q: What do the letters in the coat of arms of the town of Lugano stand for?
69681.e: The coat of arms of Lugano has the letters LVGA. They are the first letters of the town’s name.
69681.m: The letters in Lugano’s coat of arms stand for the town’s name.

69682.q: What can be seen on the white diagonal band in the coat of arms of the town of Thun?
69682.e: The coat of arms of Thun is red with a white diagonal band. On it is a golden star; in the past it was black.
69682.m: The coat of arms of Thun has a golden star.

69683.q: What can be seen next to the abbot’s staff in the coat of arms of Kreuzlingen?
69683.e: The coat of arms of Kreuzlingen shows a red cross and a white abbot’s staff. The cross matches the name of the town (Kreuz means cross).
69683.m: The coat of arms of Kreuzlingen has a cross.

69684.q: Where do you often see the municipal coat of arms?
a: On the municipality’s flags and letters
69684.e: The municipal coat of arms is the emblem of the municipality. You see it on flags, on the town hall and on letters.
69684.m: The municipal coat of arms is the emblem of the municipality.

69685.q: What do you call a coat of arms whose picture matches the place name?
69685.e: With canting arms, the picture explains the name. For example, a fish may appear in the arms of a place whose name sounds like a fish.
69685.m: Canting arms show a picture that matches the place name.

69686.q: Which flag often hangs on the town hall next to the Swiss flag and the cantonal flag?
69686.e: Many town halls fly three flags: Switzerland, the canton and the municipality. This shows the three levels of Switzerland.
69686.m: The municipality, the canton and the Confederation each have their own flag.

69687.q: How many tens does the number 100 have?
69687.m: A hundred is made up of ten tens.

69688.q: How do you write “forty-seven” as a number?
69688.e: Forty is 4 tens and seven is 7 ones, so together they make 47.
69688.m: Forty-seven is written with a four at the front and a seven at the back.

69690.q: What is the biggest two-digit number?
69690.e: Two-digit numbers have two digits. The biggest is 99, because 100 already has three digits.

69691.q: What is the smallest two-digit number?
69691.e: The numbers from 1 to 9 have only one digit. The first number with two digits is 10.

69693.q: How many numbers do you say when you count from 1 to 100?
69693.e: From 1 to 100 you say each number once, which is exactly 100 numbers.
69693.m: If you count from 1 to 100, you say a hundred numbers.

69694.q: Lea has 4 ten-franc notes and 6 one-franc coins. How many francs does she have?
69694.e: 4 ten-franc notes are 40 francs, plus 6 francs: 40 + 6 = 46.
69694.m: Count ten-franc notes as tens and one-franc coins as ones.

69695.q: How do you write “three hundred and twenty-five” as a number?
69695.e: Three hundred is 3 hundreds, and twenty-five is 2 tens and 5 ones. Together that makes 325.
69695.m: Three hundred and twenty-five is written as 325.

69696.q: How many hundreds are there in 1000?
69696.e: 10 times 100 makes 1000. So 1000 is exactly 10 hundreds.
69696.m: A thousand is made up of ten hundreds.

69697.q: What is the biggest three-digit number?
69697.e: Three-digit numbers have three digits. The biggest is 999, because 1000 already has four digits.

69698.q: What is the smallest three-digit number?
69698.e: The numbers up to 99 have at most two digits. The first number with three digits is 100.

69699.q: You count in hundreds: 200, 300, 400. Which number comes next?
69699.e: When counting in hundreds, you add 100 each time: 400 + 100 = 500.
69699.m: When counting in hundreds, only the hundreds digit changes.

69700.q: How do you say the number 708 in words?
69700.e: 708 has 7 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones. That is why you say seven hundred and eight.
69700.m: You do not hear a zero in the tens place when you say the number.

69701.q: You count backwards in tens: 530, 520, 510. Which number comes next?
69701.e: Counting backwards in tens, you take away 10 each time: 510 − 10 = 500.
69701.m: When counting backwards, the numbers get smaller.

69702.q: Which of these numbers lies between 600 and 700?
69702.e: 650 has 6 hundreds and is bigger than 600 but smaller than 700. The other numbers have 5 or 7 hundreds.
69702.m: All numbers between 600 and 700 have six hundreds.

69703.q: How many tens does the number 58 have?
69703.e: In 58, the 5 is in the tens place and the 8 is in the ones place. So 58 has five tens.
69703.m: The left digit of a two-digit number shows the tens.

69704.q: Which digit is in the hundreds place in 472?
69704.e: In three-digit numbers, the hundreds are on the far left. In 472 that is the 4.
69704.m: In three-digit numbers, the hundreds digit is on the far left.

69705.q: Which number has 3 hundreds, 6 tens and 2 ones?
69705.e: 3 hundreds are 300, 6 tens are 60, plus 2 ones: 300 + 60 + 2 = 362.
69705.m: You write the hundreds first, then the tens and finally the ones.

69706.q: Which number has 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 ones?
69706.e: 5 hundreds are 500, plus 4 ones: 500 + 4 = 504. For the missing tens, you write a 0.
69706.m: If a place is empty, you write a zero there.

69707.q: How many ones are the same as 1 ten?
69707.e: You can bundle 10 ones into one ten. That is why 1 ten equals 10 ones.
69707.m: Ten ones together make one ten.

69708.m: Twelve tens make a hundred and twenty.

69709.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in the number 765?
69709.e: In 765, the 6 is in the tens place. So it means 6 tens, which is 60.
69709.m: The place of a digit decides its value.

69710.q: How many whole hundreds are there in the number 890?
69710.e: In 890, the 8 is in the hundreds place. So there are 8 whole hundreds in 890.
69710.m: The hundreds digit shows how many whole hundreds a number has.

69711.q: Which number is exactly halfway between 0 and 10 on the number line?
69711.e: From 0 to 5 is 5 steps and from 5 to 10 is also 5 steps. That is why 5 is exactly in the middle.
69711.m: The middle is the same distance from both ends.

69712.q: Which number is exactly halfway between 20 and 40 on the number line?
69712.e: From 20 to 30 is 10 steps and from 30 to 40 is also 10. So 30 is in the middle.
69712.m: Between two tens numbers, you find the middle with jumps of equal size.

69713.q: Which number is exactly halfway between 100 and 200 on the number line?
69713.e: From 100 to 150 is 50 steps and from 150 to 200 is also 50. So 150 is in the middle.
69713.m: Half the way from 100 to 200 is a jump of 50.

69714.q: Where are the bigger numbers on a horizontal number line?
69714.e: On the number line, the numbers get bigger and bigger from left to right.
69714.m: The further right a number is, the bigger it is.

69715.q: You are standing on 35 on the number line and jump 10 to the right. Where do you land?
69715.e: A jump to the right means plus: 35 + 10 = 45.
69715.m: Jumping to the right means adding.

69716.q: You are standing on 80 on the number line and jump 3 steps to the left. Where do you land?
69716.e: A jump to the left means minus: 80 − 3 = 77.
69716.m: Jumping to the left means taking away.

69717.q: Which of these numbers is closest to 50 on the number line?
69717.e: 47 is only 3 steps away from 50. 56 is 6 steps, 57 is 7 and 42 is 8 steps away.
69717.m: The number with the shortest distance is the closest.

69718.q: Between which tens numbers does the number 64 lie?
69718.e: 64 has 6 tens. It is bigger than 60 but smaller than 70.
69718.m: The tens digit tells you the ten before.

69719.q: What is the smallest even number that is bigger than 50?
69719.e: 51 is odd, and 50 is not bigger than 50. The next even number after 50 is 52.
69719.m: Even numbers follow each other in steps of two.

69720.q: Which digit tells you whether a number is even?
69720.e: Whether a number is even or odd depends only on the last digit, which is the ones.
69720.m: The ones digit shows whether a number is even.

69721.q: What do you get if you add two even numbers together?
69721.e: Even numbers are made up entirely of pairs. If you add pairs together, they stay pairs, for example 4 + 6 = 10.
69721.m: Even plus even always makes even.

69722.q: What do you get if you add two odd numbers together?
69722.e: With every odd number, one is left over. The two leftover ones together make a pair, for example 3 + 5 = 8.
69722.m: Odd plus odd always makes even.

69723.q: Is the number 0 even or odd?
69723.e: 0 can be divided by 2 with no remainder. That is why 0 belongs to the even numbers.
69723.m: Zero is also an even number.

69724.q: What is the biggest odd number that is smaller than 100?
69724.e: 99 ends in 9 and so is odd. 101 is bigger than 100.

69725.q: Two children want to share 15 sweets fairly with none left over. Why does this not work?
69725.e: Each child would get 7 sweets, which makes 14 altogether. One sweet is left over because 15 is odd.
69725.m: Odd numbers cannot be split into two equal parts with no remainder.

69726.e: Doubling means taking the number twice: 7 + 7 = 14.
69726.m: Doubling means adding a number to itself.

69728.e: Halving means splitting into two equal parts: 9 + 9 = 18, so half is 9.
69728.m: Halving is the opposite of doubling.

69729.e: 150 + 150 = 300. That is why 150 is half of 300.
69729.m: Halving makes two parts of the same size.

69730.e: 45 + 45 = 90. You can work it out like this: 40 + 40 = 80 and 5 + 5 = 10, together 90.
69730.m: You can double the tens and the ones separately.

69731.e: 35 + 35 = 70. You can work it out like this: half of 60 is 30 and half of 10 is 5, together 35.
69731.m: You can split a number into parts and halve each part.

69732.q: Mia has 12 francs. Tim has twice as much. How many francs does Tim have?
69732.m: Twice as much means two times as much.

69733.q: A cake has 8 pieces. Half of them are eaten. How many pieces are left?
69733.e: Half of 8 is 4. When 4 pieces have been eaten, 4 pieces are left.
69733.m: If you take away half, the other half is left.

69734.e: 250 + 250 = 500. Two two hundred and fifties make five hundred.
69734.m: Double two hundred and fifty is five hundred.

69735.e: You can first go up to 10: 8 + 2 = 10, then 5 more makes 15.
69735.m: When crossing ten, first go up to the full ten.

69736.e: You first go back to 10: 13 − 3 = 10, then take away 3 more to make 7.
69736.m: When taking away, you can first go back to the full ten.

69737.m: Split the number so that you reach the next ten first.

69738.e: 72 − 2 = 70, then take away 3 more to make 67.
69738.m: When taking away across a ten, it helps to stop at the full ten.

69739.e: First the tens: 35 + 20 = 55. Then the ones: 55 + 7 = 62.
69739.m: You can add the tens first and then the ones.

69740.m: You can take away the tens first and then the ones.

69741.m: You can add the hundreds and the tens separately.

69742.m: Big numbers are best taken away in steps.

69743.q: An ice cream costs 3 francs 40 centimes. You pay with 5 francs. How much change do you get?
69743.e: From 3.40 to 4 francs, 60 centimes are missing, and from 4 to 5 francs another 1 franc. Together that is 1 franc 60 centimes.
69743.m: You can work out change by counting up to the amount you paid.

69745.e: 6 times 7 = 42. You can work it out like this: 5 times 7 = 35, and 7 more makes 42.
69745.m: You can work out a hard times sum from an easy one.

69746.e: 10 times 9 = 90. Take away two lots of 9 from that: 90 − 18 = 72.
69746.m: Multiplying by ten helps with harder times table sums.

69747.e: 7 times 8 = 56. A memory aid is the sequence 5, 6, 7, 8: 56 = 7 times 8.

69748.e: 9 times 9 = 81. You can work it out like this: 10 times 9 = 90, minus 9 makes 81.

69749.e: 6 times 6 = 36. You can work it out like this: 5 times 6 = 30, and 6 more makes 36.

69750.q: Which of these numbers is not an answer in the five times table?
69750.e: The answers in the five times table always end in 5 or 0. 32 ends in 2 and does not belong.
69750.m: All numbers in the five times table end in 5 or 0.

69751.q: A bike has 2 wheels. How many wheels do 8 bikes have altogether?
69751.m: You count equal groups using the times tables.

69752.q: A week has 7 days. How many days are there in 4 weeks?

69753.e: 3 times 5 = 15 fits into 17. From 15 to 17 there are 2 more, and that is the remainder.
69753.m: The remainder is what is left over when dividing.

69754.m: Look for the biggest times sum that still fits.

69755.m: The times tables help when dividing with a remainder.

69756.m: You can check any division with a remainder.

69757.m: To check, work out four times eight plus six and you get thirty-eight.

69758.q: 19 apples are shared equally between 3 children. How many apples are left over?
69758.e: Each child gets 6 apples, because 6 times 3 = 18. Of 19 apples, 1 is left over.
69758.m: What is left over when sharing fairly is called the remainder.

69759.q: 26 children make groups of 4. How many full groups are there?
69759.e: 6 times 4 = 24 children are in full groups. 2 children are left over and are not a full group.
69759.m: Count full groups without the remainder.

69760.q: Which remainder is not possible when dividing by 5?
69760.e: If the remainder were 5, you could take away another 5. That is why the remainder when dividing by 5 is at most 4.
69760.m: The remainder must be smaller than the number you divide by.

69761.e: 5 times 9 = 45. 9 fits exactly five times into 45, and nothing is left over.
69761.m: If a division works out exactly, the remainder is zero.

69762.e: The number before is the one directly in front of it. Before 40 comes 39.
69762.m: The number before is one smaller.

69763.e: The number after is the one directly following it. After 59 comes 60.
69763.m: The number after is one bigger.

69764.q: Which numbers are the neighbours of 100?
69764.e: The neighbouring numbers are the number before and the number after: 99 and 101.
69764.m: Every number has one neighbour before it and one after it.

69765.m: After a number ending in two nines, a new hundred always starts.

69766.m: Before a full hundred comes a number ending in two nines.

69767.q: Which number is exactly between 26 and 28?
69767.e: 26 and 28 are the neighbouring numbers of 27. That is why 27 is in between.
69767.m: A number always lies between its two neighbours.

69768.q: Which number has the neighbours 549 and 551?
69768.e: The number between 549 and 551 is 550. The number before it is 549 and the number after it is 551.
69768.m: Neighbouring numbers always differ from their number by one.

69769.e: 45 has 4 tens, 54 has 5 tens. 45 is smaller than 54, so you write 45 < 54.
69769.m: With two-digit numbers, the tens decide first.

69770.q: Which of these numbers is the biggest?
69770.e: They all have three digits. 710 and 701 have 7 hundreds, but 710 has more tens. That is why 710 is the biggest.
69770.m: First compare the hundreds, then the tens and then the ones.

69771.e: 8 + 5 makes 13. Both sides are the same size, so the equals sign goes there.
69771.m: If both sides are the same size, you write the equals sign.

69772.e: With “>”, the open side is on the left. The number on the left is bigger, for example 9 > 4.
69772.m: The open side of the sign faces the bigger number.

69773.e: 20 + 30 makes 50, and 50 is bigger than 45. The other statements are false.
69773.m: Work it out first and then compare.

69774.q: Which sign goes between 2 times 6 and 3 times 4?
69774.e: 2 times 6 = 12 and 3 times 4 = 12. Both sides make 12, so the equals sign goes in between.
69774.m: Different sums can have the same answer.

69775.q: Which list is in order from the smallest to the biggest number?
69775.e: 19 is the smallest, then comes 91. The three-digit numbers 109 and 190 are bigger, and 109 is smaller than 190.
69775.m: Two-digit numbers are always smaller than three-digit numbers.

69776.e: 3 tens and 4 tens are 7 tens. 7 tens are 70.
69776.m: Work with tens numbers like ones, just with tens.

69777.e: 9 tens minus 6 tens are 3 tens, so 30.
69777.m: Nine minus six helps you work out ninety minus sixty.

69778.e: 8 tens and 6 tens are 14 tens, so 140.
69778.m: Fourteen tens make a hundred and forty.

69779.m: You can take away too much first and then add some back.

69780.m: With tens numbers, you multiply as in the times tables and add a zero.

69781.e: 6 tens divided by 3 are 2 tens, so 20.
69781.m: Sixty divided by three makes twenty.

69783.e: 10 fits eight times into 80, because 8 times 10 = 80.
69783.m: When you divide a tens number by ten, the zero disappears.

69784.q: How many tens do you need to add to 40 to get 100?
69784.e: From 40 to 100, 60 is missing. That is 6 tens.
69784.m: When making up to a hundred, count the missing tens.

69785.q: How many sides does a circle have?
69785.e: A circle has just one round line. It has no straight sides and no corners.
69785.m: A circle is completely round and has no straight sides.

69786.q: Which object has the shape of a circle?
69786.e: A coin like the 5-franc coin is round. From above it looks like a circle.
69786.m: Coins have the shape of a circle.

69787.q: What can you use to draw a nice circle?
69787.e: A pair of compasses turns around a fixed point. This makes a round line, a circle.
69787.m: You draw circles with a pair of compasses.

69788.q: Which road sign has the shape of a triangle?
69788.e: The “Give way” sign is a triangle standing on its point. The stop sign is an octagon.
69788.m: The “Give way” sign is a triangle.

69789.q: You put two identical triangles together along their long side. Which shape can this make?
69789.e: If you put two identical triangles side by side, you get a four-sided shape, for example a square or a rectangle.
69789.m: Two identical triangles together make a four-sided shape.

69790.q: How many corners does a quadrilateral have?
69790.e: A quadrilateral has four corners and four sides. Squares and rectangles are quadrilaterals.

69791.q: Which of these shapes is NOT a quadrilateral?
69791.e: The square, rectangle and rhombus have four corners. The triangle has only three corners.
69791.m: A triangle is not a quadrilateral.

69792.q: How many corners does a pentagon have?
69792.e: A pentagon has five corners and five sides.

69793.q: What is special about a square?
a: All its sides are the same length
Two of its sides are round
69793.e: In a square, all four sides are the same length. All the corners are right angles.
69793.m: In a square, all four sides are the same length.

69794.q: What is true of a rectangle that is not a square?
a: Two sides are longer than the others
All sides are the same length
69794.e: A rectangle has two long and two short sides. The opposite sides are the same length.
69794.m: In a rectangle, opposite sides are the same length.

69795.q: Which object usually has the shape of a rectangle?
69795.e: A door is taller than it is wide and has four square corners. That is a rectangle.
69795.m: A door has the shape of a rectangle.

69796.q: Which object usually has the shape of a square?
69796.e: A chessboard has 64 squares. Each one has four sides of equal length and four square corners.
69796.m: The squares on a chessboard are squares.

69797.q: A rectangle is 5 cm long and 2 cm wide. How long are all its sides together?
69797.e: You work out 5 + 2 + 5 + 2 = 14. All four sides together are 14 cm long.
69797.m: For the perimeter, you add up all the sides.

69798.q: A square has sides of 2 cm. How long are all four sides together?
69798.e: You work out 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. All the sides together are 8 cm long.
69798.m: For a square, you multiply one side by four.

69799.q: Is every square also a rectangle?
69799.e: A rectangle has four right angles. A square also has four right angles, and its sides are the same length too.
69799.m: Every square is also a rectangle.

69800.q: A rectangle is 3 cm long and 2 cm wide. How many squares with 1 cm sides fit into it?
69800.e: 3 squares fit in a row, and there are 2 rows. 3 times 2 is 6.
69800.m: You can cover a rectangle with small squares.

69801.q: How many small squares with 1 cm sides fit into a square with 2 cm sides?
69801.e: 2 small squares fit in each row, and there are 2 rows. 2 times 2 is 4.
69801.m: You can divide a square into smaller squares.

69802.q: Which solid can roll in every direction?
69802.e: A sphere is round all over. That is why it rolls in every direction.
69802.m: A sphere rolls in every direction.

69803.q: Which of these solids cannot roll?
69803.e: A cube has only flat faces and edges. That is why it does not roll but only tips over. The sphere, cylinder and cone have round surfaces and can roll.
69803.m: A cube has only flat faces and does not roll.

69804.q: What shape is a tin can?
69804.e: A tin is round at the top and bottom and curved at the side. This shape is called a cylinder.
69804.m: A tin has the shape of a cylinder.

69805.e: A shoebox has only rectangular faces and straight edges. This shape is called a cuboid.

69806.q: Which object has the shape of a sphere?
69806.e: A football is round all over. It has the shape of a sphere.
69806.m: A football has the shape of a sphere.

69807.q: Which solid can roll and also stand flat?
69807.e: A cylinder has flat round faces to stand on. It can roll on its curved side.
69807.m: A cylinder can roll and stand.

69808.q: Which solid has six square faces of the same size?
69808.e: In a cube, all six faces are squares of the same size.
69808.m: A cube has six identical squares as faces.

69809.q: What makes a cuboid different from a cube?
69809.e: In a cube, all the faces are squares. In a cuboid, the faces can also be rectangles.
69809.m: A cuboid can have rectangular faces.

69810.q: Roughly what shape is an ice cream cone?
69810.e: An ice cream cone is round at the top and pointed at the bottom. This shape is called a cone.
69810.m: An ice cream cone has the shape of a cone.

69811.q: How many corners does a sphere have?
69811.e: A sphere is completely round. It has no corners and no edges.

69812.q: How many corners does a cube have?
69812.e: A cube has four corners at the top and four corners at the bottom. 4 + 4 = 8.

69813.q: How many edges does a cube have?
69813.e: There are 4 edges at the top, 4 edges at the bottom and 4 edges at the sides. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

69814.q: How many faces does a cuboid have?
69814.e: A cuboid has one face each at the top, bottom, front, back, left and right. That is 6 faces.

69815.q: How many corners does a pyramid with a square base have?
69815.e: It has 4 corners at the bottom, plus the tip at the top. 4 + 1 = 5.
69815.m: A pyramid with a square base has five corners.

69816.q: What is an edge on a cube?
a: The line where two faces meet
69816.e: Where two faces meet, a straight line is formed. This line is called an edge.
69816.m: An edge is where two faces meet.

69817.q: What is a corner on a cube?
69817.e: On a cube, three edges meet at each corner. The corner is pointed.

69818.q: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
69818.e: A cylinder has one flat, round face at the top and one at the bottom. In between there is a curved surface.
69818.m: A cylinder has two flat, round faces.

69819.q: How many points does a cone have?
69819.e: A cone has a round face at the bottom and exactly one point at the top.

69820.q: A pyramid has a square at the bottom. How many triangles does it have at the sides?
69820.e: There is a triangle on each side of the square. The square has 4 sides, so there are 4 triangles.
69820.m: A pyramid with a square base has four triangles.

69821.q: What is a line of symmetry?
a: A line that divides a shape into two equal halves
A round line around a shape
69821.e: The line of symmetry divides a shape so that one half is the mirror image of the other.
69821.m: The line of symmetry divides a shape into two equal halves.

69822.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
69822.e: A rectangle has one vertical and one horizontal line of symmetry. The lines through the corners are not lines of symmetry.
69822.m: A rectangle has two lines of symmetry.

69823.q: Which capital letter is symmetrical if you divide it vertically down the middle?
69823.e: With A, the left and right halves are the same. That is not the case with F, R and G.

69824.q: On which animal do the two wings look like mirror images?
69824.e: The two wings of a butterfly look the same, like mirror images.

69825.q: You hold your right hand up to a mirror. Which hand does your reflection seem to be holding up?
69825.e: A mirror swaps left and right. That is why your right hand looks like a left hand in the mirror.
69825.m: In a mirror, left and right are swapped.

69826.q: Can you fold the square Swiss flag so that both halves fit exactly on top of each other?
69826.e: The white cross is exactly in the middle of the red square. If you fold the flag in the middle, both halves fit on top of each other.

69827.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
69827.e: Every straight line through the centre divides the circle into two equal halves. There are infinitely many of these.
69827.m: A circle has infinitely many lines of symmetry.

69828.q: Which digit is symmetrical if you divide it horizontally across the middle?
69828.e: With 3, the top half is the same as the bottom half. That is not the case with 4, 7 and 2.
69828.m: The digit 3 has a horizontal line of symmetry.

69829.q: What comes next in the pattern: red, blue, red, blue, red, ...?
69829.e: Red and blue always take turns. After red comes blue.
69829.m: In a pattern, the same thing always repeats.

69830.q: What comes next in the pattern: circle, triangle, triangle, circle, triangle, triangle, ...?
69830.e: The pattern is always circle, triangle, triangle. Then it starts again with a circle.
69830.m: Look for the part that repeats.

69831.q: What comes next in the sequence: 2, 4, 6, 8, ...?
69831.e: Each number is 2 bigger than the one before. 8 + 2 = 10.
69831.m: In this sequence, you always add 2.

69832.q: Which shape is missing: square, circle, square, ..., square, circle?
69832.e: Square and circle take turns. After a square there is always a circle.
69832.m: You can find missing parts in a pattern.

69834.q: What comes next in the pattern: A, B, B, A, B, B, A, ...?
69834.e: The pattern is A, B, B. So after the A comes a B again.
69834.m: A pattern always repeats in the same way.

69836.q: A pattern goes: star, heart, moon, star, heart, moon. Which picture is 7th?
69836.e: The pattern has 3 parts. After 6 pictures it starts again, so the 7th picture is a star again.
69836.m: After each complete pattern, it starts from the beginning.

69837.q: You are facing forwards and turn to the right and then to the right again. Which way are you facing now?
69837.e: Two quarter turns to the right make a half turn. That is why you are now facing backwards.
69837.m: Two right turns make a half turn.

69838.q: In Switzerland, which side of the road do cars drive on?
69838.e: In Switzerland, traffic drives on the right. Cars and bikes drive on the right-hand side.
69838.m: In Switzerland, you drive on the right.

69839.q: Which hand do most people write with?
69839.e: Most people are right-handed. About one person in ten writes with their left hand.
69839.m: Most people write with their right hand.

69840.q: In Switzerland, which way do you look first before crossing a road?
69840.e: On the near side of the road, the cars come from the left. That is why you look left, right and left again.
69840.m: Before crossing, look left, right, left.

69841.q: A child is standing opposite you and raises their right hand. On which side do you see this hand?
69841.e: Someone standing opposite you is facing the other way. So their right hand is on your left.
69841.m: When someone faces you, left and right are swapped.

69842.q: In which direction do you read a line of text in German?
69842.e: In German you start on the left and read to the right.
69842.m: German is read from left to right.

69843.q: You walk north and turn left. Which direction are you walking in now?
69843.e: When you face north, west is on your left. After turning left, you walk west.
69843.m: When you walk north, west is on your left-hand side.

69844.q: Where in the chest is the heart in most people?
a: A little more to the left
A little more to the right
69844.e: The heart is in the middle of the chest, but a little more to the left.
69844.m: The heart is a little more on the left side.

69845.q: A lamp hangs above the table. Where is the table?
69845.e: If the lamp is above the table, then the table is under the lamp.
69845.m: If A is above B, then B is under A.

69846.q: Anna is standing in front of Ben. Where is Ben standing?
69846.e: If Anna is in front, Ben is standing behind her.
69846.m: If A is in front of B, then B is behind A.

69847.q: Three children are standing in a row: Lea, Tim, Mia. Who is in the middle?
69847.e: Tim is standing between Lea and Mia. He is in the middle.
69847.m: Whoever stands between two others is in the middle.

69848.q: The cat is lying right inside, and the basket is all around it. Which word fits: The cat is lying ... the basket.
69848.e: When something is inside, you say “in”. The cat is lying in the basket.

69849.q: On the shelf, the red book is above the blue one and the blue one is above the green one. Which book is at the very bottom?
69849.e: Red is at the top, then comes blue and green is at the very bottom.
69849.m: You put the things in order from top to bottom.

69850.q: 5 children are standing in a queue. Max is third from the front. How many children are behind him?
69850.e: There are 2 children in front of Max. 5 minus 3 = 2, so there are 2 children behind him.
69850.m: You can count to work out places in a row.

69851.q: The ball is lying between the house and the tree. What is true?
a: The ball is in the middle
The ball is in the house
The ball is in the tree
The ball is behind the house
69851.e: “Between” means there is something on both sides. The ball is in the middle.
69851.m: “Between” means in the middle of two things.

69852.q: A tower is made of 4 cubes on top of each other. You put 2 more cubes on top. How many cubes does the tower have now?
69852.e: You work out 4 + 2 = 6. The tower now has 6 cubes.
69852.m: You add up all the cubes in the tower.

69853.q: A wall has 2 rows with 3 cubes each. How many cubes is that?
69853.e: 2 rows times 3 cubes are 6 cubes. Or: 3 + 3 = 6.

69854.q: How many small cubes do you need for a big cube that is 2 cubes long, 2 wide and 2 high?
69854.e: At the bottom there are 2 times 2 = 4 cubes. On top there are another 4. 4 + 4 = 8.
69854.m: A cube made of two layers of four cubes needs eight small cubes.

69855.q: You build a staircase with 3 steps: 1 cube, then 2 cubes high, then 3 cubes high. How many cubes do you need?
69855.m: For a staircase, you add up the cubes of each step.

69856.q: A tower has 7 cubes. You take 3 cubes away. How many are left?
69856.m: When you take cubes away, the building gets smaller.

69857.q: You build 3 towers with 4 cubes each. How many cubes do you need?
69857.m: You can multiply towers of the same height.

69858.q: You look at a cube building from above. What can you not see well from above?
69858.e: From above you see the base. You cannot see from above how many cubes are stacked on top of each other.
69858.m: You see the height best from the side.

69859.q: A building plan seen from above shows a number on each square. What does the number mean?
a: How many cubes are stacked there
What colour the cubes are there
How many cubes the whole building has
69859.e: In a building plan from above, you write in each square how tall the tower is there, so how many cubes are stacked on top of each other.
69859.m: In the building plan, the number shows the height of the tower.

69860.q: You fold a square sheet once exactly from corner to corner. What shape do you get?
69860.e: If you fold a square along the diagonal, two triangles lie on top of each other. You see a triangle.
69860.m: A square folded diagonally makes a triangle.

69861.q: You fold a square sheet once exactly in the middle, edge to edge. What shape do you get?
69861.e: If you fold a square edge to edge, it is only half as wide. You get a rectangle.
69861.m: A square cut in half makes a rectangle.

69862.q: You fold a sheet once and cut a small hole in it, not on the fold line. How many holes does the sheet have when you open it?
69862.e: The sheet is doubled. So you cut through two layers and get 2 holes.
69862.m: A folded sheet has two layers.

69863.q: What is the Japanese art of folding figures out of paper called?
69863.e: Origami comes from Japan. For example, you fold cranes or little boats out of a sheet of paper.
69863.m: Origami is the art of paper folding.

69864.q: You fold a sheet in the middle twice. Into how many equal parts is it divided now?
69864.e: The first fold makes 2 parts, the second fold divides each part again. 2 times 2 = 4.

69865.q: What do you get if you put wet paint on one half of a sheet and fold the sheet together?
69865.e: The paint prints onto the other half. Both sides look the same, as if mirrored.

69866.q: What else is the fold line on a folded sheet?
69866.e: Both halves lie exactly on top of each other at the fold line. So it is a line of symmetry.
69866.m: The fold line is a line of symmetry.

69867.q: How many pieces does a tangram have?
69867.e: A tangram has seven pieces. You can make lots of figures with them.

69868.q: Which country does the tangram come from?
69868.e: The tangram is an old puzzle game from China.

69869.q: How many triangles are there in a tangram?
69869.e: The tangram has large, medium and small triangles. Altogether there are 5 triangles.
69869.m: There are five triangles in a tangram.

69870.q: How many squares are there in a tangram?
69870.e: Among the seven pieces there is exactly one square.
69870.m: There is one square in a tangram.

69871.q: Which rule applies when making tangram figures?
a: Pieces may lie on top of each other
69871.e: For a tangram figure you need all the pieces. They must not overlap.
69871.m: With a tangram you always use all the pieces.

69872.q: What shape is a whole tangram when all the pieces are in the box?
69872.e: The seven pieces of the tangram can be put together to make a big square.
69872.m: All the tangram pieces together make a square.

69873.q: What do you do with the pieces of a tangram?
a: You thread them on a string
69873.e: With the tangram you make flat figures such as animals, people or houses. The pieces lie next to each other.
69873.m: You make figures with the tangram.

69874.q: How many large triangles does a tangram have?
69874.e: The two large triangles are the biggest pieces in the tangram.
69874.m: A tangram has two large triangles.

69875.q: What is the best thing to draw a straight line with?
69875.e: A ruler has a straight edge. You draw straight lines along it.
69875.m: You draw straight lines with a ruler.

69876.q: Which letter is made only of straight lines?
69876.e: E has only straight strokes. S, O and C are curved.
69876.m: The letter E has only straight lines.

69877.q: Which letter is made of just one curved line?
69877.e: C is curved all the way round. T, L and H have straight strokes.

69878.q: Which digit has straight and curved lines?
69878.e: The 2 is curved at the top and straight at the bottom. The 1 and the 7 are straight, the 0 is completely curved.
69878.m: The digit 2 has straight and curved parts.

69879.q: Which shape has one straight line and one curved line?
69879.e: The semicircle has a straight line at the bottom and an arc at the top. The circle is only curved, the square and triangle only straight.
69879.m: A semicircle has one straight and one curved line.

69880.q: What is the smallest number of straight lines you need for a triangle?
69880.e: You cannot close a shape with two straight lines. Only with three lines do you get a triangle.
69880.m: For a closed shape you need at least three straight lines.

a: A line that curves up and down
69881.e: A wavy line looks like waves in water. It keeps curving.
69881.m: A wavy line curves up and down.

69882.q: What is a line called that goes up and down with corners?
69882.e: A zigzag line is made of straight pieces with sharp corners.
69882.m: A zigzag line has straight pieces and corners.

69883.e: With a closed line you come back to the start, like with a circle.
69883.m: A closed line has no loose end.

69884.q: The big hand is on the 9, the small hand just before the 6. What time is it?
69884.e: The big hand on the 9 means 45 minutes after the full hour. It is 5:45, so quarter to 6.
69884.m: When the big hand is on the 9, it is quarter to.

69885.q: Which hand of the clock shows the hours?
69885.e: The small hand moves slowly and shows the hours. The big hand shows the minutes.
69885.m: The small hand shows the hours and the big hand the minutes.

69886.q: The big hand is on the 6, the small hand between 4 and 5. What time is it?
69886.e: When the big hand is on the 6, half an hour has passed. It is 4:30, so half past 4.
69886.m: Half past 4 means 30 minutes after 4 o'clock.

69887.q: How many numbers are there on a normal clock face?
69887.e: The clock face shows the numbers 1 to 12. The small hand goes all the way round twice in one day.
69887.m: A clock face shows the numbers 1 to 12.

69888.q: What time is it when the big hand is on the 3 and the small hand just after the 8?
69888.e: The big hand on the 3 means 15 minutes after the full hour. So it is 8:15.
69888.m: Quarter past means 15 minutes after the full hour.

69889.q: How do you write “quarter to 10 in the morning” in digital time?
69889.e: Quarter to 10 means 15 minutes before 10 o'clock. 60 minus 15 = 45, so 9:45.
69889.m: Quarter to means 15 minutes before the full hour.

69890.q: What is another way of saying the time 15:00?
69890.e: After 12 o'clock you keep counting: 13, 14, 15. 15 minus 12 = 3, so 3 o'clock in the afternoon.
69890.m: In the afternoon you simply keep counting the hours after 12.

69891.q: What time is midnight on a digital display?
69891.e: At midnight a new day begins. The digital clock then shows 00:00.
69891.m: At midnight the new day starts with 00:00.

69892.q: What does the digital clock show when it is “half past 7 in the evening”?
69892.e: Half past 7 means 7:30. In the evening you work out 7 + 12 = 19, so 19:30.
69892.m: Half past 7 in the evening is 19:30 on a digital clock.

69893.q: How many minutes are there in an hour?
69893.e: An hour is made of 60 minutes. The big hand takes one whole turn for it.

69895.q: How many hours are half a day?
69895.e: A whole day has 24 hours. Half of that is 24 : 2 = 12 hours.

69896.q: Which lasts longer: a minute or a second?
69896.e: A second is very short, about one clap. A minute is made of many seconds.
69896.m: A minute lasts much longer than a second.

69898.q: How many minutes are three quarters of an hour?
69898.e: A quarter of an hour has 15 minutes. 3 · 15 = 45 minutes.
69898.m: Three quarters of an hour last 45 minutes.

69899.q: Which lasts longer: 90 minutes or 1 hour?
69899.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. So 90 minutes is 30 minutes longer.
69899.m: An hour is shorter than 90 minutes.

69900.e: The order is Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. So Friday comes before Saturday.

69901.e: The months go like this: May, June, July, August. So July comes after June.

69902.e: The order is Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. So Thursday comes after Wednesday.

69903.q: Which month is the first month of the year?
69903.e: The year begins on 1 January. That is why January is the first month.
69903.m: The year begins with the month of January.

69904.q: Which month is usually the shortest?
69904.e: February has 28 days, or 29 days in a leap year. All the other months have 30 or 31 days.
69904.m: February is the shortest month of the year.

69905.q: How many days does a year have if it is not a leap year?
69905.e: A normal year has 365 days. A leap year has one day more, so 366.

69906.q: How many days does the month of December have?
69906.e: December has 31 days. 31 December is New Year's Eve.

69908.q: How many rappen is a franc worth?
69908.e: 1 franc has 100 rappen. Rappen is shortened to Rp.

69909.q: Which of these coins exists in Switzerland?
69909.e: In Switzerland there are coins of 5, 10, 20 and 50 rappen and of 1, 2 and 5 francs.
69909.m: The biggest Swiss coin is the 5-franc coin.

69910.q: Which of these banknotes exists in Switzerland?
69910.e: Swiss banknotes come in 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 and 1000 francs. 5 francs only exists as a coin.
69910.m: In Switzerland, banknotes only come in certain values.

69911.q: How do you write 3 francs and 50 rappen in short?
69911.e: The francs come before the point, the rappen after the point. So 3 francs and 50 rappen are Fr. 3.50.
69911.m: The francs come before the point and the rappen after it.

69912.q: What is the smallest coin in Switzerland?
69912.e: The 1-rappen coin has not been used since 2007. That is why the 5-rappen coin is the smallest coin.
69912.m: Today the smallest Swiss coin is the 5-rappen coin.

69913.m: One franc has 100 rappen, two francs have 200 rappen.

69914.q: An ice cream costs Fr. 2.80, a water Fr. 1.20. How much do both cost together?
69914.e: 2 francs + 1 franc = 3 francs. 80 rappen + 20 rappen = 100 rappen, so 1 franc. Together that is Fr. 4.00.
69914.m: A hundred rappen together make one whole franc.

69915.q: You pay Fr. 5.00 for an apple that costs Fr. 1.00. How much change do you get?
69915.e: You work out 5 minus 1 = 4. You get Fr. 4.00 back.
69915.m: The change is the amount paid minus the price.

69916.q: How many 10-rappen coins are worth the same as one franc?
69916.m: Ten 10-rappen coins together are worth one franc.

69917.q: How many 2-franc coins do you get for a 10-franc note?
69917.m: Five 2-franc coins together are worth 10 francs.

69918.q: How many 20-franc notes are worth the same as one 100-franc note?

69919.q: How many 50-rappen coins are worth the same as 2 francs?
69919.m: Two 50-rappen coins together make one franc.

69920.q: An exercise book costs Fr. 3.40. You pay with Fr. 5.00. How much change do you get?
69920.e: You work out 5.00 minus 3.40 = 1.60. You get Fr. 1.60 back.
69920.m: For the change, you take the price away from the money paid.

69921.q: Which coins together make exactly 1 franc?
69921.m: A hundred rappen together make exactly one franc.

69922.q: How many 5-rappen coins are worth the same as 50 rappen?
69922.m: Ten 5-rappen coins together are worth 50 rappen.

69923.q: A loaf of bread costs Fr. 4.50. You pay with a 10-franc note. How much change do you get?
69923.e: You work out 10.00 minus 4.50 = 5.50. You get Fr. 5.50 back.
69923.m: To check, you count up from the price to the amount paid.

69924.q: How many centimetres are 1 metre and 20 centimetres?
69924.m: To add metres and centimetres, you change everything into centimetres.

69925.q: What is the abbreviation for centimetre?
69925.e: Centimetre is shortened to cm. Metre is shortened to m.
69925.m: Centimetre is written cm for short.

69926.q: What is best measured in metres?
a: The thickness of an exercise book
69926.e: A classroom is several metres long. Small things are better measured in centimetres or millimetres.
69926.m: Large lengths are measured in metres.

69927.q: How many centimetres are half a metre?
69927.e: 1 metre has 100 centimetres. Half of that is 50 centimetres.
69927.m: Half a metre is 50 centimetres long.

69929.q: Which is longer: 1 metre or 80 centimetres?
69929.e: 1 metre is 100 centimetres. 100 centimetres is more than 80 centimetres.
69929.m: It is best to compare lengths in the same unit.

69930.m: A hundred centimetres together make one metre.

69931.q: How many grams are a quarter of a kilogram?
69931.m: A quarter of a kilogram weighs 250 grams.

69932.q: What is the abbreviation for kilogram?
69932.e: Kilogram is shortened to kg. Gram is shortened to g.
69932.m: Kilogram is written kg for short.

69933.e: A bag of flour usually weighs 1 kilogram. A feather is much lighter, a bike much heavier.
69933.m: A bag of flour often weighs exactly one kilogram.

69934.m: A thousand grams together make one kilogram.

69935.q: How many grams are half a kilogram?
69935.e: 1 kilogram has 1000 grams. Half of that is 500 grams.

69936.q: What is best measured in grams?
69936.e: A bar of chocolate is light and weighs about 100 grams. Heavy things are measured in kilograms.
69936.m: Light things are weighed in grams.

69938.q: One bag weighs 2 kg, another 3 kg. How heavy are both together?
69938.e: You work out 2 + 3 = 5. Both bags together weigh 5 kilograms.
69938.m: Weights in the same unit can simply be added up.

69939.q: How many decilitres are there in a litre?

69940.q: What is the abbreviation for decilitre?
69940.e: Decilitre is shortened to dl. Litre is shortened to l.
69940.m: Decilitre is written dl for short.

69941.q: What do you measure in litres?
a: How much water fits into a bucket
69941.e: With litres you measure how much liquid fits into a container. This is called capacity.

69942.q: About how much fits into a normal drinking glass?
69942.e: A normal glass holds about 2 decilitres. 2 litres would be a big bottle.
69942.m: About 2 decilitres fit into a drinking glass.

69943.q: How many decilitres are half a litre?
69943.e: 1 litre has 10 decilitres. Half of that is 5 decilitres.

69945.q: How many millilitres are there in a litre?
69945.e: Milli means thousandth. That is why a litre has 1000 millilitres.

69946.q: What usually holds more than 10 litres?
69946.e: Far more than 100 litres of water fit into a bath. A cup, an egg cup and a spoon hold much less than 1 litre.
69946.m: Large containers such as a bath hold a great many litres.

69947.q: Where do you put the ruler when measuring?
69947.e: You put the zero at the start of the object. Otherwise the length you read off is wrong.
69947.m: When measuring, you always start at zero.

69948.q: A line starts at 0 and ends at 7 on the ruler. How long is it?
69948.m: If you start at zero, you read the length at the end.

69949.q: What do the big numbers on a school ruler mean?
69949.e: The numbers on the school ruler show the centimetres. The small marks in between are millimetres.
69949.m: The numbers on the ruler show centimetres.

69950.q: A pen lies along the ruler from 2 to 10. How long is it?
69950.e: You work out 10 minus 2 = 8. The pen is 8 centimetres long.
69950.m: If you don't start at zero, you take the start away from the end.

69951.q: What is best measured with a ruler?
a: The length of an exercise book
The length of the sports hall
69951.e: An exercise book is short enough for the ruler. For the sports hall you need a tape measure.
69951.m: Short lengths are measured with a ruler.

69952.q: What is best for measuring the length of a garden?
69952.e: A tape measure is many metres long. A school ruler is far too short for this.
69952.m: Long distances are measured with a tape measure.

69953.q: A line ends on the ruler at 4 cm and 5 mm. How long is it if it starts at 0?
69953.m: A centimetre is made of ten small millimetre marks.

69954.q: What must you pay attention to when measuring with a ruler?
a: Holding the ruler at a slant
