70377.e: The rule of three has three steps: the starting statement, working back to one unit and working forward to the amount you want. In the middle step you find the value for one unit.
70377.m: The rule of three goes via one unit to the value you want.

70378.q: 250 g of cheese cost 6 francs. How much does 1 kg of this cheese cost?
70378.e: 1 kg is 1000 g, so four times 250 g. The price is therefore 4 · 6 = 24 francs.
70378.m: One kilogram is four times 250 grams.

70379.q: At an assumed exchange rate, 100 euros cost 94 francs. How many francs do 250 euros cost?
70379.e: 1 euro costs 0.94 francs. 250 euros cost 250 · 0.94 = 235 francs.
70379.m: When changing money, you use the rate like a price per unit.

70380.q: What does the graph of a direct proportion look like?
a: A straight line through the origin
A straight line that does not go through the origin
70380.e: In a direct proportion, x = 0 goes with y = 0, and y grows steadily with x. That is why all the points lie on a straight line through the origin.
70380.m: Direct proportions give a straight line through the origin.

70381.q: Each of x = 1, 2, 3 has a y-value. Which y-values fit a direct proportion?
70381.e: With 4, 8, 12, y is always four times x. In the other rows, y divided by x is not always the same.
70381.m: With directly proportional values, y is always the same multiple of x.

70382.q: In a direct proportion, what is the same for all pairs of values?
a: The quotient y divided by x
70382.e: In direct proportions, y divided by x is always the same. This number is called the constant of proportionality.
70382.m: The constant of proportionality is the same for all pairs of values.

70383.q: In a table of direct proportion, x = 4 goes with y = 10. Which value goes with x = 10?
70383.e: The factor is 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. So x = 10 goes with 10 · 2.5 = 25.
70383.m: With the factor of a table, you can fill in all the missing values.

a: Amount of minced meat and price at a fixed price per kilo
Age and height of a child
Time of day and outside temperature
Number of painters and length of the job
70384.e: At a fixed price per kilo, twice the amount costs twice as much. Age and height or time and temperature do not grow steadily together.
70384.m: A relationship is only proportional if double always gives double.

70385.q: In a direct proportion, x is tripled. What happens to y?
70385.e: With proportionality, x and y change in the same ratio. If x is multiplied by 3, y is also multiplied by 3.
70385.m: With proportional quantities, both change in the same ratio.

70386.q: A taxi ride costs a basic fee of 6 francs plus 3 francs per kilometre. Is the price proportional to the distance?
a: No, because of the basic fee
Yes, because each kilometre costs the same
Yes, because the price rises with the distance
No, because the price falls with the distance
70386.e: For 1 km you pay 9 francs, but for 2 km only 12 francs and not 18 francs. Because of the basic fee, the price does not double with the distance.
70386.m: A fixed basic fee stops a price from being proportional.

70387.q: For a relationship, y = 2.5 · x. Which y-value goes with x = 8?
70387.m: In the equation of a direct proportion, the factor comes before the x.

70388.q: 4 workers need 15 days to build a wall. How long do 6 workers who work just as fast need?
70388.e: The whole job is 4 · 15 = 60 working days. So 6 workers need 60 ÷ 6 = 10 days.
70388.m: More workers need less time for the same job.

70389.q: In an inverse proportion, what stays the same for all pairs of values?
a: The quotient y divided by x
70389.e: If x is doubled, y is halved. That is why the product x times y always stays the same.
70389.m: In inverse proportion, the product of the pairs of values is constant.

70390.q: What is the curve called that an inverse proportion makes in the coordinate system?
70390.e: The points lie on a curved line that gets closer and closer to the axes but never touches them. This curve is called a hyperbola.

70391.q: A supply of feed lasts 8 horses for 30 days. How long does it last for 12 horses?
70391.e: The supply is enough for 8 · 30 = 240 horse days. For 12 horses it lasts 240 ÷ 12 = 20 days.
70391.m: More eaters empty a supply faster.

70392.q: A journey takes exactly 3 hours at 60 km/h. How long does it take at 90 km/h?
70392.e: The distance is 60 · 3 = 180 km. At 90 km/h it takes 180 ÷ 90 = 2 hours.
70392.m: For the same distance, the journey time falls when the speed rises.

70393.q: In an inverse proportion, x is halved. What happens to y?
70393.e: Because the product x times y must stay the same, y becomes twice as big when x becomes half as big.
70393.m: If you halve one quantity, the other doubles.

a: Number of people and share of a pizza per person
Amount of petrol and price at the petrol station
Side length and perimeter of a square
Number of tickets and total price
70394.e: If twice as many people share the same pizza, each one only gets half. The other examples are directly proportional.
70394.m: When sharing fairly, everyone gets less if more people join in.

70395.q: A rectangle must always have an area of 36 cm². How long is it if it is 3 cm wide?
70395.e: Length times width gives 36 cm². So the length is 36 ÷ 3 = 12 cm.
70395.m: For the same area, a rectangle gets longer when it gets narrower.

70397.m: One tonne equals a thousand kilograms.

70398.m: To convert grams into kilograms, you divide by a thousand.

70400.q: How many grams are there in a tonne?
70400.m: A tonne has a million grams.

70401.q: How many centimetres do 5 dm and 30 cm make together?
70401.e: 5 dm is 50 cm. 50 cm + 30 cm = 80 cm.
70401.m: Before adding, all lengths must be in the same unit.

70402.q: How many milligrams are there in a gram?
70402.e: Milli means one thousandth. That is why a gram has 1000 milligrams.
70402.m: A milligram is a thousandth of a gram.

70403.q: Which prefix for units of measurement means “one hundredth”?
70403.e: A centimetre is a hundredth of a metre. Deci means one tenth and milli one thousandth.
70403.m: The prefix centi stands for one hundredth.

70404.q: How many metres are 0.6 km and 450 m together?
70404.m: You change kilometres into metres by multiplying by a thousand.

70405.q: A cyclist covers 36 km in 2 hours. What is her average speed?
70405.e: Speed is distance divided by time: 36 km ÷ 2 h = 18 km/h.
70405.m: Average speed shows how far you travel per hour.

70406.q: How many metres per second are 36 km/h?
70406.m: One metre per second is faster than one kilometre per hour.

70407.m: To get km/h, you multiply a speed in m/s by 3.6.

70408.q: A train travels at 120 km/h. How far does it get in 45 minutes?
70408.m: The distance is speed times time.

70409.q: A hiker walks at 4.5 km/h. How long does she take for 18 km?
70409.e: Time is distance divided by speed: 18 ÷ 4.5 = 4 hours.
70409.m: You get the time by dividing the distance by the speed.

70410.q: A cyclist rides at 12 km/h. How many minutes does he take for 1 km?
70410.e: In 60 minutes he rides 12 km. So for 1 km he needs 60 ÷ 12 = 5 minutes.
70410.m: If you know the speed, you can work out the time for one kilometre.

70411.q: What is the general speed limit on Swiss motorways?
70411.e: On Swiss motorways you may generally drive at no more than 120 km/h, unless a lower limit is signposted.
70411.m: On Swiss motorways the general limit is 120.

70412.q: Sound travels about 340 m per second in air. 3 seconds pass between the lightning and the thunder. About how far away is the storm?
70412.e: In 3 seconds sound travels about 3 · 340 = 1020 m. That is about 1 km.
70412.m: Three seconds between lightning and thunder mean a distance of about one kilometre.

70413.q: A train leaves at 8.47 and arrives at 10.12. How long is the journey?
70413.e: From 8.47 to 9.47 is 1 hour. From 9.47 to 10.12 there are another 25 minutes.
70413.m: Journey times are easiest to work out in steps over full hours.

70414.q: From 6.05 a bus leaves every 15 minutes. When does the fifth bus leave?
70414.e: The buses leave at 6.05, 6.20, 6.35, 6.50 and 7.05. So the fifth bus leaves at 7.05.
70414.m: For the first bus, no 15 minutes are added yet.

70415.q: How many minutes are 2 hours and 15 minutes?

70416.q: How many seconds are there in an hour?
70416.e: An hour has 60 minutes, each with 60 seconds. 60 · 60 = 3600 seconds.
70416.m: An hour has three thousand six hundred seconds.

70417.q: A night train leaves at 23.40 and travels for 50 minutes. When does it arrive?
70417.e: It is 20 minutes to midnight. The remaining 30 minutes take you to 0.30.
70417.m: After 24:00 the time starts again at 0:00.

70418.q: In a regular-interval timetable, a train leaves every hour at the same minute. The first leaves at 6.07. When does the fourth train leave?
70418.e: The trains leave at 6.07, 7.07, 8.07 and 9.07. So the fourth train leaves at 9.07.
70418.m: In a regular-interval timetable, trains leave at regular intervals at the same minute.

70419.q: A film starts at 19.35 and lasts 128 minutes. When does it end?
70419.e: 128 minutes are 2 hours and 8 minutes. 19.35 plus 2 h 8 min gives 21.43.
70419.m: You split long periods of time into hours and minutes.

70420.q: Lea has the marks 5, 4.5, 6 and 4.5. What is her average mark?
70420.e: The sum is 5 + 4.5 + 6 + 4.5 = 20. Divided by 4 marks, that gives 5.
70420.m: For the average, you divide the sum by the number of values.

70421.q: On five days, 12, 15, 9, 14 and 10 degrees are measured. What is the average temperature?
70421.m: The mean evens out high and low values.

70422.q: The average of 4 numbers is 8. What is their sum?
70422.e: Average times number of values gives the sum: 8 · 4 = 32.
70422.m: From the mean and the number of values, you can work out the sum.

70423.q: The mean of 4 numbers is 6. Now the number 11 is added. What is the new mean?
70423.e: The 4 numbers have the sum 4 · 6 = 24. With the 11 the sum is 35, and 35 ÷ 5 = 7.
70423.m: A new value above the mean raises the mean.

70424.q: Which measure is changed especially strongly by a single extremely large value?
70424.e: In the arithmetic mean, every value goes into the sum with its full size. That is why an outlier moves the average a lot.
70424.m: Outliers can badly distort an average.

70425.q: What is the mean of the numbers -3, 5, 7 and -1?
70425.e: The sum is -3 + 5 + 7 + (-1) = 8. Divided by 4, that gives 2.
70425.m: Negative numbers also count with their sign in the mean.

70426.q: A cyclist rides 42 km, 35 km and 49 km on three days. How many kilometres does he ride per day on average?
70426.m: The daily average is the total distance divided by the number of days.

70427.q: The mean of three numbers is 10. Two of the numbers are 8 and 9. What is the third number?
70427.e: The sum of the three numbers is 3 · 10 = 30. Missing: 30 minus 8 minus 9 = 13.
70427.m: You find missing values using the sum of all the values.

70428.q: What is the median of the values 2, 8, 4 and 10?
70428.e: In order, the list is 2, 4, 8, 10. With an even number of values you take the mean of the two middle values: (4 + 8) ÷ 2 = 6.
70428.m: With an even number of values, the median is between the two middle values.

70429.q: What is the median of a set of data?
a: The value in the middle of the ordered list
The most common value in the list
The sum divided by the number of values
The difference between the largest and smallest value
70429.e: You put all the values in order of size. The value exactly in the middle is the median.
70429.m: For the median, you must first put the values in order of size.

70430.q: What is the median of the values 12, 3, 7, 3, 20, 9 and 5?
70430.e: In order: 3, 3, 5, 7, 9, 12, 20. With 7 values, the 7 is in fourth place.
70430.m: With an odd number of values, the median is exactly one value in the list.

70431.q: An ordered list has 9 values. In which place is the median?
70431.e: Before the 5th value there are 4 values and after it there are also 4 values. So it is exactly in the middle.
70431.m: With an odd number of values, there is exactly one middle value.

70432.q: Five monthly wages are 4000, 4200, 4500, 4800 and 30,000 francs. What is the median?
70432.e: The values are already in order; the middle one is 4500 francs. Because of the very high wage, the mean would be 9500 francs.
70432.m: With wages, the median often tells you more than the average.

70433.q: The ordered values are 2, 4, x, 10, 12 and 15. The median is 8. What is x?
70433.e: The two middle values are x and 10. Their mean is 8, so x + 10 = 16 and x = 6.
70433.m: You can work back to a missing middle value from the median.

70434.q: What is the median of the values 1.5, 2.5, 4, 6, 6 and 7?
70434.e: The list is in order and has 6 values. The middle values are 4 and 6, so (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.
70434.m: You find the median of an ordered list by working in from both ends.

70435.q: The number 20 is added to the values 4, 6 and 9. How does the median change?
70435.e: Before, 6 is the middle value. With 4, 6, 9, 20 there are four values; the middle ones are 6 and 9, so (6 + 9) ÷ 2 = 7.5.
70435.m: An extra value can move the median, even if it changes it only a little.

70436.q: What is a chart with upright rectangles called?
70436.e: In a column chart the rectangles stand upright like columns. If they lie horizontally, it is called a bar chart.
70436.m: Columns stand upright, bars lie horizontally.

70437.q: In a pie chart, one sector is 72°. What proportion is that?
70437.e: The whole circle has 360°. 72 ÷ 360 = 0.2, which is 20 %.
70437.m: In a pie chart, 360 degrees stand for the whole.

70438.q: Which type of chart shows how often values occur that are grouped into classes such as 0 to 10 kg, 10 to 20 kg?
70438.e: A histogram uses rectangles that touch each other to show how many values are in each class.
70438.m: A histogram shows the frequencies of classes.

70439.q: Which type of chart is suitable for showing the link between height and weight of many people?
70439.e: In a scatter graph, each person is plotted as a point with two values. This lets you see whether the quantities are linked.
70439.m: A scatter graph shows how two features are linked.

70440.q: What does a box plot show besides the minimum and maximum?
70440.e: A box plot shows the minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum. The box covers the middle half of the values.
70440.m: The box of a box plot contains the middle half of the data.

70441.q: In a pictogram, one bike symbol stands for 50 bikes. How many bikes do 3.5 symbols show?
70441.e: 3.5 · 50 = 175. The half symbol stands for 25 bikes.
70441.m: In a pictogram you must always check what one symbol stands for.

70442.q: Why can a column chart be misleading if the y-axis does not start at 0?
a: Differences look bigger than they are
The columns all become the same height
The values are added up wrongly
The order of the columns changes
70442.e: If you cut off the bottom part of the axis, small differences between the columns look very large.
70442.m: With charts, it is always worth looking at the axis labels.

70443.q: What is a chart with horizontal rectangles called?
70443.e: In a bar chart the rectangles lie horizontally. It works well when the labels are long.
70443.m: Long labels fit well next to horizontal bars.

70444.q: A spinner has 8 equal sections, 3 of which are red. What is the probability of red?
70444.e: There are 3 favourable sections out of 8 possible, equally likely sections. The probability is 3/8.
70444.m: Probability is the number of favourable outcomes divided by the number of possible outcomes.

70445.q: What probability does a certain event have?
70445.e: A certain event always happens. Its probability is 1, which is 100 %.

70446.q: There are 200 tickets in a raffle drum, 10 of which win. What is the probability of winning with one ticket?
70446.e: 10 out of 200 tickets win. 10 ÷ 200 = 0.05, which is 5 %.
70446.m: Probabilities can also be given in per cent.

70447.q: A pack of Jass cards (a Swiss card game) has 36 cards with 4 aces. What is the probability of drawing an ace without looking?
70447.e: There are 4 aces among 36 cards. 4/36 simplified gives 1/9.
70447.m: Fractions in probability are simplified like other fractions.

70448.q: What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4 with a dice?
70448.e: Only 5 and 6 are greater than 4. That is 2 out of 6 outcomes, so 1/3.
70448.m: For probabilities, you first count all the favourable outcomes.

70449.q: You roll a fair dice 600 times. About how often do you expect a 3?
70449.m: With many trials, the relative frequency gets close to the probability.

70450.q: What is true of a Laplace experiment?
a: The outcomes depend on each other
70450.e: A Laplace experiment has outcomes that are all equally likely, as with a fair dice or a coin.
70450.m: A fair dice is a typical Laplace experiment.

70451.q: The probability of rain is 0.3. What is the probability that it does not rain?
70451.e: An event and its opposite add up to 1. 1 minus 0.3 = 0.7.
70451.m: The probability of the opposite event makes a probability up to 1.

70452.q: You roll two dice. What is the probability of a double (two equal numbers)?
70452.e: There are 36 equally likely outcomes, 6 of which are doubles (1 and 1 up to 6 and 6). 6/36 = 1/6.
70452.m: With two dice there are thirty-six possible outcomes.

70453.q: How many two-digit numbers can you make with the digits 1 to 5 if digits may be repeated?
70453.e: There are 5 choices for the tens place and again 5 for the ones place. 5 · 5 = 25 numbers, including 11 or 55, for example.
70453.m: If digits may repeat, the choice stays the same at every place.

70454.q: Mia has 3 T-shirts and 4 pairs of trousers. How many different combinations can she wear?
70454.e: Each T-shirt goes with 4 pairs of trousers. 3 · 4 = 12 combinations.

70455.q: A combination lock has 3 wheels with the digits 0 to 9. How many codes are there?
70455.e: Each wheel has 10 options. 10 · 10 · 10 = 1000 codes, from 000 to 999.
70455.m: Each extra wheel multiplies the number of codes by ten.

70456.q: Which diagram shows all the possibilities of a multi-step choice clearly as branches?
70456.e: In a tree diagram, each step branches into its possibilities. Every path from start to finish is one possible combination.
70456.m: A tree diagram helps you count systematically.

70457.q: A menu offers a choice of 2 starters, 3 main courses and 2 desserts. How many different menus are there?
70457.m: With several steps of choice, you multiply the number of possibilities at each step.

70458.m: The factorial is the product of all natural numbers up to that number.

70459.q: A team of two is picked from 6 children. How many different teams are possible?
70459.e: For ordered pairs there would be 6 · 5 = 30 possibilities. Since the order in the team does not matter, there are 30 : 2 = 15.
70459.m: If the order does not matter, you divide by the number of arrangements.

70460.q: 5 runners start a race. In how many ways can gold, silver and bronze be awarded?
70460.e: There are 5 possibilities for gold, then 4 for silver and 3 for bronze. 5 · 4 · 3 = 60.
70460.m: When order matters, the choice shrinks with every place awarded.

70461.q: How many ares are there in a hectare?
70461.e: An are is 100 m² and a hectare is 10,000 m². 10,000 : 100 = 100 ares.
70461.m: A hectare is made up of a hundred ares.

70462.q: How many hectares are there in a square kilometre?
70462.e: 1 km² is 1000 m · 1000 m = 1,000,000 m². Divided by 10,000 m² per hectare, that gives 100 ha.
70462.m: With units of area, the conversion step is often a hundred.

70463.q: How many square decimetres are 3.5 m²?
70463.m: Between neighbouring units of area there is a factor of a hundred.

70464.q: A building plot measures 2400 m². How many ares is that?
70464.m: An are is the area of a square ten metres by ten metres.

70466.q: How many litres are there in a hectolitre?
70466.e: The prefix hecto means hundred. A hectolitre is 100 litres.
70466.m: A hectolitre holds a hundred litres.

70467.q: How many centilitres are there in a litre?
70467.e: A litre has 10 decilitres and a decilitre has 10 centilitres. 10 · 10 = 100 cl.
70467.m: A hundred centilitres fit into one litre.

70468.q: How much liquid do 4 bottles of 7.5 dl each hold altogether?
70468.m: Large amounts in decilitres are converted into litres.

70469.q: What is the expression 3x + 5x − 2x in simplified form?
70469.e: You combine the like terms: 3 + 5 − 2 gives 6, so 6x remains.
70469.m: You combine like terms by adding their coefficients.

70470.e: Expanding gives 2a + 6 − a + 4. Combined, a + 10 remains.
70470.m: A minus sign in front of a bracket reverses all the signs inside when you remove it.

70471.e: You multiply the numbers (4 · 3 gives 12) and the variables (x · x gives x²).
70471.m: When multiplying terms, you multiply numbers and variables separately.

70472.e: Only 5a²b and 3a²b are like terms: 5 + 3 gives 8a²b. The term -2ab² has different exponents and stays as it is.
70472.m: Only terms with the same variables and the same exponents can be added.

70473.e: Removing the brackets gives -2x + 5 + 3x − 3. Combined, x + 2 remains.
70473.m: First remove the brackets, then combine like terms.

70474.q: What is the quotient (12x²y) : (4xy) for x and y not equal to zero?
70474.e: 12 : 4 gives 3, x² : x gives x and y : y gives 1. 3x remains.
70474.m: When dividing terms, you cancel numbers and variables one at a time.

70475.q: Which terms are called like terms?
a: Terms with the same variables and exponents
Terms with the same number of parts
70475.e: Like terms differ at most in their coefficient, for example 4xy² and -7xy².
70475.m: Like terms match exactly in their variable part.

70476.q: What does a(b + c) give by the distributive law?
70476.e: The factor a is multiplied by each term in the bracket.
70476.m: A factor in front of a bracket is multiplied by each term inside the bracket.

70477.e: (-x − 4)² equals (x + 4)², because squaring removes the sign. That gives x² + 8x + 16.
70477.m: The square of a sum always includes twice the product of the two terms.

70478.e: By the second binomial formula: x² − 2 · x · 3 + 3², so x² − 6x + 9.
70478.m: In the square of a difference, the middle term is negative.

70479.e: By the third binomial formula: (2x)² − 5², so 4x² − 25.
70479.m: Sum times difference of the same terms gives the difference of their squares.

70480.m: When squaring, the coefficients must be squared too.

70481.q: What is 99² if you calculate it as (100 − 1)²?
70481.m: Binomial formulas help with quick mental arithmetic.

70482.q: What is 51 · 49 if you calculate it as (50 + 1)(50 − 1)?
70482.e: By the third binomial formula: 50² − 1², so 2500 − 1, which is 2499.
70482.m: Two numbers the same distance from a round number can be multiplied cleverly with the third binomial formula.

70483.q: How can x² + 10x + 25 be written as a square?
70483.e: x² + 2 · 5 · x + 5² matches the first binomial formula with b equal to 5.
70483.m: A trinomial with two squares and the right middle term is a perfect square.

70484.e: Expanding gives x² + 2x + 1 − (x² − 2x + 1). What remains is 2x + 2x, so 4x.
70484.m: In the difference of two squares, many terms often cancel out.

70485.q: Which positive middle term makes 9x² + ... + 49 a perfect square?
70485.e: 9x² is (3x)² and 49 is 7². The middle term is 2 · 3x · 7, so 42x.
70485.m: The middle term of a perfect square is twice the product of the two bases.

70486.q: What is the solution of the equation 7x − 4 = 3x + 20?
70486.e: You subtract 3x and add 4. This gives 4x = 24 and x = 6.
70486.m: You solve a linear equation by isolating the variable step by step.

70487.q: What is the solution of the equation 3(x + 4) = 5x − 2?
70487.e: Expanding gives 3x + 12 = 5x − 2. From this, 14 = 2x and x = 7.
70487.m: First remove the brackets, then bring all the variables to one side.

70488.q: What is the solution of the equation x/4 − 3 = 2?
70488.e: You add 3 and get x/4 = 5. Multiplying by 4 gives x = 20.
70488.m: You get rid of a fraction in an equation by multiplying by the denominator.

70489.q: How many solutions does the equation 2x + 3 = 2x + 5 have?
70489.e: Subtracting 2x leaves the false statement 3 = 5. No x can satisfy the equation.
70489.m: If rearranging leads to a false statement, the solution set is empty.

70490.q: How many solutions does the equation 4(x + 1) = 4x + 4 have?
70490.e: After expanding, the same terms appear on the left and right. Every real number satisfies the equation.
70490.m: An equation that is true for every number is called an identity.

70491.q: What is the solution of the equation 0.5x + 1.5 = 6?
70491.e: You subtract 1.5 and get 0.5x = 4.5. Dividing by 0.5 gives x = 9.
70491.m: Dividing by 0.5 is the same as doubling.

70492.q: A bike costs x francs, a helmet 60 francs less. Together they cost 340 francs. How much does the bike cost?
70492.e: The equation is x + (x − 60) = 340. From this, 2x = 400 and x = 200.
70492.m: In word problems, first translate the text carefully into an equation.

a: A rearrangement that does not change the solution set
A rearrangement that doubles the variable
Swapping both sides and changing the signs
Squaring both sides of an equation
70493.e: If you add, subtract, multiply or divide both sides by the same number (but not divide by zero), the solution set stays the same.
70493.m: Whatever you do to one side of the equation, you must also do to the other side.

70494.q: What is the solution of the equation (2x − 1)/3 = (x + 4)/2?
70494.e: Multiplying by 6 gives 2(2x − 1) = 3(x + 4), so 4x − 2 = 3x + 12 and x = 14.
70494.m: You get rid of several fractions in an equation with the lowest common denominator.

70495.q: What is the solution of the system x + 2y = 11 and x − y = 2?
70495.e: Subtracting the second equation from the first gives 3y = 9 and y = 3. Substituting gives x = 5.
70495.m: A solution of a system of equations must satisfy all the equations at the same time.

70496.q: What is the solution of the system 2x + y = 11 and x + y = 7?
70496.e: Subtracting the second equation from the first leaves x = 4. Then y = 7 − 4 = 3.
70496.m: When you subtract two equations, one variable can disappear.

70497.q: What is the method called in which you add equations so that one variable disappears?
70497.e: In the elimination method you multiply the equations so that one variable cancels out when you add them.
70497.m: Systems of linear equations can be solved by elimination, substitution or equating.

70498.q: How many solutions does the system x + 3y = 4 and 2x + 6y = 8 have?
70498.e: The second equation is double the first. Both describe the same line, and every point on it is a solution.
70498.m: If one equation is a multiple of the other, the system has infinitely many solutions.

70499.q: What does it mean geometrically if a system of two linear equations in two variables has exactly one solution?
a: The lines meet at one point
The lines lie on top of each other
The lines pass through the origin
70499.e: Each equation describes a line. The common solution is the only point the two lines share.
70499.m: The solution of a system of two lines is the point where they intersect.

70500.q: At the farm shop, 3 apples and 2 pears cost 3.40 francs together, and 1 apple and 2 pears cost 2.20 francs. How much does one apple cost?
70500.e: The difference between the two purchases is 2 apples for 1.20 francs. So one apple costs 60 centimes.
70500.m: If you compare two similar equations, one unknown often disappears.

70501.q: Chickens and rabbits live on a farm. Together they have 20 heads and 56 legs. How many rabbits are there?
70501.e: With h chickens and k rabbits: h + k = 20 and 2h + 4k = 56. Subtracting double the first equation leaves 2k = 16, so k = 8.
70501.m: For word problems with two unknowns, you set up two equations.

70502.q: What is the value of x in the system x + y + z = 6, y + z = 5 and z = 3?
70502.e: From z = 3 it follows that y = 2. Substituting into the first equation gives x = 6 − 2 − 3 = 1.
70502.m: A system in triangular form is solved from the bottom up by substitution.

70503.q: What is the solution set of the inequality 2x + 3 < 11?
70503.e: Subtracting 3 gives 2x < 8. Dividing by 2 gives x < 4.
70503.m: You solve inequalities in a similar way to equations.

70504.q: What is the solution set of the inequality -3x > 12?
70504.e: You divide by -3. Because the number is negative, the inequality sign is reversed.
70504.m: When you multiply or divide by a negative number, the inequality sign flips.

70505.q: What is the solution set of the inequality x/2 + 1 ≤ 4?
70505.e: Subtracting 1 gives x/2 ≤ 3. Multiplying by 2 gives x ≤ 6.
70505.m: The sign ≤ means less than or equal to.

70506.q: What is the smallest whole number that satisfies 5x − 2 > 13?
70506.e: From 5x > 15 it follows that x > 3. The smallest whole number greater than 3 is 4.
70506.m: In a strict inequality, the boundary itself is not part of the solution.

70507.q: Which numbers x satisfy the inequality |x| < 3?
70507.e: The absolute value is the distance from zero. It is less than 3 for all numbers between -3 and 3.
70507.m: The absolute value of a number gives its distance from zero.

70508.e: A product is negative when the factors have different signs. This is exactly the case between the zeros -2 and 1.
70508.m: You examine the sign of a product using the zeros of its factors.

70509.q: How do you write the numbers x with 2 ≤ x < 5 as an interval?
70509.e: 2 is included, so it gets a square bracket. 5 is not included, so it gets a round bracket.
70509.m: A round bracket in interval notation excludes the endpoint.

70510.q: Lena has 50 francs. A cinema ticket costs 14 francs. What is the largest number of tickets she can buy?
70510.e: 14n ≤ 50 must hold, so n ≤ 3.57. The largest whole number is 3.
70510.m: When counting things, only whole numbers are possible as solutions.

70511.q: What are the solutions of the equation (x + 2)² = 25?
70511.e: From (x + 2)² = 25 it follows that x + 2 = 5 or x + 2 = -5. That gives x = 3 or x = -7.
70511.m: When taking a square root in an equation, you must consider both signs.

70512.q: What are the solutions of the equation x² − 5x = 0?
70512.e: Factorising gives x(x − 5) = 0. A product is zero when one factor is zero.
70512.m: If there is no term without x, you can take x out as a factor.

70513.q: What are the solutions of the equation (x − 3)(x + 8) = 0?
70513.e: A product is zero when one factor is zero: x − 3 = 0 gives 3, x + 8 = 0 gives -8.
70513.m: A product is zero exactly when at least one factor is zero.

70514.q: What are the solutions of the equation x² − 7x + 12 = 0?
70514.e: You need two numbers with a sum of 7 and a product of 12. These are 3 and 4.
70514.m: The solutions of an equation in normal form can sometimes be guessed directly.

70515.q: According to Vieta's theorem, what is the product of the solutions of x² + px + q = 0?
70515.e: If you write the equation as (x − x₁)(x − x₂) = 0 and expand, the constant term is x₁ · x₂.
70515.m: Vieta's theorem links the solutions to the coefficients.

70516.q: What is the form x² + px + q = 0 of a quadratic equation called?
70516.e: In normal form, the squared term has the coefficient 1. You get it by dividing by the coefficient of x².
70516.m: The normal form always starts with x² without a number in front.

70517.q: What is the largest number of real solutions a quadratic equation can have?
70517.e: A parabola can cross the x-axis at most twice. That is why there are at most two real solutions.
70517.m: The degree of an equation limits the number of its solutions.

70518.q: What are the solutions of the equation x(x − 4) = 12?
70518.e: You rearrange to x² − 4x − 12 = 0, so (x − 6)(x + 2) = 0. From this, x = 6 or x = -2.
70518.m: First bring a quadratic equation into the form with zero on one side.

70519.q: Which number do you add when completing the square for x² + 6x?
70519.e: You halve the coefficient 6 and square it: 3² gives 9. This gives (x + 3)².
70519.m: When completing the square, you add the square of half the coefficient of x.

70520.q: What is the quadratic formula for ax² + bx + c = 0?
70520.e: The formula comes from completing the square on the general form. It gives all the real solutions.
70520.m: With the quadratic formula you can solve any quadratic equation.

70521.q: How many real solutions does ax² + bx + c = 0 have if b² − 4ac < 0?
70521.e: You cannot take a real square root of a negative number. That is why there is no real solution.
70521.m: If the expression under the root is negative, there is no real solution.

70522.q: How many real solutions does ax² + bx + c = 0 have if b² − 4ac = 0?
70522.e: The root is then zero, and plus and minus give the same result -b/(2a).
70522.m: If the expression under the root is zero, both solutions coincide.

70523.q: What is the expression b² − 4ac in the quadratic formula called?
70523.e: The name comes from the Latin discriminare, to distinguish. The sign of the expression tells you how many solutions there are.
70523.m: The discriminant decides how many real solutions there are.

70524.q: What are the solutions of the equation 2x² − 5x − 3 = 0?
70524.e: Under the root is 25 + 24 = 49. So x = (5 ± 7)/4, which gives 3 or -0.5.
70524.m: Before using the quadratic formula, read off a, b and c carefully.

70525.q: What are the solutions of the equation x² − 2x − 1 = 0?
70525.e: Under the root is 4 + 4 = 8. So x = (2 ± √8)/2, and since √8 = 2√2 this gives 1 ± √2.
70525.m: Give solutions with roots exactly and simplify them.

70526.q: For which values of k does x² + kx + 9 = 0 have exactly one solution?
70526.e: k² − 36 = 0 must hold. From this, k² = 36, so k = 6 or k = -6.
70526.m: A double solution occurs exactly when the expression under the root is zero.

70527.q: In Germany, what is the quadratic formula often jokingly called?
70527.e: You are supposed to know it so well that you could recite it even if someone woke you at midnight.
70527.m: In Germany, the quadratic formula has the nickname “midnight formula”.

70528.q: What are the solutions of the equation x² − 6x − 16 = 0?
70528.e: Under the root is 36 + 64 = 100. So x = (6 ± 10)/2, which gives 8 or -2.
70528.m: Checking by substitution shows whether the solutions are correct.

70530.q: What is the value of 8 to the power of 2/3?
70530.e: The denominator 3 means the cube root: the cube root of 8 is 2. Then you square it and get 4.
70530.m: With a fraction as the exponent, you take the root and then raise to the power.

70531.q: What is (a/b)³ for b not equal to zero?
70531.e: You raise a fraction to a power by raising the numerator and the denominator to that power.
70531.m: For a fraction, the numerator and denominator are each raised to the power.

70532.q: What is the value of a⁰ for a not equal to zero?
70532.e: a³ : a³ equals a⁰, and a number divided by itself gives 1.
70532.m: Any number except zero to the power of zero equals one.

70533.e: A negative exponent means the reciprocal: 2⁻³ is 1/2³, so 1/8.
70533.m: A negative exponent stands for the reciprocal of the power.

70534.e: Each factor in the bracket is squared: (x²)² gives x⁴ and (y³)² gives y⁶.
70534.m: You raise a product to a power by raising each factor to that power.

70535.e: The exponents are added: 4 + (-2) gives 2, and 3² is 9.
70535.m: The addition law for the same base also holds with negative exponents.

70536.e: With the same exponent you multiply the bases: (5 · 2)³ gives 10³, so 1000.
70536.m: With the same exponent, you may multiply the bases.

70537.e: 0.3 · 0.3 equals 0.09. That is why 0.3 is the square root of 0.09.
70537.m: The square root is the non-negative number that, multiplied by itself, gives the number under the root.

70538.e: √8 is √(4 · 2), so 2√2. Together with √2 that gives 3√2.
70538.m: You can only add roots if they have the same number under the root.

70539.e: First you work out 16 + 9 equals 25 under the root. The square root of 25 is 5, not 4 + 3.
70539.m: The root of a sum is not the sum of the roots.

70540.e: You may multiply roots: √(2 · 18) is √36, so 6.
70540.m: The product of two roots is the root of the product.

70541.q: What is the solution of the equation √x = -3 in the real numbers?
70541.e: A square root is never negative. Checking x = 9 gives √9 = 3, not -3.
70541.m: With equations involving roots, checking is essential.

70542.q: What is √(x²) for every real number x?
70542.e: The square root is never negative. For x = -3, √9 equals 3, which is the absolute value of x.
70542.m: The root of a square gives the absolute value.

70543.q: What is the value of the fourth root of 81?
70543.e: 3 · 3 · 3 · 3 equals 81. That is why 3 is the fourth root of 81.
70543.m: The nth root is the inverse of raising to the power of n.

70544.q: How do you write a to the power of 3/4 as a root?
70544.e: The denominator of the exponent gives the index of the root, the numerator gives the exponent under the root.
70544.m: Powers with fractional exponents can be written as roots.

70545.q: What is the value of log₂(8)?
70545.e: You need the exponent to which 2 must be raised to get 8. 2³ equals 8.
70545.m: The logarithm is the exponent you are looking for.

70546.q: What is the value of log₁₀(0.01)?
70546.e: 0.01 is 1/100, so 10⁻². That is why the base-10 logarithm is -2.
70546.m: Logarithms of numbers between 0 and 1 are negative.

70547.q: What is the value of log_b(1) for any valid base b?
70547.e: Any valid base to the power of 0 gives 1. That is why the logarithm of 1 is always 0.
70547.m: The logarithm of one is zero for every base.

70548.q: According to the laws of logarithms, what is log(a · b)?
70548.e: Because exponents are added when powers are multiplied, the logarithm of a product becomes a sum.
70548.m: The logarithm turns a product into a sum.

70549.q: What is the base of the natural logarithm ln?
70549.e: The natural logarithm has the base e, which is about 2.718.
70549.m: The natural logarithm is the logarithm to base e.

70550.q: What is the solution of the equation 2ˣ = 32?
70550.e: x = log₂(32), and 2⁵ gives 32. So x = 5.
70550.m: You solve exponential equations with the logarithm.

70551.q: What is the value of log₂(4⁵)?
70551.e: By the power law, log₂(4⁵) equals 5 · log₂(4), so 5 · 2, which is 10.
70551.m: An exponent inside a logarithm can be moved in front of the logarithm as a factor.

70552.q: Which clockmaker from Lichtensteig in the Toggenburg developed logarithm tables independently of John Napier?
70552.e: Jost Bürgi calculated tables equivalent to logarithms before 1610. They were published in Prague in 1620 as the “Progress Tabulen”.
70552.m: In Jost Bürgi, Switzerland has a co-inventor of logarithms.

70553.q: How do you write 3 400 000 in scientific notation?
70553.e: You move the decimal point 6 places to the left until you get a number between 1 and 10.
70553.m: In scientific notation, the number in front of the power of ten is from 1 to less than 10.

70554.q: How do you write 7.03 · 10⁻⁵ as a decimal?
70554.e: The exponent -5 means you move the decimal point 5 places to the left.
70554.m: A negative exponent moves the decimal point to the left.

70555.e: You multiply 2 · 4 equals 8 and add the exponents 3 + 5 equals 8.
70555.m: When multiplying, you multiply the leading numbers and add the exponents.

70556.e: You divide 6 : 3 equals 2 and subtract the exponents 8 − 2 equals 6.
70556.m: When dividing, you divide the leading numbers and subtract the exponents.

70557.q: Roughly how fast is the speed of light in a vacuum?
70557.e: The speed of light is exactly 299 792 458 m/s, about 300 000 km per second.
70557.m: Light travels about 300 000 kilometres in one second.

70558.q: Which form is correct scientific notation?
70558.e: All four numbers are the same size. Only in 4.5 · 10⁷ is the leading number between 1 and 10.
70558.m: The leading number in scientific notation has exactly one non-zero digit before the decimal point.

70559.q: A calculator shows 2.5E-3. Which number is meant?
70559.m: Calculators often write the power of ten with the letter E.

70560.q: Switzerland has about 9 million inhabitants (as of 2024). How do you write 9 million in scientific notation?
70560.e: A million has 6 zeros and equals 10⁶. So 9 million is 9 · 10⁶.
70560.m: A million equals ten to the power of six.

70561.e: Both terms contain the factor 3: 6x is 3 · 2x and 9 is 3 · 3.
70561.m: When factorising, you look for the highest common factor.

70562.e: You need two numbers with a product of 6 and a sum of -5. These are -2 and -3.
70562.m: You split a trinomial x² + bx + c using two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is b.

70563.e: The highest common factor is 2ab. Left in the bracket are 2a and -3b.
70563.m: Take out numbers and variables as completely as possible.

70564.q: What is x³ − x when fully factorised?
70564.e: First you take out x and get x(x² − 1). Then you split x² − 1 into (x − 1)(x + 1).
70564.m: After taking out a factor, check whether the bracket can be factorised further.

70565.q: What is ax + ay + bx + by when factorised?
70565.e: You group it as a(x + y) + b(x + y) and then take out (x + y).
70565.m: With four terms, factorising step by step in groups often helps.

70566.q: What is x² + x − 12 when factorised?
70566.e: You need two numbers with a product of -12 and a sum of 1. These are 4 and -3.
70566.m: If the constant term is negative, the two numbers have different signs.

70567.e: First you take out 2: 2(x² + 4x + 4). The bracket is a perfect square.
70567.m: Often you take out a number first and then spot a binomial formula.

70568.q: Which expression cannot be factorised over the real numbers?
70568.e: x² + 1 is positive for every real x and has no real zero. That is why it has no real linear factors.
70568.m: A quadratic expression with no real zero cannot be factorised over the real numbers.

70569.q: What is the general equation of a linear function?
70569.e: In f(x) = mx + q, m is the gradient and q is the y-intercept. The variable x appears only to the first power.
70569.m: The graph of a linear function is always a straight line.

70570.q: What is the y-intercept of the line y = −3x + 7?
70570.e: The y-intercept is the value at x = 0: y = −3·0 + 7 = 7. The number −3 is the gradient.
70570.m: The y-intercept is the constant term of the equation of the line.

70571.q: What is the equation of the line with gradient 2 that passes through the point (1|5)?
70571.e: Substituting into y = 2x + q gives 5 = 2·1 + q, so q = 3. The equation is y = 2x + 3.
70571.m: You find the y-intercept by putting a point into the equation of the line.

70572.q: How are two lines positioned relative to each other if they have the same gradient but different y-intercepts?
70572.e: The same gradient means the same direction. Because the y-intercepts are different, they do not coincide, so they are parallel.
70572.m: Lines with the same gradient are parallel.

70573.q: A taxi charges a basic fare of 6 francs and 4 francs per kilometre. How much does a 12 km ride cost?
70573.e: The price is the linear function P(x) = 4x + 6. For x = 12, P = 48 + 6 = 54 francs.
70573.m: With fares that include a basic charge, the basic charge is the y-intercept.

70574.q: At which point do the lines y = x + 1 and y = -x + 5 intersect?
70574.e: Setting them equal: x + 1 = -x + 5 gives 2x = 4, so x = 2. Substituting gives y = 3.
70574.m: You find the intersection of two lines by setting their expressions equal.

70575.q: What is a linear function of the form f(x) = mx, whose graph passes through the origin, called?
70575.e: When q = 0, f(x) is proportional to x: if x doubles, f(x) doubles too. The graph is a line through the origin.
70575.m: Proportional functions have a line through the origin as their graph.

70576.q: What does the graph of the constant function f(x) = 4 look like?
a: A line parallel to the x-axis
A line parallel to the y-axis
70576.e: For every x the function value is 4. So the graph is a horizontal line at height 4, parallel to the x-axis.
70576.m: A constant function has a gradient of zero.

70577.q: What is the gradient of the line through the points (0|4) and (2|0)?
70577.e: m = (0 − 4)/(2 − 0) = -4/2 = -2. So the line goes downwards.
70577.m: A negative gradient means the line goes downwards.

70578.q: Which expression gives the gradient m between the points (x₁|y₁) and (x₂|y₂)?
70578.e: The gradient is the change in the y direction divided by the change in the x direction. You can show it with a gradient triangle.
70578.m: The gradient is the vertical difference divided by the horizontal difference.

70579.q: What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to a line with gradient 2?
70579.e: For perpendicular lines, m₁·m₂ = -1. From 2·m₂ = -1 it follows that m₂ = -1/2.
70579.m: The gradients of two perpendicular lines multiply to give minus one.

70580.q: A road has a 10 % gradient. How many metres does it climb over 500 m of horizontal distance?
70580.e: A 10 % gradient means 10 m of height per 100 m of horizontal distance. Over 500 m that is 0.1·500 = 50 m.
70580.m: The percentage given for roads refers to the horizontal distance.

70581.q: What is the angle of a line with gradient 1?
70581.e: tan(α) = m. From tan(α) = 1 it follows that α = 45°.
70581.m: The tangent of the angle of slope equals the gradient.

70582.q: What is the gradient of a line with an angle of slope of 60°?
70582.e: The gradient is m = tan(60°) = √3, about 1.73.
70582.m: The larger the angle of slope, the larger the gradient.

70583.q: The Pilatus Railway has a maximum gradient of 48 %. Roughly what angle of slope is that?
70583.e: The angle is α = arctan(0.48), about 25.6°. The Pilatus Railway is considered the steepest cogwheel railway in the world.
70583.m: Gradient in per cent and angle of slope are not the same thing.

70584.q: What is the gradient of the line with the equation 2y = 6x + 4?
70584.e: Dividing by 2 gives y = 3x + 2. The gradient is the factor in front of x, so 3.
70584.m: You can read off the gradient once the equation is solved for y.

70585.q: What does the parabola of f(x) = ax² look like if a is negative?
a: It lies entirely above the x-axis
70585.e: If a < 0, all function values except at x = 0 are negative. So the parabola opens downwards.
70585.m: The sign of a decides which way the parabola opens.

70586.q: Which parabola is narrower than the standard parabola?
70586.e: If the absolute value of a is greater than 1, the parabola is stretched and looks narrower. With y = 0.5x² it is squashed, and the others are only shifted.
70586.m: A large absolute value of a makes a parabola narrower.

70587.q: What is the graph of the function f(x) = x² called?
70587.e: The function f(x) = x² is the simplest quadratic function. Its graph is called the standard parabola and has its vertex at the origin.
70587.m: The standard parabola is the graph of x squared.

70588.q: About which axis is the standard parabola symmetrical?
70588.e: (-x)² = x², so f(-x) = f(x). That is why the graph is symmetrical about the y-axis.
70588.m: Functions with f(-x) equal to f(x) are symmetrical about the y-axis.

70589.q: What does the coefficient c in f(x) = ax² + bx + c tell you?
70589.e: If you put in x = 0, you get f(0) = c. So the parabola crosses the y-axis at the point (0|c).
70589.m: The constant term of a parabola is its y-intercept.

70590.q: The height of a ball is h(t) = -5t² + 20t (h in metres, t in seconds). How high is the ball after 1 second?
70590.e: Substituting gives h(1) = -5·1 + 20·1 = 15. So the ball is 15 m high.
70590.m: You calculate function values by putting in the x value.

70591.q: What is the range of the function f(x) = x² + 2?
70591.e: Because x² is never negative, x² + 2 is always at least 2. The smallest value 2 is reached at x = 0.
70591.m: A parabola that opens upwards has its smallest value at the vertex.

70592.q: What is the path of a ball thrown at an angle called, if air resistance is ignored?
70592.e: Without air resistance, the height is a quadratic function of the horizontal distance. So the path is a parabola.
70592.m: Without air resistance, a thrown ball flies along a parabola.

70593.q: What is the form f(x) = a(x − d)² + e of a quadratic function called?
70593.e: In this form you can read off the vertex S(d|e) directly. That is why it is called vertex form.
70593.m: You read off the vertex directly from the vertex form.

70594.q: Where is the vertex of the parabola f(x) = (x − 2)² + 5?
70594.e: In vertex form a(x − d)² + e, the vertex is S(d|e). Here d = 2 and e = 5.
70594.m: In vertex form, the x-coordinate has the opposite sign to the number in the bracket.

70595.q: Where is the vertex of the parabola f(x) = -(x + 4)² − 1?
70595.e: x + 4 = x − (-4), so d = -4. With e = -1 the vertex is S(-4|-1), a maximum.
70595.m: A plus sign in the bracket means a shift to the left.

70596.q: Which expression gives the x-coordinate of the vertex of f(x) = ax² + bx + c?
70596.e: Completing the square gives the vertex at x = -b/(2a). There the derivative 2ax + b is also zero.
70596.m: The axis of symmetry of a parabola is at minus b over two a.

70597.q: Where is the vertex of the parabola f(x) = 2x² − 8x + 3?
70597.e: Completing the square gives f(x) = 2(x² − 4x + 4) − 8 + 3 = 2(x − 2)² − 5. So S(2|-5).
70597.m: You get the y-coordinate of the vertex by substituting the x-coordinate.

70598.q: What kind of point is the vertex of the parabola f(x) = -x² + 6x, and where is it?
70598.e: Because a = -1 the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex is a maximum. Completing the square gives f(x) = -(x − 3)² + 9.
70598.m: For a parabola that opens downwards, the vertex is the highest point.

70599.q: A rectangular enclosure is to be fenced with 40 m of fencing. What is the largest possible area?
70599.e: With side x the other side is 20 − x, so A(x) = x(20 − x). The vertex is at x = 10, and the largest area is 10·10 = 100 m².
70599.m: In optimisation problems with parabolas, the optimum is at the vertex.

70600.q: What is the equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola y = (x − 7)² + 1?
70600.e: The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through the vertex S(7|1). Its equation is x = 7.
70600.m: The axis of symmetry of a parabola runs vertically through the vertex.

70601.q: Where is the variable x in an exponential function such as f(x) = 3ˣ?
70601.e: In exponential functions the base is fixed and the variable is in the exponent. With power functions such as x³ it is the other way round.
70601.m: In exponential functions, the variable is in the exponent.

70602.q: Through which point does the graph of every function f(x) = bˣ with b > 0 pass?
70602.e: For every base b > 0, b⁰ = 1. So every such graph passes through the point (0|1).
70602.m: Any number except zero to the power of zero equals one.

70603.q: What is the rounded value of Euler's number e?
70603.e: Euler's number is e ≈ 2.71828. The number 3.142 is π, 1.618 is the golden ratio and 1.414 is the square root of 2.

70604.q: Which horizontal asymptote does the graph of f(x) = 2ˣ have?
70604.e: For very small x, 2ˣ becomes as small as you like but stays positive. The graph gets closer and closer to the x-axis without touching it.
70604.m: On the left, the graph of 2 to the power of x hugs the x-axis.

70605.q: For which base b is the function f(x) = bˣ strictly decreasing?
70605.e: If the base is between 0 and 1, the function value gets smaller as x grows. With b > 1 the function increases, with b = 1 it is constant.
70605.m: A base between zero and one describes decrease.

70606.q: What is f(3) for the function f(x) = 5·2ˣ?
70606.e: f(3) = 5·2³ = 5·8 = 40. First you raise to the power, then you multiply.
70606.m: With a times b to the power of x, the power is worked out first.

70607.q: Which function is equal to its own derivative?
70607.e: The natural exponential function eˣ has the derivative eˣ. That is why e is the most important base in calculus.
70607.m: The derivative of e to the power of x is again e to the power of x.

70608.q: How does f(x) = 0.5ˣ behave for very large x?
70608.e: With every step of 1 the value halves. The values get as small as you like but stay positive.
70608.m: An exponential function never becomes negative.

70609.q: What is characteristic of exponential growth?
a: The same factor in equal time intervals
The same amount added in equal time intervals
Growth up to a fixed limit
70609.e: In exponential growth the amount is multiplied by the same factor in each time step. In linear growth the same amount is added each time.
70609.m: Exponential growth means multiplying by a constant factor.

70610.q: A culture of 100 bacteria doubles every hour. How many bacteria are there after 5 hours?
70610.e: N(5) = 100·2⁵ = 100·32 = 3200. The number doubles after every hour.
70610.m: When something doubles, you multiply by two in each time step.

70611.q: Which growth factor belongs to an increase of 4 % per year?
70611.e: 4 % is added to the old amount of 100 %, giving 104 %. As a decimal that is the factor 1.04.
70611.m: The growth factor is one plus the percentage as a decimal.

70612.q: A quantity grows by 7 % a year. After roughly how many years has it doubled?
70612.e: From 1.07ⁿ = 2 it follows that n = ln(2)/ln(1.07), about 10.2 years.
70612.m: The doubling time depends only on the growth factor, not on the starting amount.

70613.q: According to a legend, there is 1 grain of rice on the first square of a chessboard and twice as many on each following square. How many grains are on the 64th square?
70613.e: Square n holds 2ⁿ⁻¹ grains, because square 1 starts with 2⁰ = 1. On square 64 there are 2⁶³, over 9 quintillion grains.
70613.m: The chessboard legend shows how quickly doubling leads to huge numbers.

70614.q: A population grows by 10 % every year. By what percentage has it grown in total after 2 years?
70614.e: The factor after 2 years is 1.1² = 1.21. That is an increase of 21 %, not 20 %.
70614.m: You cannot simply add percentage increases over several years.

70615.q: Water lilies double their area every day and cover the whole pond on day 30. On which day was the pond half covered?
70615.e: Because the area doubles every day, it was exactly half as big one day earlier. So the pond was half covered on day 29.
70615.m: Exponential growth looks harmless for a long time and then suddenly becomes huge.

70616.q: What does exponential growth look like on a graph with a logarithmic y-axis?
70616.e: From N = N₀·bᵗ it follows that log(N) = log(N₀) + t·log(b). That is a linear function of t, so a straight line.
70616.m: On a logarithmic scale, exponential growth becomes a straight line.

70617.q: Which growth model starts almost exponentially, then levels off and approaches an upper limit?
70617.e: In logistic growth a capacity limit slows the growth down. The graph is S-shaped.
70617.m: Growth with a saturation limit follows an S-shape.

70618.q: What do 1000 francs grow to in 2 years at 2 % compound interest?
70618.e: K = 1000·1.02² = 1000·1.0404 = 1040.40 francs. The interest from the first year also earns interest in the second year.
70618.m: With compound interest, capital grows more than with simple interest.

70619.q: Which formula gives the capital Kₙ after n years with compound interest at p %?
70619.e: Each year the capital is multiplied by the interest factor 1 + p/100. After n years that gives the nth power of this factor.
70619.m: Capital with compound interest grows exponentially.

70620.q: According to the rule of 72, after roughly how many years does capital double at 3 % interest?
70620.e: The rule of thumb is doubling time ≈ 72/p. At 3 % that gives 72/3 = 24 years; the exact value is about 23.4 years.
70620.m: With the rule of 72 you can estimate how long it takes capital to double.

a: Interest is added to the capital and earns interest too
Interest is paid out every year
The interest rate rises every year
Interest is only calculated on the starting capital
70621.e: With compound interest, the interest stays in the account. The next year it earns interest itself.
70621.m: With compound interest, the interest also earns interest.

70622.q: Which type of function describes capital with compound interest over time?
70622.e: The capital is K(n) = K₀·qⁿ with the fixed interest factor q. Time is in the exponent, so it is an exponential function.
70622.m: Simple interest grows linearly, compound interest grows exponentially.

70623.q: Which starting capital grows to 2100 francs in one year at 5 % interest?
70623.m: To work backwards, you divide by the interest factor.

70624.q: What do 5000 francs grow to in 3 years at 1 % compound interest?
70624.m: With low interest rates, the compound interest effect is small over a short time.

70625.q: Which number does (1 + 1/n)ⁿ approach as n gets bigger and bigger?
70625.e: The Basel mathematician Jakob Bernoulli studied this expression for interest paid more and more often. The limit is Euler's number e.
70625.m: Continuous compounding leads to Euler's number.

70626.q: After how many whole years has capital at 10 % compound interest first more than doubled?
70626.e: 1.1⁷ ≈ 1.95 is still less than 2, but 1.1⁸ ≈ 2.14 is greater. So after 8 years it is more than twice as much.
70626.m: With compound interest, capital doubles faster than with simple interest.

70627.q: What is meant by the half-life of a radioactive substance?
a: The time after which half of it has decayed
Half the time until it has completely decayed
The time in which the radiation doubles
Half the lifetime of an atom
70627.e: After one half-life, on average half of the atomic nuclei have decayed. After each further half-life the rest halves again.
70627.m: After each half-life, only half is left.

70628.q: Roughly how long is the half-life of carbon-14?
70628.e: Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5730 years.

70629.q: What fraction of a radioactive substance is left after 3 half-lives?
70629.e: After each half-life the rest halves: (1/2)³ = 1/8. That is 12.5 %.
70629.m: After n half-lives, one half to the power of n is left.

70630.q: Iodine-131 has a half-life of about 8 days. How much of 80 mg is left after 24 days?
70630.e: 24 days are 3 half-lives. 80 mg becomes 40 mg, then 20 mg and finally 10 mg.
70630.m: Divide the time by the half-life and halve that many times.

70631.q: Which formula describes the remaining amount N(t) with half-life T?
70631.e: For each half-life you multiply by 1/2. After time t, t/T half-lives have passed.

70632.q: What is the known half-life of carbon-14 used for?
70632.e: Living things take in carbon-14; after death it decays. From the remaining amount you calculate the age; this is called radiocarbon dating.
70632.m: Radiocarbon dating tells you the age of bones and wood.

70633.q: After how many half-lives is less than 1 % of a substance left for the first time?
70633.e: (1/2)⁶ ≈ 1.56 % is still more than 1 %, (1/2)⁷ ≈ 0.78 % is less. So it takes 7 half-lives.
70633.m: After about seven half-lives, almost everything has decayed.

70634.q: How is the half-life T related to the decay constant λ?
70634.e: From e^(-λT) = 1/2 it follows that λT = ln(2), so T = ln(2)/λ.
70634.m: The larger the decay constant, the shorter the half-life.

70635.q: What happens to the half-life if you take twice the amount of a radioactive substance?
70635.e: The half-life is a property of the substance and does not depend on the amount. Even with twice the amount, half decays in the same time.
70635.m: The half-life does not depend on the starting amount.

70636.q: What is the period of the function f(x) = sin(x)?
70636.e: After one full turn on the unit circle, that is 2π or 360°, the values repeat. The period is 2π.

70637.e: The sine is the y-coordinate of a point on the unit circle. This is always between -1 and 1.
70637.m: The values of the sine function lie between minus one and one.

70638.q: What is the value of sin(π/2)?
70638.e: π/2 corresponds to 90°. There the point (0|1) lies on the unit circle, so sin(π/2) = 1.
70638.m: The sine of 90 degrees is one.

70639.q: What is the amplitude of the function f(x) = 3·sin(x)?
70639.e: The factor in front of the sine stretches the graph in the y direction. The values lie between -3 and 3, so the amplitude is 3.
70639.m: The factor in front of the sine sets the amplitude.

70640.q: What is the period of the function f(x) = sin(2x)?
70640.e: For sin(bx) the period is 2π/b. With b = 2 that gives π; the curve oscillates twice as fast.
70640.m: A factor inside the sine shortens the period.

70641.q: Where are the zeros of the function f(x) = sin(x)?
a: At all whole-number multiples of π
70641.e: The sine is zero when the point on the unit circle lies on the x-axis, so at 0, π, 2π and so on, and the negative multiples.
70641.m: The sine function has zeros at all multiples of π.

70642.q: By how much must you shift the sine curve to the left to get the cosine curve?
70642.e: cos(x) = sin(x + π/2). So the cosine curve is the sine curve shifted π/2 to the left.
70642.m: Cosine and sine differ only by a shift of 90 degrees.

70643.q: What symmetry does the graph of the sine function have?
70643.e: sin(-x) = -sin(x). Functions with this property are symmetrical about the origin.
70643.m: The sine function is an odd function.

70644.q: The Swiss power grid has a frequency of 50 Hz. How long does one period of the sinusoidal alternating voltage last?
70644.e: The period is the reciprocal of the frequency: T = 1/50 s = 0.02 s = 20 ms.
70644.m: Period and frequency are reciprocals of each other.

70645.q: Which function is the inverse of f(x) = eˣ?
70645.e: The natural logarithm undoes the exponential function: ln(eˣ) = x. It is its inverse function.
70645.m: The natural logarithm is the inverse of e to the power of x.

70646.q: How do you get the graph of the inverse function from the graph of f?
a: By reflecting it in the line y = x
By reflecting it in the x-axis
By reflecting it in the y-axis
By reflecting it through the origin
70646.e: For the inverse function, x and y are swapped. Geometrically, that is a reflection in the line y = x.
70646.m: A function and its inverse are mirror images in the line y = x.

70647.q: Which property must a function have so that it has an inverse function?
a: Each function value occurs only once
70647.e: Only if each y value belongs to exactly one x value is the inverse unique. Such functions are called injective or invertible.
70647.m: A function can only be inverted if no y value occurs twice.

70648.q: Which function is the inverse of f(x) = x³?
70648.e: The cube root undoes cubing: ∛(x³) = x. Because x³ is strictly increasing, the function can be inverted on the whole of ℝ.
70648.m: The cube root is the inverse of cubing.

70649.q: Which of these functions is its own inverse?
70649.e: If you solve y = 1/x for x, you get x = 1/y. The graph of the hyperbola is symmetrical about the line y = x.
70649.m: A function whose graph is symmetrical about y equals x is its own inverse.

70650.q: f(2) = 7. What is the value of the inverse function at 7?
70650.e: The inverse function swaps x and y. From f(2) = 7 it follows that f⁻¹(7) = 2.
70650.m: The inverse function leads from the function value back to the starting value.

70651.q: What is the inverse of the sine function restricted to [-π/2, π/2] called?
70651.e: The arcsine arcsin(x) gives the angle for a given sine value. On a calculator the key is often labelled sin⁻¹.
70651.m: With the arcsine you find the angle for a sine value.

70652.q: Which set becomes the domain of the inverse function?
a: The set of zeros of f
70652.e: Because x and y are swapped, you can put exactly the values that f takes into f⁻¹. Domain and range swap roles.
70652.m: For the inverse function, domain and range swap roles.

70653.q: What is a zero of a function f?
a: The lowest point of the graph
An x value where f is not defined
70653.e: At a zero, the function value is zero. There the graph crosses or touches the x-axis.
70653.m: Zeros are the places where the graph meets the x-axis.

70654.q: What are the zeros of the function f(x) = x² − 9?
70654.e: From x² − 9 = 0 it follows that x² = 9, so x = 3 or x = -3. You can also factorise it as (x − 3)(x + 3).
70654.m: The equation x² equals a positive number has two solutions with opposite signs.

70655.q: What are the zeros of the function f(x) = (x − 1)(x + 5)?
70655.e: A product is zero when one factor is zero. x − 1 = 0 gives 1, x + 5 = 0 gives -5.
70655.m: A product is zero exactly when at least one factor is zero.

70656.q: How many real zeros does the function f(x) = x² + 4 have?
70656.e: Because x² is never negative, x² + 4 ≥ 4. The graph lies entirely above the x-axis.
70656.m: A parabola that lies entirely above the x-axis has no zeros.

70657.q: What are the zeros of the function f(x) = x² − 8x + 15?
70657.e: You look for two numbers with a sum of 8 and a product of 15: 3 and 5. So f(x) = (x − 3)(x − 5).
70657.m: With Vieta's theorem you can often find zeros in your head.

70658.q: What is the zero of the function f(x) = 2ˣ − 8?
70658.m: In exponential equations, you compare powers with the same base.

70659.q: What does the graph of f(x) = (x − 4)² do at its double zero x = 4?
a: It touches the x-axis without changing sign
70659.e: At x = 4, f(x) = 0, and to the left and right of it f(x) is positive. The graph only touches the x-axis.
70659.m: At a double zero, the graph touches the x-axis.

70660.q: Which method approximates a zero by repeatedly halving an interval where the sign changes?
70660.e: In the bisection method you check the sign in the middle of the interval and keep the half with the sign change. This narrows down the zero more and more.
70660.m: By repeatedly halving, you can find a zero as accurately as you like.

70661.q: What does the derivative f'(x₀) tell you geometrically?
a: The gradient of the tangent at x₀
70661.e: The derivative is the limit of the gradients of secants. It gives the gradient of the tangent to the graph at the point x₀.
70661.m: The derivative measures the instantaneous gradient of a graph.

70662.q: What is the derivative of the function f(x) = 5x²?
70662.e: By the power rule, x² becomes 2x and the factor 5 stays: 5·2x = 10x.
70662.m: Constant factors stay when you differentiate.

70663.q: Who developed differential calculus independently of Isaac Newton?
70663.e: Newton and Leibniz developed calculus independently of each other in the 17th century. The notation dy/dx comes from Leibniz.
70663.m: Newton and Leibniz are regarded as the founders of differential calculus.

70664.q: What is the derivative of the function f(x) = sin(x)?
70664.e: The gradient of the sine curve follows the shape of the cosine curve. (sin x)' = cos x.
70664.m: The derivative of sine is cosine.

70665.q: Which condition holds at a maximum or minimum of a differentiable function?
70665.e: At a turning point the graph has a horizontal tangent. Its gradient is zero, so f'(x) = 0.
70665.m: At maxima and minima the tangent is horizontal.

70666.q: What is the expression (f(x + h) − f(x))/h called?
70666.e: It gives the gradient of the secant through two points. If you let h approach zero, you get the derivative.
70666.m: The difference quotient is the average rate of change.

70667.q: What is the gradient of the graph of f(x) = x² at x = 3?
70667.e: The derivative is f'(x) = 2x. At 3 this gives f'(3) = 6.
70667.m: You get the gradient at a point by putting it into the derivative.

70668.q: What is true of a function on an interval where f'(x) > 0 everywhere?
70668.e: A positive derivative means a positive tangent gradient. So the graph rises over the whole interval.
70668.m: If the derivative is positive, the graph rises.

70669.q: How tall is an equilateral triangle with a side length of 10 cm?
70669.e: The height halves the base, so h² + 5² = 10². So h² = 75 and h = 5·√3 ≈ 8.66 cm.
70669.m: The height of an equilateral triangle is half the side times the square root of three.

70670.q: For which triangles does the equation a² + b² = c² hold, if c is the longest side?
70670.e: Pythagoras' theorem holds exactly in right-angled triangles. For other triangles you need a correction term with the angle.
70670.m: Pythagoras' theorem only holds in a right-angled triangle.

70671.q: In a right-angled triangle the hypotenuse is c = 10 cm and the segment of the hypotenuse is p = 3.6 cm. How long is the leg a by Euclid's leg theorem?
70671.e: Euclid's leg theorem says a² = c·p. So a² = 10·3.6 = 36 and a = 6 cm.
70671.m: The square of a leg equals the product of the hypotenuse and the adjacent segment of the hypotenuse.

70672.q: The height divides the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle into the segments p = 4 cm and q = 9 cm. How long is the height h?
70672.e: By Euclid's altitude theorem, h² = p·q = 4·9 = 36. So h = 6 cm.
70672.m: The square of the height equals the product of the two segments of the hypotenuse.

70673.q: A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 24 cm and 25 cm. How big is the angle opposite the 25 cm side?
70673.e: 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625 = 25². By the converse of Pythagoras' theorem the triangle is right-angled, and the right angle is opposite the longest side.
70673.m: If three sides satisfy the Pythagoras equation, the triangle is right-angled.

70674.q: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 6 cm and 8 cm. What kind of triangle is it?
70674.e: 5² + 6² = 61, but 8² = 64. Because the square of the longest side is greater than the sum of the other squares, the largest angle is greater than 90°.
70674.m: If the square of the longest side is greater than the sum of the other two squares, the triangle is obtuse.

70675.q: A rectangular garden gate is 6 m wide and 2.5 m high. How long is a diagonal brace from corner to corner?
70675.e: The brace is the hypotenuse: √(6² + 2.5²) = √(36 + 6.25) = √42.25 = 6.5 m.
70675.m: You calculate the diagonal of a rectangle with Pythagoras' theorem.

70676.q: Which people knew Pythagorean triples more than a thousand years before Pythagoras?
70676.e: The Babylonian clay tablet Plimpton 322 from the 18th century BC contains numbers belonging to Pythagorean triples. Pythagoras only lived in the 6th century BC.
70676.m: The Babylonians knew Pythagorean triples over a thousand years before Pythagoras.

70677.q: A point C lies on a circle with diameter AB. How big is the angle ACB?
70677.e: This is Thales' theorem: every angle on the diameter of a circle is a right angle.
70677.m: An angle in a semicircle is always a right angle.

70678.q: Which city did the Greek mathematician Thales, after whom the theorem is named, come from?
70678.e: Thales of Miletus lived around the 6th century BC in the Ionian city of Miletus on the west coast of Asia Minor. He is regarded as one of the first Greek philosophers.
70678.m: Thales of Miletus is regarded as one of the first Greek mathematicians and philosophers.

70679.q: In triangle ABC, AB is a diameter of a circle and C lies on the circle. The angle at A is 35°. How big is the angle at B?
70679.e: By Thales, the angle at C is 90°. The angles add up to 180°, so 180° − 90° − 35° = 55°.
70679.m: In a Thales triangle, the two acute angles add up to 90°.

70680.q: Where is the centre of the circumcircle of a right-angled triangle?
a: at the midpoint of the hypotenuse
at the vertex of the right angle
at the centroid of the triangle
70680.e: By the converse of Thales' theorem, the right-angled corner lies on the circle over the hypotenuse. This circle is the circumcircle, and its centre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse.
70680.m: The circumcircle of a right-angled triangle is the Thales circle over the hypotenuse.

70681.q: You place the right-angled corner of a set square on the edge of a round plate and mark where its two sides cross the edge. What is the line joining these two points?
70681.e: By the converse of Thales' theorem, every right angle whose vertex lies on the circle stands on a diameter. With two such diameters, their intersection gives you the centre of the plate.
70681.m: With a right angle on the edge of a circle you can find a diameter.

70682.q: What is the Thales circle often used for in constructions with compasses and ruler?
a: for tangents from an outside point to a circle
70682.e: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact. The points of contact therefore lie on the Thales circle over the line from the outside point to the centre of the circle.
70682.m: With the Thales circle you can find where tangents touch a circle.

70683.q: A point C lies inside the circle with diameter AB, but not on AB. How big is the angle ACB?
70683.e: On the circle the angle is exactly 90°. If C moves inwards, closer to the line AB, the angle gets bigger, so it is obtuse.
70683.m: Inside the Thales circle, the angle on the diameter is obtuse.

70684.q: Which theorem of circle geometry generalises Thales' theorem to any chord?
70684.e: The inscribed angle theorem says that all inscribed angles on the same chord are equal. If the chord is a diameter, you get Thales' theorem with 90°.
70684.m: Thales' theorem is a special case of the inscribed angle theorem.

70685.q: Two rays start from Z and are cut by two parallel lines. ZA = 4 cm, ZA' = 10 cm and ZB = 6 cm. How long is ZB'?
70685.e: By the first intercept theorem, ZA' : ZA = ZB' : ZB. So ZB' = 6 · 10 : 4 = 15 cm.
70685.m: The sections on the rays are in the same ratio.

70686.q: Two parallel lines cut two rays from Z. ZA = 3 cm, ZA' = 9 cm and the parallel segment AB = 5 cm. How long is A'B'?
70686.e: By the second intercept theorem, A'B' : AB = ZA' : ZA = 3. So A'B' = 3 · 5 = 15 cm.
70686.m: The parallel segments are in the same ratio as the matching sections of the rays from the vertex.

70687.q: Which condition must be met for the intercept theorems to hold?
a: The rays are the same length.
The angle at the vertex is 45°.
70687.e: The intercept theorems only hold if the two lines cutting the rays are parallel to each other. Otherwise the ratios are wrong.
70687.m: Without parallel lines, the intercept theorems do not hold.

70688.q: A 2 m pole casts a shadow 1.5 m long. At the same time a tree casts a shadow 12 m long. How tall is the tree?
70688.e: The sun's rays are parallel, so height : shadow is the same for both. 2 : 1.5 = h : 12 gives h = 16 m.
70688.m: With shadow lengths and the intercept theorem you can measure heights indirectly.

70689.q: According to tradition, how did Thales measure the height of an Egyptian pyramid?
a: with the shadow of a stick
with a plumb line from the top
by the position of the stars
70689.e: Thales is said to have compared the pyramid's shadow with the shadow of an upright stick. Because the sun's rays are parallel, the height follows from the same ratio.
70689.m: With shadow ratios you can find heights you cannot reach.

70690.q: Which classic construction with compasses and ruler is based directly on the intercept theorem?
a: dividing a line segment into equal parts
70690.e: You mark off equal lengths on a helper ray and draw parallels to the connecting line. By the intercept theorem these divide the segment into equal parts.
70690.m: With parallels to a helper ray you can divide any line segment into equal parts.

70691.q: In an X-shaped figure, the vertex Z lies between the parallel lines. ZA = 2 cm, ZA' = 5 cm and AB = 3 cm. How long is the opposite parallel segment A'B'?
70691.e: In the X figure too, A'B' : AB = ZA' : ZA. So A'B' = 3 · 5 : 2 = 7.5 cm.
70691.m: The intercept theorems also hold when the lines cross between the parallels.

70692.q: A 30 m tower stands 100 m in front of a pinhole camera. The image forms 10 cm behind the hole. How tall is the image?
70692.e: The light rays cross in the hole, forming an X figure. Image height = 30 m · 0.1 m : 100 m = 0.03 m = 3 cm.
70692.m: A pinhole camera makes smaller images according to the intercept theorem.

70693.q: All sides of a shape are enlarged by a factor of 3. How does its area change?
70693.e: In an enlargement with scale factor k, the area grows by k². Here 3² = 9.
70693.m: The areas of similar shapes are in the ratio of the squares of their side ratios.

70694.q: A model is built on a scale of 1 : 10. How does its volume compare with the original?
70694.e: For similar solids, the volume grows with the cube of the length factor. 10³ = 1000.
70694.m: The volumes of similar solids are in the ratio of the cube of their length ratio.

70695.q: On the Swiss national map at 1 : 25 000, two places are 6 cm apart. How far apart are they as the crow flies in reality?
70695.m: At a scale of 1 to 25 000, one centimetre on the map is 250 metres.

70696.q: What real area does 1 cm² on a map at a scale of 1 : 50 000 correspond to?
70696.e: 1 cm corresponds to 500 m. So 1 cm² corresponds to an area of 500 m · 500 m = 250 000 m² = 0.25 km².
70696.m: For areas on maps, you have to square the scale.

70697.q: Which condition is enough to be sure two triangles are similar?
a: One side is the same length.
70697.e: If two angles are equal, the third is equal too because of the angle sum. Then the triangles are similar.
70697.m: Two triangles with two equal angles are similar.

70698.q: Which transformation is an enlargement with scale factor k = -1?
70698.e: With k = -1, each point is mapped to the opposite side of the centre at the same distance. That is exactly a point reflection in the centre.
70698.m: An enlargement with factor minus one is a point reflection.

70699.q: What ratio of sides do A-series paper sizes such as A4 have, so that halved sheets stay similar?
70699.e: If you halve a rectangle with the ratio 1 : √2 along its long side, you again get the ratio 1 : √2. So all A sizes are similar to each other.
70699.m: All A-series sheets are similar rectangles.

70700.q: A 10 cm × 15 cm photo is enlarged without distortion so that the short side is 20 cm. How long will the long side be?
70700.e: In a similar enlargement all lengths are multiplied by the same factor. The factor is 20 : 10 = 2, so 15 · 2 = 30 cm.
70700.m: In similar shapes, all lengths are stretched by the same factor.

70701.q: What is the exact value of cos(30°)?
70701.e: In half an equilateral triangle with side 2, the side adjacent to 30° is the height √3. cos(30°) = √3 / 2 ≈ 0.866.
70701.m: The cosine of 30 degrees is half the square root of three.

70702.q: How is the tangent of an acute angle defined in a right-angled triangle?
70702.e: The tangent is the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side. It also equals sin(α) : cos(α).
70702.m: The tangent compares the opposite side with the adjacent side.

70703.q: A road has a 12 % gradient. Roughly what is its angle of slope?
70703.e: 12 % means 12 m of height over 100 m horizontally, so tan(α) = 0.12. From this α = arctan(0.12) ≈ 6.8°.
70703.m: The gradient in per cent is the tangent of the angle of slope times a hundred.

70704.q: The Stoos funicular in the canton of Schwyz climbs a maximum gradient of 110 %. Roughly what angle is that?
70704.e: 110 % means tan(α) = 1.1. This gives α = arctan(1.1) ≈ 47.7°. So a gradient over 100 % is steeper than 45°.
70704.m: A gradient of one hundred per cent equals an angle of 45 degrees.

70705.q: In a triangle, a = 10 cm, α = 30° and β = 45°. How long is b by the sine rule?
70705.e: By the sine rule, b = a · sin(β) : sin(α) = 10 · 0.7071 : 0.5 ≈ 14.1 cm.
70705.m: In the sine rule, the sides are in the same ratio as the sines of the opposite angles.

70706.q: In a triangle, a = 5 cm, b = 7 cm and the angle between them γ = 60°. How long is c?
70706.m: With the cosine rule you work out the third side from two sides and the angle between them.

70707.q: You stand 50 m from a tower and see the top at an angle of elevation of 30° (ignoring eye height). How tall is the tower?
