73139.e: Three- and four-year apprenticeships end with the Federal VET Diploma (EFZ). The EBA only exists after two-year programmes.
73139.m: After a three- or four-year apprenticeship you get an EFZ.

73140.q: Who must the training company inform immediately if an apprenticeship contract is ended early?
73140.e: According to the Vocational Training Act (Article 14), an early termination must be reported to the cantonal authority without delay.
73140.m: An ended apprenticeship must be reported to the canton.

73141.q: In which month do most apprenticeships in Switzerland start?
73141.e: Most apprenticeships start in summer, usually in August, together with the new school year at the vocational school.

73142.q: Which office must approve an apprenticeship contract?
73142.e: The training company submits the contract to the canton. The cantonal vocational training office checks and approves it.
73142.m: The canton approves every apprenticeship contract.

73143.q: What is the probation period at the start of an apprenticeship for?
a: Both sides check whether it works
You don't have to work yet
73143.e: During the probation period, the apprentice and the company find out whether the job and working together suit them. It usually lasts three months.
73143.m: In the probation period both sides check whether it works.

73144.q: Can the probation period of an apprenticeship be extended?
a: Yes, in exceptional cases with the canton's approval
Yes, for as long as you like
73144.e: If necessary, the probation period can be extended with the canton's approval, to a maximum of six months.
73144.m: The probation period can be extended in exceptional cases.

73145.q: What applies if notice is given during the probation period of an apprenticeship?
a: You can leave at short notice
You cannot give notice at all
You have to wait a year
Only the company may give notice
73145.e: During the probation period, both sides can give notice with a short period of seven days. Later, there must be important reasons.
73145.m: During the probation period, giving notice is easy.

73146.q: When may an apprenticeship contract be ended early after the probation period?
a: At any time without a reason
Never, not even in an emergency
73146.e: After the probation period, ending it without notice is only possible for important reasons, for example if the company can no longer provide training.
73146.m: After the probation period, you need important reasons to end an apprenticeship.

73147.q: Among other things, what must be written in the apprenticeship contract?
73147.e: The apprenticeship contract sets out at least the type and length of training, wages, probation period, working hours and holidays.
73147.m: The apprenticeship contract states wages, working hours and holidays.

73148.q: Who makes an apprenticeship contract with each other?
a: The training company and the apprentice
The parents and the vocational school
The federal government and the municipality
73148.e: The parties to the contract are the training company and the apprentice. The canton only approves the contract.
73148.m: The training company and the apprentice make the apprenticeship contract.

73149.q: About how many days a week do apprentices go to vocational school?
73149.e: Apprentices usually go to school one or two days a week. The rest of the time they work at the training company.
73149.m: Apprentices spend about one to two days a week at vocational school.

73150.q: What do compulsory lessons at vocational school cost apprentices?
73150.e: According to the Vocational Training Act (Article 22), compulsory lessons at vocational schools are free of charge.
73150.m: Compulsory lessons at vocational school are free.

73151.q: What do you learn in general education lessons at vocational school?
a: Topics such as law, politics and language
Only the theory of your own job
73151.e: General education lessons (ABU) cover topics from society, law, politics, the economy and language. You learn the theory of your job in vocational subject lessons.
73151.m: In ABU you learn things you need for everyday life and society.

73152.q: Besides vocational subjects and general education, which subject is compulsory at vocational school?
73152.e: In Switzerland, sport lessons are also required in basic vocational education.
73152.m: Vocational school also has compulsory sport lessons.

73153.q: Do lessons at vocational school count as working time for apprentices?
a: Yes, with no deduction from wages
73153.e: The training company must give apprentices time off for compulsory lessons, with no deduction from their wages (Article 345a of the Code of Obligations).
73153.m: School time counts as working time for apprentices.

73154.q: What does the vocational school offer apprentices who have learning difficulties?
73154.e: Vocational schools offer support courses for apprentices who are struggling and optional courses for those who are especially interested.
73154.m: If you struggle, you can take support courses at vocational school.

73155.q: What do apprentices learn in vocational subject lessons at vocational school?
a: The theoretical knowledge of their job
73155.e: In vocational subject lessons, apprentices learn the theory of their job, for example materials or job-related maths.
73155.m: In vocational subject lessons you learn the theory of your own job.

73156.q: What are the courses called that apprentices with good results can also choose at vocational school?
73156.e: Optional courses are voluntary extras, such as languages. The company must allow them with no deduction from wages, as long as the apprentice's results are good.
73156.m: Optional courses are voluntary extra courses at vocational school.

73157.q: Who pays the costs of the inter-company courses?
73157.e: According to the Vocational Training Ordinance, the training company bears the costs. The course costs may not be passed on to apprentices.
73157.m: The training company pays for inter-company courses, not the apprentices.

73158.q: Is attending the inter-company courses voluntary for apprentices?
73158.e: Attending the üK is compulsory for apprentices if the training regulations for the job provide for such courses.

73159.q: Who usually organises the inter-company courses?
73159.e: The professional associations, known as organisations of the world of work (OdA), are usually responsible.
73159.m: Inter-company courses are usually organised by the professional associations.

73160.q: Together with the federal government and the cantons, who decides what is learned in an apprenticeship?
73160.e: The professional associations, also called organisations of the world of work (OdA), know their trade best. That is why they help decide what an apprenticeship covers.
73160.m: The professional associations help decide what an apprenticeship covers.

73161.q: How many places of learning does basic vocational education in Switzerland have?
73161.e: The three places of learning are the training company, the vocational school and the inter-company courses.
73161.m: An apprenticeship takes place at three places of learning.

73162.q: Where do the inter-company courses (üK) usually take place?
a: At a professional association's training centre
73162.e: The üK usually take place in the professional associations' own training centres. There are workshops and materials there for all apprentices in a trade.
73162.m: The üK usually take place in the professional associations' training centres.

73163.q: Why are inter-company courses especially useful for apprentices in small companies?
a: They practise tasks there that rarely come up at their own company
They don't have to go to school there
73163.e: Not every company can show all the basic techniques of a trade. In the üK, all apprentices learn the same basics.
73163.m: In the üK all apprentices learn the same basic skills of their trade.

73164.q: Which course in the triangle of learning places links school knowledge and company practice with targeted exercises?
73164.e: The üK add to practice at the company and theory at school with targeted practice of basic skills.
73164.m: The inter-company course complements the company and the vocational school.

a: Extended general education on top of the apprenticeship
The final exam of primary school
Another word for the probation period
73165.e: With the vocational baccalaureate you take extra lessons alongside your apprenticeship, for example in languages and maths. It opens the way to a university of applied sciences.
73165.m: The vocational baccalaureate adds more general education to the apprenticeship.

73166.q: Which vocational baccalaureate stream best suits a commercial apprenticeship?
73166.e: People doing a commercial apprenticeship (KV) usually choose the business and services stream, with subjects such as finance and accounting.
73166.m: The business and services stream suits a commercial apprenticeship.

73167.q: Which vocational baccalaureate stream best suits an apprenticeship as a polymechanic?
73167.e: The technology, architecture, life sciences stream, focusing on maths and science, is meant for technical jobs.
73167.m: Technical apprentices often choose the technology, architecture, life sciences stream.

73168.q: How long does the vocational baccalaureate take full-time after the apprenticeship?
73168.e: If you do the vocational baccalaureate after the EFZ, you take about one year of full-time lessons or about two years part-time alongside work.
73168.m: After the apprenticeship, the full-time vocational baccalaureate takes about a year.

73169.q: Which qualification do you need in addition to the vocational baccalaureate certificate for the vocational baccalaureate to be valid?
73169.e: The vocational baccalaureate combines the Federal VET Diploma (EFZ) with extended general education.
73169.m: The vocational baccalaureate always goes with an EFZ.

73170.q: Can you go to university later with a vocational baccalaureate?
73170.e: With the Passerelle, an extra year with an exam, people with a vocational baccalaureate can go to universities and ETH.
73170.m: The Passerelle leads from the vocational baccalaureate to university.

73171.q: Which subject is one of the core subjects of the vocational baccalaureate?
73171.e: Core subjects include the first national language, the second national language, a third language and maths.
73171.m: Maths is a core subject of the vocational baccalaureate.

73172.q: What is the option called where you do the vocational baccalaureate during your apprenticeship?
73172.e: With the vocational baccalaureate alongside the apprenticeship (BM 1), you spend more days at school during the apprenticeship. BM 2 only comes after the EFZ.
73172.m: You can do the vocational baccalaureate during or after the apprenticeship.

73173.q: Where can you NOT study directly with a vocational baccalaureate and no extra exam?
a: At a university of applied sciences in a matching field
At a college of higher education
73173.e: The vocational baccalaureate opens the doors to universities of applied sciences. For universities or ETH you also need supplementary exams.
73173.m: The vocational baccalaureate alone does not get you into a university.

73174.q: What is the final qualification of a Gymnasium (academic secondary school) in Switzerland called?
73174.e: The Gymnasium ends with the academic baccalaureate, also called the Matura.
73174.m: The Gymnasium ends with the Matura.

73175.q: What does the academic baccalaureate (Matura) allow you to do?
a: Only do an apprenticeship as a cook
Only do an apprenticeship in retail
73175.e: With the academic baccalaureate you can usually go to universities and ETH without an entrance exam. For medicine there is sometimes an aptitude test.
73175.m: The Matura opens the way to universities and ETH.

73176.q: What is the minimum length of the route to the academic baccalaureate?
73176.e: The education leading to the Matura lasts at least four years. Sometimes one year of lower secondary school counts towards it.
73176.m: The Gymnasium course lasts at least four years.

73177.q: Which written piece of work must every student at a Gymnasium write on their own?
73177.e: The Matura project is a larger independent piece of work on a topic you choose yourself, and you present it.
73177.m: At the Gymnasium you write a Matura project.

73178.q: What is the subject called that lets you choose your own focus at the Gymnasium?
73178.e: As your main focus subject you choose, for example, Latin, biology and chemistry, or economics and law.
73178.m: At the Gymnasium you choose a main focus subject.

73179.q: What is the Gymnasium called that in some cantons starts straight after year 6 of primary school?
73179.e: You join the long-course Gymnasium after primary school. You only move to the short-course Gymnasium from lower secondary school.
73179.m: The long-course Gymnasium starts straight after primary school.

73180.q: Who runs the Gymnasiums in Switzerland?
73180.e: Gymnasiums are the responsibility of the cantons. So that a Matura is valid throughout Switzerland, the Confederation and the cantons recognise it together.

73181.q: What is a university of applied sciences?
a: A higher education institution with a strong practical focus
73181.e: At universities of applied sciences you study in a practical way, for example engineering, business or social work. With an academic Matura you usually need a year of work placement first.
73181.m: Universities of applied sciences are colleges with lots of practice.

73182.q: How long does the upper secondary specialised school (FMS) take until the FMS certificate?
73182.e: The FMS lasts three years and is part of upper secondary education.
73182.m: The upper secondary specialised school lasts three years.

73183.q: What is the qualification after three years at an upper secondary specialised school called?
73183.e: After three years you receive the FMS certificate, often called the FMS diploma.
73183.m: After the FMS you receive the FMS certificate.

73184.q: Which additional qualification can you gain in about one more year after the FMS?
73184.e: After the FMS certificate, the specialised baccalaureate takes about one year with lessons and a work placement.
73184.m: After the FMS you can do the specialised baccalaureate.

73185.q: Where does the specialised baccalaureate in education lead directly?
a: To a university of teacher education
73185.e: With the specialised baccalaureate in education you can study at a university of teacher education, for example to become a primary school teacher.
73185.m: The specialised baccalaureate in education leads to a university of teacher education.

73186.q: Which field is a typical specialisation at an upper secondary specialised school?
73186.e: Typical FMS specialisations are health, social work, education, communication, design and music.
73186.m: Health is a typical FMS specialisation.

73187.q: What kind of school is the upper secondary specialised school (FMS)?
a: An upper secondary school like the Gymnasium
73187.e: The FMS is an upper secondary school after compulsory schooling. It prepares students especially for jobs in health, social work and education.
73187.m: The upper secondary specialised school is an upper secondary school.

73188.q: What could you do after gaining the FMS certificate, for example?
a: Attend a college of higher education
73188.e: The FMS certificate lets you enter a college of higher education, for example in nursing. For universities you need a Matura.
73188.m: With the FMS certificate you can go to a college of higher education.

73189.q: What is compulsory at the upper secondary specialised school in all cantons?
a: A work placement in your field
73189.e: In all cantons, a work placement related to your field is part of the FMS.
73189.m: A work placement is part of the upper secondary specialised school.

73190.q: When do young people in Switzerland usually choose a path of education for the first time?
a: Towards the end of compulsory school
73190.e: Towards the end of compulsory school you choose an apprenticeship, an upper secondary school or a bridging programme. This transition is also called interface I.
73190.m: At the end of school you choose your next path of education.

73191.q: Who is the motivation semester (SEMO) meant for?
a: Young people without an apprenticeship place after school
73191.e: The motivation semester helps young people who have not found an apprenticeship place after school. It combines work assignments, lessons and application training.
73191.m: SEMO helps young people without an apprenticeship place.

73192.q: What help do young people with many difficulties get on their way into an apprenticeship?
a: They have to pay a fine
They have to finish school abroad
73192.e: In vocational training case management, a specialist coordinates the support. The aim is for the young people to complete an education.
73192.m: If you have big difficulties, a specialist will support you.

73193.q: What goal do the Confederation and the cantons have for the education of young people?
a: Almost everyone should gain a qualification after school
Everyone should study at a university
Nobody should do an apprenticeship any more
School should only last six years
73193.e: The Confederation and the cantons want 95 per cent of 25-year-olds to have completed an apprenticeship or upper secondary school. Bridging programmes help with this.
73193.m: Almost all young people should complete an education.

73194.q: How long does a bridging programme usually last?
73194.e: Most bridging programmes last about one school year.
73194.m: A bridging programme usually lasts about one year.

73195.q: After how many years of compulsory school, counting kindergarten, does a bridging programme usually start?
73195.e: Under HarmoS, compulsory school including two years of kindergarten lasts eleven years. Then comes an apprenticeship, an upper secondary school or a bridging programme.
73195.m: Compulsory school including kindergarten lasts eleven years.

73196.q: What is it called when an experienced person voluntarily supports a young person looking for an apprenticeship?
73196.e: In mentoring, an experienced person, often a volunteer, supports young people, for example with applications and contacts with companies.
73196.m: In mentoring, an experienced person supports you in finding an apprenticeship.

73197.q: Which qualification is the goal after a bridging programme?
73197.e: Bridging programmes are meant to help you start an apprenticeship or upper secondary school, in other words upper secondary education.
73197.m: Bridging programmes lead to upper secondary education.

73198.q: What does “dual” mean in the dual education system?
a: Training in two places: company and school
Two apprenticeships at the same time
73198.e: Dual means two-track: apprentices work in a company and learn theory at vocational school.
73198.m: In the dual system you learn at work and at school.

73199.q: Who works closely together on apprenticeships in Switzerland?
a: The Confederation, the cantons and businesses
73199.e: The Confederation, the cantons and businesses with their professional associations run vocational education together. This is called a partnership.
73199.m: The Confederation, cantons and businesses run vocational education together.

73200.q: Is an EFZ from the canton of Bern also valid in the canton of Geneva?
a: No, only in its own canton
73200.e: Vocational education is regulated by the Confederation for the whole of Switzerland. That is why the Federal VET Diploma is worth the same in all cantons.
73200.m: An EFZ is valid throughout Switzerland.

73201.q: Which of Switzerland's neighbouring countries also have a strong dual apprenticeship system?
73201.e: Besides Switzerland, Germany and Austria in particular have a strong tradition of dual apprenticeships.
73201.m: Germany and Austria also have dual apprenticeships.

73202.q: Which advantage does the dual system show particularly clearly in Switzerland?
73202.e: Because apprentices gain experience of the job market early, youth unemployment in Switzerland is low compared with other countries.
73202.m: The dual system helps keep youth unemployment low.

73203.q: Who has a major say in what you learn in an apprenticeship?
73203.e: Businesses know what is needed in the job. That is why professional associations help decide what is taught in an apprenticeship.
73203.m: Professional associations help decide what is taught in an apprenticeship.

73204.q: Why do many companies train apprentices?
a: The law forces all companies to
The Confederation pays all their wages
73204.e: Companies train their own skilled workers of tomorrow. Because apprentices also do productive work, training pays off financially for most companies too.
73204.m: For most training companies, training apprentices pays off.

73205.q: Can any company simply train apprentices?
a: No, the canton must allow it
Only with permission from the municipality
73205.e: The canton checks whether a company meets the requirements and then grants a training licence.
73205.m: A training company needs a licence from the canton.

73206.q: Which motto describes how open the Swiss education system is to changing paths?
a: No qualification without a next step
Once an apprentice, always an apprentice
Only those with a Matura get further
73206.e: In Switzerland, every qualification should open the way to further education.
73206.m: In the Swiss education system there should be no qualification without a next step.

73207.q: Can adults without an apprenticeship gain a vocational qualification later?
73207.e: Adults with enough work experience, usually five years, can catch up on an EFZ or EBA.
73207.m: Adults can also catch up on a vocational qualification.

73208.q: What is often possible after a good EBA qualification?
a: Taking the professional exam without experience
Going straight into the last year of Gymnasium
73208.e: People with an EBA can often gain an EFZ in the same field through a shortened apprenticeship.
73208.m: After the EBA you can often do a shortened EFZ.

73209.q: What can people with an academic Matura do if they want to learn a trade?
73209.e: Some industries offer shortened apprenticeships for Matura holders, for example in IT or commerce.
73209.m: With a Matura you can also do a shortened apprenticeship.

73210.q: Can you continue your education after an apprenticeship?
a: Yes, for example with a professional exam
No, it ends after the apprenticeship
73210.e: After the apprenticeship and some work experience you can, for example, take a professional exam and receive the Federal Diploma of Higher Education.
73210.m: Learning goes on after the apprenticeship.

73211.q: How can you still get into ETH Zurich without a Matura?
a: With a good primary school report
73211.e: ETH offers an entrance exam for people without a recognised Matura certificate.
73211.m: Without a Matura, an entrance exam leads to ETH.

73212.q: What does permeability mean in the education system?
a: You can switch between paths of education
You can retake any exam as often as you like
73212.e: A permeable system allows changes, for example from an apprenticeship to a university or from the Gymnasium to an apprenticeship.
73212.m: Permeability means you can change your path of education.

73213.q: Which qualification after an apprenticeship leads directly to higher vocational education?
73213.e: The EFZ is the basis for professional exams, advanced professional exams and colleges of higher education.
73213.m: With the EFZ, higher vocational education is open to you.

73214.q: Which apprenticeship had the most new contracts in Switzerland in 2020?
73214.e: The commercial apprenticeship has been by far the most common apprenticeship in Switzerland for years. According to the Federal Statistical Office, over 12,000 young people started a commercial apprenticeship in 2020.
73214.m: The commercial apprenticeship is the most common apprenticeship in Switzerland.

73215.q: Which health job is one of the most common apprenticeships in Switzerland?
73215.e: In 2020, almost 5,000 young people started the apprenticeship as a healthcare assistant (FaGe). This makes it one of the most popular apprenticeships.
73215.m: FaGe is one of the most common apprenticeships in Switzerland.

73216.q: What does the abbreviation FaBe stand for?
73216.e: Social care workers work, for example, in nurseries, care homes for the elderly or with people with disabilities.

73217.q: What is the two-year EBA training in health and social care called?
a: Health and social care assistant EBA
73217.e: Health and social care assistants (AGS) help people in everyday life, for example in care homes. The training lasts two years and ends with the EBA.
73217.m: AGS is the two-year EBA apprenticeship in health and social care.

73218.q: What is the apprenticeship with an EFZ for selling and advising in shops called?
73218.e: Retail specialists advise customers and manage goods. It is one of the most common apprenticeships in Switzerland.
73218.m: If you sell and advise in a shop, you train as a retail specialist.

73219.q: Which apprenticeship combines IT, multimedia and marketing?
73219.e: Mediamaticians design websites and videos, for example, look after IT equipment and help with marketing. The apprenticeship lasts four years.
73219.m: Mediamaticians combine IT, multimedia and marketing.

73220.q: How long does the apprenticeship as an electrician EFZ take?
73220.e: Electricians lay cables and install switches, sockets and systems. Their training lasts four years.
73220.m: The electrician's apprenticeship lasts four years.

73221.q: What is the two-year EBA training in agriculture called?
73221.e: Agricultural assistants help on farms and in vegetable or fruit businesses. After the EBA they can often go on to a shortened EFZ apprenticeship.
73221.m: Agricultural assistant is the two-year apprenticeship in agriculture.

73222.q: What support are apprentices in an EBA apprenticeship entitled to if they have learning difficulties?
a: Higher pay than in the EFZ
73222.e: The Vocational Education Act (Art. 18 BBG) provides expert individual support for apprentices in two-year training courses when needed.
73222.m: EBA apprentices can receive individual support.

73223.q: Up to what age are apprentices treated as young people with special protection under employment law?
73223.e: Youth employment protection applies until your 18th birthday, for example with limits on night and Sunday work.
73223.m: Youth employment protection applies up to 18.

73224.q: What must the training company issue at the end of the apprenticeship?
73224.e: Under Art. 346a of the Code of Obligations, the employer issues a reference about the training at the end of the apprenticeship.
73224.m: At the end of your apprenticeship the company gives you a reference.

73225.q: What duty do apprentices have towards their training company?
73225.e: Apprentices must do everything they can to reach the training goal, follow instructions and work carefully (Art. 345 Code of Obligations).
73225.m: Apprentices follow instructions and work carefully.

73226.q: Apprentices lead a youth camp during the holidays. How much extra time off can they take for this each year?
73226.e: Anyone up to the age of 30 who helps with youth work unpaid, for example as a camp leader, can take up to one week of youth leave per year.
73226.m: For youth work you get up to one week of youth leave per year.

73227.q: Is apprentices' pay set by law in Switzerland?
a: No, there are only recommendations from the industries
Yes, it is the same as for adults
73227.e: There is no legal minimum wage for apprentices. Many professional associations give pay recommendations.
73227.m: Apprentice pay is based on industry recommendations.

73228.q: What must apprentices keep regularly at the company to record their learning?
73228.e: In the learning log, apprentices record what they have learned. The trainer checks it.

73229.q: What is the document called in which the training company regularly records the apprentice's progress?
73229.e: In the training report, the company regularly records, usually each semester, how the apprentice is developing.
73229.m: The training report is used to discuss progress regularly.

73230.q: Is night work generally allowed for apprentices under 18?
73230.e: Night work is generally forbidden for young people under 18. There are exceptions only for certain jobs where it is needed for the training, for example in a bakery.
73230.m: Young people are generally not allowed to work at night.

73231.q: In which law is the individual employment contract mainly regulated in Switzerland?
73231.e: The individual employment contract is regulated in Articles 319 ff. of the Code of Obligations (CO). The CO is the fifth part of the Civil Code but is cited as a law of its own.
73231.m: The rules on employment contracts are in the Code of Obligations from Article 319.

73232.q: What form does the CO basically require for an ordinary permanent employment contract?
73232.e: Under Art. 320 CO, an employment contract basically needs no particular form. It can also be made verbally or even tacitly, for example when someone accepts work for pay.
73232.m: An employment contract is valid even without a signature, unless the law requires otherwise.

73233.q: Which contract in working life must, according to the CO, always be made in writing?
a: The contract of a temporary helper
The contract for a holiday job
73233.e: Art. 344a CO requires the apprenticeship contract to be in writing. It must also be approved by the cantonal authority.
73233.m: An apprenticeship contract always has to be in writing.

73234.q: Which two main duties are set against each other in an employment contract?
a: Purchase price and delivery of goods
73234.e: According to Art. 319 CO, the employee agrees to work in the employer's service and the employer to pay a wage. Being subject to the employer's instructions is typical.
73234.m: In an employment contract, work is exchanged for wages.

73235.q: How does a fixed-term employment contract end if nothing else has been agreed?
a: Without notice when the time runs out
Through notice with a three-month period
73235.e: Under Art. 334 CO, a fixed-term employment relationship ends without notice on the agreed date. If it then continues tacitly, it counts as permanent.
73235.m: A fixed-term contract ends by itself on the agreed day.

73236.q: What wage supplement applies to overtime under the CO if nothing else has been agreed in writing?
73236.e: Art. 321c CO requires the normal wage plus a quarter for overtime, so a 25 per cent supplement. With the employee's agreement, time off of the same length can be given instead.
73236.m: Without another agreement, overtime is paid with a quarter extra.

73237.q: For how long at least must an employer continue to pay wages in the first year of service if an employee is ill through no fault of their own?
73237.e: Art. 324a CO provides for at least three weeks of continued pay in the first year of service, if the employment has lasted more than three months or was entered into for longer. After that a suitably longer period applies, often set by the Bern, Basel or Zurich scale.
73237.m: In the first year of service you get at least three weeks' pay if you are ill.

73238.q: What does the CO require for a non-competition clause to be valid after employment ends?
a: It must be agreed in writing
It must be in the commercial register
It must be approved by a court
73238.e: Under Art. 340 CO, a non-competition clause is only valid if it was agreed in writing and the person had insight into the customer base or trade secrets. Except in special circumstances it may last at most three years.
73238.m: A non-competition clause only applies if it was agreed in writing.

73239.q: What maximum weekly working time applies under the Labour Act to office staff and industrial companies?
73239.e: Art. 9 of the Labour Act sets 45 hours for industrial companies, office staff, technical employees and sales staff in large companies. For all other employees it is 50 hours.
73239.m: For office work the legal maximum is 45 hours a week.

73240.q: Which period counts as night work under the Labour Act?
73240.e: Under Art. 10 of the Labour Act, day and evening work runs from 6 am to 11 pm. Work between 11 pm and 6 am is night work and basically needs a permit.
73240.m: Night work begins at 11 pm and ends at 6 am.

73241.q: Under the Labour Act, how long must the break be at least if someone works more than 7 hours a day?
73241.e: Art. 15 of the Labour Act requires a quarter of an hour's break for more than 5.5 hours, half an hour for more than 7 hours and one hour for more than 9 hours of work.
73241.m: Anyone working more than seven hours is entitled to a half-hour break.

73242.q: Under the Labour Act, how long must the daily rest period for adult employees last at least?
73242.e: Art. 15a of the Labour Act requires a daily rest period of at least eleven consecutive hours. Under certain conditions it may be cut to eight hours once a week.
73242.m: There are usually at least eleven hours of rest between two working days.

73243.q: What wage supplement does the Labour Act require for temporary Sunday work?
73243.e: Under Art. 19 of the Labour Act, employees get a 50 per cent wage supplement for temporary Sunday work. For temporary night work, by contrast, the supplement is 25 per cent.
73243.m: Temporary Sunday work is paid with a fifty per cent supplement.

73244.q: Which public holiday is treated like a Sunday by federal law throughout Switzerland?
73244.e: The Federal Constitution declares the national holiday on 1 August a paid public holiday with no work. The cantons set other public holidays and can treat up to eight of them like Sundays.
73244.m: The national holiday on 1 August is a paid public holiday everywhere in Switzerland.

73245.q: According to Ordinance 1 to the Labour Act, what must employers basically keep ready for inspections?
a: The doctor's certificates of all families
73245.e: Under Art. 73 of Ordinance 1, records of the hours worked, including breaks, must be kept. For certain groups simplified recording, or under strict conditions none at all, is possible.
73245.m: Hours worked must usually be recorded.

73246.q: Under the Labour Act, how many hours of extra overtime are usually allowed per person per day at most?
73246.e: Art. 12 of the Labour Act limits this extra time to two hours a day, except on working days off or in emergencies. With a 45-hour maximum week, at most 170 hours per year are allowed.
73246.m: More than two hours of extra overtime per day is usually not allowed.

73247.q: How many weeks' holiday per year of service are adult employees entitled to at least under the CO?
73247.e: Art. 329a CO guarantees at least four weeks' holiday per year of service. Employment contracts or collective agreements may provide more, but never less.
73247.m: Adults in Switzerland are entitled to at least four weeks' holiday.

73248.q: Up to what age are employees entitled to at least five weeks' holiday under the CO?
73248.e: According to Art. 329a CO, employees get at least five weeks' holiday until the age of 20. This mainly affects apprentices.
73248.m: Anyone not yet 20 has at least five weeks' holiday.

73249.q: Under the CO, how many weeks of holiday must at least be taken in one go?
73249.e: Under Art. 329c CO, at least two weeks of holiday must be taken together so that real rest is possible. The other holiday days may be spread out.
73249.m: By law, at least two weeks of holiday are taken in one go.

73250.q: Under the CO, who basically decides when holidays are taken?
a: The employer, taking the employee's wishes into account
73250.e: Art. 329c CO gives the employer the right to set the dates. However, the employer must take the employees' wishes into account as far as the business allows.
73250.m: The employer sets the holidays but considers the staff's wishes.

73251.q: May holidays be replaced by money while the employment is still running?
a: Yes, at any time on request
Yes, but only in the first year of service
Yes, if the holidays are too short
73251.e: Art. 329d CO forbids paying money instead of holidays while the employment lasts. Holidays are for rest and should actually be taken.
73251.m: Holidays should be taken, not paid out.

73252.q: With an hourly wage and four weeks' holiday, what holiday supplement is usually added to the wage?
73252.e: With four weeks' holiday you work 48 of 52 weeks. The supplement is therefore 4 divided by 48, about 8.33 per cent of the wage.
73252.m: With an hourly wage, four weeks' holiday equals a supplement of 8.33 per cent.

73253.q: What does the CO say about so-called youth leave for youth work outside school?
a: Up to the age of 30, up to one week per year
Up to the age of 20, two weeks per year
Three days a month for everyone
Only for apprentices, one day per week
73253.e: Art. 329e CO grants up to one working week a year, until the age of 30, for leading or supervising activities in youth work, for example running a camp. The employer does not have to pay wages for it.
73253.m: Young people up to 30 can take up to a week's leave for youth work.

73254.q: From when may the employer reduce holidays if an employee is ill through no fault of their own?
a: From the second full month of absence
From the first day of illness
From the second week of illness
Never, not even after a year
73254.e: Under Art. 329b CO, a reduction for absence through no fault of your own is only allowed if it lasts more than one month in total. For the second and each further full month, holidays may be cut by one twelfth.
73254.m: Short illnesses that are not your fault may not reduce your holidays.

73255.q: What is the wage after deduction of all social insurance contributions on the payslip called?
73255.e: The gross wage is the agreed wage before deductions. After deducting social insurance contributions and any other deductions, the net wage remains and is paid out.
73255.m: The net wage is the amount that actually arrives in your account.

73256.q: Is a 13th month's salary required by law in Switzerland?
a: No, only if it has been agreed
Yes, from the second year of service
73256.e: The CO has no legal entitlement to a 13th month's salary. It only exists if it is agreed in the employment contract, a collective agreement or through long practice.
73256.m: There is only a 13th month's salary if it has been agreed.

73257.q: Under the CO, when must the monthly wage be paid at the latest if nothing else has been agreed?
a: At the end of each month
On the 15th of the following month
At the end of each quarter
At the end of the calendar year
73257.e: Art. 323 CO states that, without another agreement or practice, wages are to be paid at the end of each month. The employer must also hand over a written statement.
73257.m: Wages are usually due at the end of the month.

73258.q: What is the gross wage for 160 working hours at 28.50 francs per hour?
73258.e: You multiply the hours by the hourly rate: 160 times 28.50 francs gives 4,560 francs.
73258.m: With an hourly wage, the gross wage is the number of hours times the hourly rate.

73259.q: Which document do employees receive from their employer every year for their tax return?
73259.e: The salary statement sums up all wage payments and deductions for a year. It is attached to the tax return.
73259.m: For your tax return you need your employer's salary statement.

73260.q: From whose wages is withholding tax typically deducted directly in Switzerland?
a: Foreign employees without a C settlement permit
Only apprentices in their first year
All employees with a part-time job
73260.e: Foreign employees without a C settlement permit are usually taxed at source. The employer deducts the tax directly from the wages and passes it on to the canton.
73260.m: The employer deducts withholding tax directly from the wages.

73261.q: What applies to family allowances for children aged 16 and over who are still in education?
a: They receive the higher education allowance
There is no allowance at all any more
They receive half the child allowance
The allowance goes to the child as wages
73261.e: For children up to 16 there is the child allowance. From 16, during education up to the age of 25 at most, there is the higher education allowance. The cantons can provide more than the minimum.
73261.m: From 16, those in education get the higher education allowance.

73262.q: What is the monthly wage if an annual salary of 71,500 francs is paid in 13 equal parts?
73262.e: With 13 monthly payments, you divide the annual salary by 13: 71,500 divided by 13 gives exactly 5,500 francs.
73262.m: With a 13th month's salary, you divide the annual salary by thirteen.

73263.q: What percentage of their gross wage do employees pay for AHV, IV and EO together (as of 2026)?
73263.e: The total contribution to AHV (old-age insurance), IV (disability insurance) and EO (loss of earnings insurance) is 10.6 per cent of the wage. Employers and employees each pay half, so 5.3 per cent each.
73263.m: 5.3 per cent of the gross wage goes to AHV, IV and EO.

73264.q: What percentage is deducted from employees for unemployment insurance up to the maximum wage (as of 2026)?
73264.e: The contribution to unemployment insurance is 2.2 per cent up to an annual wage of 148,200 francs. Employers and employees each pay 1.1 per cent.
73264.m: Employees pay 1.1 per cent of their wage to unemployment insurance.

73265.q: How many francs are deducted for AHV, IV and EO from a gross wage of 5,000 francs (rate 5.3 per cent)?
73265.e: 5.3 per cent of 5,000 francs is 5,000 times 0.053, so 265 francs.
73265.m: You work out percentage deductions by multiplying the gross wage by the percentage.

73266.q: What is the amount called that is deducted from the annual wage in the pension fund to calculate the insured wage?
73266.e: In occupational pensions, not the whole wage is insured. The coordination deduction is taken off the annual wage because part of the income is already covered by the AHV. The deductible and the excess belong to health insurance.
73266.m: The insured wage in the pension fund is the wage minus the coordination deduction.

73267.q: Which insurance belongs to the second pillar of the Swiss pension system?
73267.e: The first pillar is the state AHV/IV, the second is occupational pension provision (pension fund) under the BVG, and the third is private provision. The second pillar is funded by wage deductions and employer contributions.
73267.m: The pension fund forms the second pillar of retirement provision.

73268.q: Who pays the premium for insurance against workplace accidents?
73268.e: Under the Accident Insurance Act, the employer pays the premiums for workplace accidents and occupational diseases. The premium for non-work accidents, on the other hand, may be deducted from employees' wages.
73268.m: Only the employer pays for workplace accident insurance.

73269.q: From how many working hours per week with one employer are you also insured against non-work accidents?
73269.e: Anyone who works at least eight hours a week for one employer is also insured against accidents in their free time through accident insurance. With fewer hours, the health insurer must provide accident cover.
73269.m: From eight hours a week, the employer's accident insurance also covers accidents in your free time.

73270.q: From when do people in work in Switzerland have to pay AHV contributions on their wages?
a: From the end of their apprenticeship
73270.e: People in work pay AHV contributions from 1 January after turning 17. People not in work only have to pay from 1 January after their 20th birthday.
73270.m: Apprentices already pay AHV contributions from the year after their 17th birthday.

73271.q: How long is the probation period in a permanent employment contract if nothing has been agreed?
73271.e: Under Art. 335b CO, the first month of a permanent employment counts as the probation period. Anything different must be agreed in writing, in a standard employment contract or in a collective agreement.
73271.m: Without an agreement, the first month is the probation period.

73272.q: Up to how many months at most may the probation period of an employment contract be extended under the CO?
73272.e: Art. 335b CO allows a probation period of at most three months by written agreement. Longer probation periods are not allowed.
73272.m: The probation period in an employment contract may last at most three months.

73273.q: Under the CO, what notice period applies during the probation period if nothing else has been agreed?
73273.e: During the probation period, the employment can be ended at any time with seven days' notice under Art. 335b CO. The notice does not have to end at the end of a month.
73273.m: During the probation period the notice period is seven days.

73274.q: What happens to the probation period if someone is off ill during it?
a: It is shortened by the illness
73274.e: Art. 335b para. 3 CO states that the probation period is extended accordingly in case of illness, accident or a legal duty not taken on voluntarily. That way the time to get to know each other stays the same length.
73274.m: Illness during the probation period extends it by the time missed.

73275.q: Under the CO, how long may the probation period in an apprenticeship contract last?
a: Exactly one whole year of training
73275.e: Under Art. 344a CO, the probation period in an apprenticeship may be no less than one and no more than three months. Without an agreement, a probation period of three months applies.
73275.m: In an apprenticeship, the probation period lasts between one and three months.

73276.q: Up to what length can the probation period of an apprenticeship exceptionally be extended with the cantonal authority's consent?
73276.e: Art. 344a para. 4 CO allows the apprenticeship probation period to be extended to six months. For this the parties must agree and the cantonal authority must consent.
73276.m: An apprenticeship probation period can exceptionally last up to six months.

73277.q: Do the protection periods during illness (notice at an inopportune time) also apply during the probation period?
a: No, only after the probation period ends
Yes, from the first working day
73277.e: Protection against notice at an inopportune time under Art. 336c CO expressly applies only after the probation period has ended. During the probation period, notice may therefore be given even during illness.
73277.m: During the probation period there is no protection against dismissal because of illness.

73278.q: Under the CO, what notice period applies in the first year of service after the probation period?
73278.e: Art. 335c CO provides for a period of one month in the first year of service, always to the end of a month. The longer the employment lasts, the longer the notice periods become.
73278.m: In the first year of service you can give notice with one month's notice.

73279.q: Under the CO, what notice period applies from the tenth year of service?
73279.e: Under Art. 335c CO, the notice period from the tenth year of service is three months, always to the end of a month. The contract may differ, but only in writing.
73279.m: After nine years of service, the notice period is three months.

73280.q: Someone in their third year of service gives notice on 15 March with the legal notice period. When does the employment end?
73280.e: In the third year of service, a period of two months to the end of a month applies. From 15 March, two full months have only passed on 15 May, so the employment ends at the next month end, 31 May.
73280.m: The notice period always runs to the end of a month.

73281.q: When does written notice legally count as given?
a: When it is taken to the post office
When it is confirmed by a court
73281.e: Notice is a statement that has to be received. What matters is the moment it comes within the recipient's sphere of control, not the date of the letter or when it was posted.
73281.m: Notice only takes effect once the other side has received it.

73282.q: Under the CO, may different notice periods apply to employers and employees?
a: No, they must be the same length
Yes, employers may have shorter ones
Yes, apprentices always have longer ones
Yes, if the wage is high
73282.e: Art. 335a CO requires notice periods of equal length for both parties. If an agreement says otherwise, the longer period applies to both.
73282.m: Notice periods must be the same for both parties to the contract.

73283.q: How many days does the protection period during illness last in the second to fifth year of service?
73283.e: Art. 336c CO forbids the employer to give notice during illness that is not the employee's fault for 30 days in the first year of service, 90 days in the second to fifth year and 180 days from the sixth year.
73283.m: In the second to fifth year of service, a 90-day protection period protects against dismissal during illness.

73284.q: Under the CO, how many months' wages can compensation for unfair dismissal amount to at most?
73284.e: An unfair dismissal remains valid, but under Art. 336a CO the court can award compensation of at most six months' wages. For this you must object in writing before the notice period ends.
73284.m: For unfair dismissal there is at most six months' wages in compensation.

73285.q: Under the CO, what is required for dismissal without notice?
a: The end of the probation period
73285.e: Under Art. 337 CO, employment can be ended without notice at any time for serious reasons. A serious reason exists if continuing in good faith can no longer reasonably be expected, for example after theft.
73285.m: Dismissal without notice needs a serious reason.

73286.q: Under the CO, when may employees ask for an employment reference?
a: Only on the last working day
Only after five years of service
73286.e: Art. 330a CO allows you to ask for a reference at any time. During employment it is called an interim reference.
73286.m: You can ask for an employment reference at any time.

73287.q: What does a full employment reference contain in addition to the type and length of the work?
73287.e: According to Art. 330a CO, the full reference covers the type and length of the employment as well as performance and conduct. Details of wages or health usually do not belong in it.
73287.m: A full reference assesses performance and conduct.

73288.q: What is a reference called that, on request, only confirms the type and length of the employment?
73288.e: On special request, the employer only has to confirm the type and length under Art. 330a para. 2 CO. This confirmation of employment is also called a simple reference.
73288.m: A confirmation of employment only states the type and length of the work.

73289.q: Which two principles must an employment reference meet at the same time?
73289.e: A reference must be true, but should also be worded with goodwill so that the person's career is not made harder than necessary. If the two conflict, truth comes first.
73289.m: An employment reference must be true and at the same time well-meaning.

73290.q: When is an interim reference particularly useful?
73290.e: An interim reference is issued while the employment is still running. Typical occasions are a change of manager, a restructuring or a job application.
73290.m: An interim reference records your performance during employment.

73291.q: Which wording counts in practice as a very good rating in Swiss employment references?
a: He made an effort to carry out the tasks
73291.e: Many references use graded standard phrases. The phrase “always to our fullest satisfaction” counts as the top mark, while “made an effort” counts as unsatisfactory.
73291.m: The words “always” and “fullest” in references stand for very good performance.

73292.q: What can employees do if their employment reference contains untrue statements?
73292.e: Because the CO gives a right to a correct reference, you can ask for a correction. If necessary, the claim can be enforced at the labour court.
73292.m: A false reference can be corrected.

73293.q: Under the CO, which reference do apprentices receive from their training company at the end of the apprenticeship?
73293.e: Under Art. 346a CO, after the apprenticeship ends the employer issues a reference about the trade learned and the length of the apprenticeship. On request it also covers skills, performance and conduct.
73293.m: After the apprenticeship, the company gives you an apprenticeship reference.

73294.q: Up to what age do employees count as young people under the Labour Act?
73294.e: Under the Labour Act, people up to the age of 18 count as young people. Special protective rules apply to them, for example regarding working hours and dangerous work.
73294.m: Under the Labour Act you are a young person until 18.

73295.q: From what age may young people in Switzerland basically be employed in regular work?
73295.e: Art. 30 of the Labour Act basically forbids employing young people under 15. Exceptions apply to light work from 13 and to cultural, artistic or sporting performances.
73295.m: Regular employment is usually only allowed from 15.

73296.q: How many hours a week at most may 13 to 15-year-olds do light work during the school term?
73296.e: The Youth Employment Protection Ordinance (ArGV 5) allows young people from 13 to do light work during term time for at most 3 hours a day and 9 hours a week. More hours are possible in the holidays.
73296.m: School pupils from 13 may do at most nine hours of light work a week alongside school.

73297.q: Under the Labour Act, how many hours a day at most may young people work?
73297.e: Art. 31 of the Labour Act limits young people's daily working time to nine hours. It also may not be longer than that of the other employees in the company.
73297.m: Young people work at most nine hours a day.

73298.q: Under the Labour Act, until what time in the evening may young people over 16 work at the latest?
73298.e: Under Art. 31 of the Labour Act, young people up to 16 may work until 8 pm at the latest and young people over 16 until 10 pm at the latest. Night and Sunday work is only allowed with a special permit.
73298.m: Young people over 16 may work until 10 pm at the latest.

73299.q: How long must the daily rest period for young people be at least?
73299.e: The Youth Employment Protection Ordinance requires a daily rest period of at least twelve consecutive hours for young people. For adults it is eleven hours.
73299.m: Young people need at least twelve hours of rest between two working days.

73300.q: Do lessons at vocational school count as working time for young people?
a: Yes, they count as working time
No, they count as free time
Only if they are in the evening
73300.e: Art. 31 of the Labour Act states that compulsory lessons during working hours count as working time. So school days count towards the maximum working hours.
73300.m: Time at vocational school counts as working time for apprentices.

73301.q: What rule applies to dangerous work for young people in basic vocational training?
a: Allowed from 15 if the training ordinance provides for it
Only allowed with the parents' permission
73301.e: Dangerous work is basically forbidden for young people. Exceptions apply to apprentices from 15 if the training ordinance of the trade provides for it and accompanying safety measures are followed.
73301.m: Dangerous work is only allowed for young people in an apprenticeship and with safety measures.

73302.q: Which federal law banned factory work for children under 14 in 1877?
73302.e: The Federal Factory Act of 1877 introduced the 11-hour day and banned factory work for children under 14. It is regarded as a milestone in protecting workers in Switzerland.
73302.m: The Factory Act of 1877 banned child labour in factories.

73303.q: Between whom is a collective employment agreement (GAV) made?
a: Employee associations and employers or their associations
73303.e: Under Art. 356 CO, employee associations (trade unions) make a collective agreement with employers or employers' associations. It sets working conditions for whole industries or companies.
73303.m: A collective agreement is made between trade unions and the employers' side.

73304.q: What form must a collective employment agreement have under the CO?
73304.e: Art. 356c CO requires written form for making a collective agreement. This also applies to joining and terminating it.
73304.m: A collective employment agreement must be made in writing.

73305.q: What does it mean when a collective agreement is declared generally binding?
a: It applies to all companies in the industry
It only applies to union members
It only applies for one year
It only applies in one company
73305.e: When it is declared generally binding, a collective agreement is extended to all employers and employees in an industry, including non-members. The Federal Council is responsible if the agreement covers several cantons, otherwise the canton.
73305.m: A generally binding collective agreement applies to the whole industry.

73306.q: What does the peace obligation in a collective employment agreement require?
a: No industrial action on matters it regulates
No pay rises without a court
No trade unions in the company
73306.e: Under Art. 357a CO, the parties agree to keep industrial peace on the matters regulated in the agreement. Strikes and lockouts on these matters are ruled out while it runs.
73306.m: The peace obligation forbids strikes over points regulated in the collective agreement.

73307.q: Which agreement of 1937 in the metal and engineering industry is regarded as the foundation of Swiss social partnership?
73307.e: On 19 July 1937, employers and trade unions in the metal and engineering industry agreed to settle conflicts through negotiation instead of strikes. This Peace Agreement had a lasting influence on social partnership.
73307.m: The Peace Agreement of 1937 relied on negotiation instead of strikes.

73308.q: What applies if an individual employment contract differs from the collective agreement to the employees' disadvantage?
a: The collective agreement's rule takes priority
Both rules apply at the same time
The individual contract applies for one year
73308.e: Under Art. 357 CO, differing agreements between bound parties are void and are replaced by the collective agreement. Differences in the employees' favour are allowed (favourability principle).
73308.m: An individual contract may only differ from the collective agreement in the employees' favour.

73309.q: What is the collective employment agreement for the main construction industry in Switzerland called?
73309.e: The National Framework Agreement (LMV) sets wages, working hours and other conditions in the main construction industry. It has been declared generally binding and is negotiated between the industry's employers' association and the trade unions.
73309.m: The National Framework Agreement applies in the main construction industry.

73310.q: Which is the largest trade union in Switzerland by number of members?
73310.e: Unia was formed in 2004 from the merger of several unions, including GBI and SMUV. It mainly represents people working in industry, construction, trades and services and is the largest union in Switzerland.
73310.m: Unia is the largest trade union in Switzerland.

73311.q: Which umbrella organisation, founded in 1880, unites most of Switzerland's trade unions?
73311.e: The Swiss Trade Union Federation (SGB) was founded in 1880 and is the largest umbrella organisation of employee organisations. The second umbrella organisation is Travail.Suisse.
73311.m: The Swiss Trade Union Federation is the largest umbrella organisation of trade unions.

73312.q: Under what condition is a strike allowed in Switzerland according to the Federal Constitution?
a: If it lasts at least a month
If the Federal Council approves it
If it takes place on a Sunday
73312.e: The Federal Constitution allows strikes if they concern employment relations, for example wages or working hours. In addition, no peace obligation from a collective agreement may stand in the way.
73312.m: Strikes are only allowed over questions of work.

73313.q: Which event in November 1918 was the largest general strike in Swiss history?
73313.e: From 12 to 14 November 1918, around 250,000 people stopped work in the national general strike. It was led by the Olten Action Committee.
73313.m: The general strike of 1918 was the largest strike in Swiss history.

73314.q: Which demand of the general strike of 1918 was already put into practice in 1919/1920?
73314.e: The Olten Action Committee demanded, among other things, the 48-hour week, the AHV and women's suffrage. The 48-hour week was largely introduced in 1919/1920, the AHV only in 1948 and women's suffrage in 1971.
73314.m: The 48-hour week was introduced soon after the general strike.

73315.q: Which United Nations organisation for labour matters has its headquarters in Geneva?
73315.e: The International Labour Organization (ILO) was founded in 1919 and is based in Geneva. It is made up of three groups: governments, employers and workers.
73315.m: The International Labour Organization ILO is based in Geneva.

73317.q: What is the main task of an employers' association such as the Swiss Employers' Association?
a: Representing companies' interests towards trade unions and politics
Paying daily allowances to the unemployed
Setting the wages of all employees
73317.e: Employers' associations represent companies, for example in negotiations on collective agreements and in social policy. Their counterpart is the trade unions, which represent employees.
73317.m: Employers' associations represent companies, trade unions represent employees.

73318.q: What does the umbrella organisation economiesuisse campaign for?
a: The interests of the Swiss economy in politics
73318.e: economiesuisse is the large umbrella organisation of the Swiss economy. It represents companies from all industries, for example in votes and laws on trade, taxes or energy.
73318.m: economiesuisse is the voice of business in politics.

73319.q: Which association mainly represents small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Switzerland?
73319.e: The Swiss Trade Association (sgv) was founded in 1879 and calls itself the largest umbrella organisation of the Swiss economy. It mainly represents SMEs and trade businesses.
73319.m: The Trade Association campaigns for small and medium-sized enterprises.

73320.q: Which employers' association represents Switzerland's mechanical, electrical and metal industry?
73320.e: Swissmem is the association of the Swiss mechanical, electrical and metal industry (MEM industry) and related technology sectors. It negotiates the MEM collective agreement with the trade unions.
73320.m: Swissmem represents the mechanical, electrical and metal industry.

73321.q: Which employers' association represents the companies of the main construction industry in negotiations with the trade unions?
73321.e: The Swiss Master Builders' Association (SBV) represents companies in the main construction industry. It negotiates the industry's collective agreement with the trade unions Unia and Syna.
73321.m: The Master Builders' Association represents construction companies in contract negotiations.

73322.q: What is the body of employer and employee representatives that checks compliance with a collective agreement called?
73322.e: Joint commissions have an equal number of representatives from both social partners. They check in companies whether the rules of a collective agreement are being followed and can charge inspection costs or contractual penalties.
73322.m: Joint commissions check compliance with collective agreements.

73323.q: How many hours a week does someone work on a 60 per cent workload if full time is 42 hours?
73323.e: You calculate 42 hours times 0.6. That gives 25.2 hours a week.
73323.m: The workload as a percentage shows what share of full time you work.

73324.q: What is the monthly wage on an 80 per cent workload if the full-time wage is 6,200 francs?
73324.e: Part-time wages are proportional to the workload: 6,200 francs times 0.8 gives 4,960 francs.
73324.m: Part-time, you get wages in proportion to your workload.

73325.q: Below what level of employment do you count as working part time according to the Federal Statistical Office?
73325.e: The Federal Statistical Office counts people working less than 90 per cent as part-time. Anyone working 90 per cent or more counts as full-time in the statistics.
73325.m: Statistically, part time in Switzerland begins below a 90 per cent workload.

73326.q: How many days' holiday per year at least does someone have who works three days a week and is entitled to four weeks?
73326.e: Four weeks of holiday equal four times the three working days per week. 4 times 3 gives 12 days of holiday.
73326.m: Part-time holiday days are holiday weeks times working days per week.

73327.q: What is a working model called in which two people share one full-time job?
73327.e: In job sharing, two or more people share one job with joint tasks and responsibility. When two people share a management role, it is also called top sharing.
73327.m: In job sharing, several people share one job.

73328.q: Why is the pension fund often incomplete for part-time employees with several small jobs?
a: Because of the entry threshold and the coordination deduction
Because the AHV does not recognise part-time work
Because the health insurer forbids it
73328.e: The BVG entry threshold and the coordination deduction are applied per employer. With several small jobs, little or no wage is therefore insured in the second pillar.
73328.m: Several small part-time jobs often lead to gaps in the pension fund.

73329.q: How does the share of people working part time in Switzerland compare with the rest of Europe?
a: It is among the highest in Europe
It is among the lowest in Europe
Part-time work is hardly common in Switzerland
73329.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, more than a third of people in work in Switzerland work part time, and among women more than half. That puts Switzerland among the countries with the highest part-time rates in Europe.
73329.m: Compared with the rest of Europe, very many people in Switzerland work part time.

73330.q: What is legally problematic about on-call work?
a: If the time spent on standby is not paid
If the wage is paid monthly
If there is a written contract
73330.e: With on-call work, the person has to wait for assignments. According to Federal Supreme Court rulings, standby time must also be paid, though not necessarily at the full wage, and the employer may not simply pass the risk of fluctuating work onto the employee.
73330.m: Standby time in on-call work must also be paid.

73331.q: How long does a full-time course at a college of higher education (HF) last at least?
73331.e: The minimum rules for HF courses require at least two years full time. Part time alongside work, the same course lasts at least three years.
73331.m: An HF course lasts at least two years full time and at least three years part time.

73332.q: How can you often complete a course at a college of higher education (HF)?
a: Full time or part time alongside work
Only as a distance course abroad
73332.e: Many HF courses are offered full time or part time alongside work. Part time the training takes longer, but you keep earning wages.
73332.m: You can often attend an HF alongside your job.

73333.q: What is the protected title after an HF qualification in nursing?
73333.e: HF graduates hold a title on the pattern “dipl. profession HF”. In nursing it is dipl. Pflegefachfrau HF or dipl. Pflegefachmann HF (registered nurse HF).
73333.m: HF titles begin with “dipl.” and end with the abbreviation HF.

73334.q: Which body gives federal recognition to the individual HF courses?
a: The State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation
The Swiss Conference of Cantonal Ministers of Education
The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs
73334.e: SERI does not recognise the schools as a whole, but each individual course. Supervision of the schools lies with the cantons.
73334.m: SERI recognises the courses of colleges of higher education in Switzerland.

73335.q: Who are courses at colleges of higher education mainly intended for?
a: Professionals who have completed basic training
73335.e: Colleges of higher education belong to higher vocational education. They build on an apprenticeship or another upper secondary qualification.
73335.m: The HF is aimed at trained professionals.

73336.q: Which document sets the content of an HF course for the whole of Switzerland?
73336.e: Framework curricula are drawn up by the professional organisations together with the education providers. They describe the job profile and the skills to be achieved.
73336.m: The framework curriculum decides what is learned in an HF course.

73337.q: Which further education in the same field is open to you after an HF diploma?
73337.e: Postgraduate courses (NDS HF) deepen or widen your skills after the diploma. HF graduates can also attend further education at universities.
73337.m: After the HF diploma you can specialise further with a postgraduate course.

73338.q: What is the usual entry requirement for an HF course in technology?
a: A relevant vocational qualification with EFZ
A bachelor's from a university of applied sciences
73338.e: In technology, courses usually require a suitable Federal VET Diploma (EFZ). In other fields an upper secondary qualification with an aptitude assessment is often enough.
73338.m: Anyone who wants to become a technician HF first needs a suitable EFZ.

73339.q: What is typical of studying at a university of applied sciences compared with a university?
a: It is more focused on practice
It is only for people over 40
73339.e: Universities of applied sciences teach close to practice, often working together with companies. Universities are more focused on basic research.
73339.m: Universities of applied sciences are practice-oriented.

73340.q: How many public universities of applied sciences are there in Switzerland (as of 2025)?
73340.e: The eight public universities of applied sciences are BFH, HES-SO, FHNW, HSLU, SUPSI, OST, ZFH and, since 2020, the University of Applied Sciences of the Grisons. There are also private ones.
73340.m: Switzerland has eight public universities of applied sciences.

73341.q: Which qualification is the standard route into a bachelor's degree at a university of applied sciences?
a: A vocational baccalaureate in a related trade
A federal certificate from a professional exam
73341.e: The classic route to a university of applied sciences is an apprenticeship with a vocational baccalaureate in a matching field. Other qualifications are possible with extra conditions.
73341.m: The royal road to a university of applied sciences is the vocational baccalaureate.

73342.q: How many ECTS credits does a bachelor's degree at a Swiss university of applied sciences involve?
73342.e: A bachelor's involves 180 ECTS credits, which equals three years of full-time study. 60 ECTS credits are awarded per year of study.
73342.m: A bachelor's degree equals 180 ECTS credits or three full-time years.

73343.q: Which academic degree can Swiss universities of applied sciences not award on their own?
73343.e: The right to award doctorates lies with the universities. Universities of applied sciences only offer doctoral programmes in cooperation with universities.
73343.m: In Switzerland doctorates are awarded by the universities and ETH.

73344.q: Which university of applied sciences serves Italian-speaking Switzerland?
73344.e: The Scuola universitaria professionale della Svizzera italiana (SUPSI) has its sites in Ticino. HES-SO, by contrast, is the university of applied sciences of western Switzerland.
73344.m: SUPSI is the university of applied sciences of Italian-speaking Switzerland.

73345.q: Which university of applied sciences brings together schools from all the cantons of French-speaking Switzerland?
73345.e: The Haute école spécialisée de Suisse occidentale (HES-SO) is a network of schools in the cantons of the Romandie. By number of students it is one of the largest universities of applied sciences.
73345.m: HES-SO is the university of applied sciences of western Switzerland.

73346.q: Which reform introduced bachelor's and master's degrees at Swiss universities?
73346.e: The Bologna reform made degree courses in Europe comparable. Since then Swiss universities have also had bachelor's and master's degrees.
73346.m: Bachelor's and master's degrees came with the Bologna reform.

73347.q: What is a CAS (Certificate of Advanced Studies)?
a: A short further education course at a university
An apprenticeship qualification for young people
A licence for driving a car
73347.e: A CAS is the smallest further education course at a university and usually lasts a few months. Larger ones are the DAS and the MAS.
73347.m: A CAS is a short university further education course.

73348.q: Which is the oldest university in Switzerland?
73348.e: Pope Pius II issued the founding bull in 1459, and the University of Basel opened in 1460. The other Swiss universities were founded much later.
73348.m: Since 1460, Basel has had the oldest university in Switzerland.

73349.q: Which Swiss university is officially bilingual in German and French?
73349.e: The University of Fribourg lies on the language border and offers many courses in German and French. You can also gain bilingual degrees there.
73349.m: At the University of Fribourg you study in German, French or both.

73350.q: In which canton is the Università della Svizzera italiana (USI)?
73350.e: USI was founded in 1996 and has its sites in Lugano and Mendrisio. It is the only university in Italian-speaking Switzerland.
73350.m: USI in Lugano is the university of Italian-speaking Switzerland.

73351.q: Roughly how many hours of work does one ECTS credit equal?
73351.e: An ECTS credit measures the total workload including lectures, self-study and exams. A full-time year of 60 credits therefore equals about 1,500 to 1,800 hours.
73351.m: One ECTS credit stands for about 25 to 30 hours of work.

73352.q: Which declaration of 1999 led to the introduction of bachelor's and master's degrees at European universities?
73352.e: The education ministers of 29 European countries, including Switzerland, signed the Bologna Declaration in 1999. The aim was a common European higher education area with comparable degrees.
73352.m: The Bologna reform brought bachelor's and master's degrees to Swiss universities.

73353.q: Which test decides admission to medical studies in German-speaking Switzerland?
a: The aptitude test for medical studies
73353.e: Because there are more applicants than places, numbers are restricted in human medicine. The aptitude test (EMS) checks abilities such as understanding texts and spatial thinking.
73353.m: To study medicine in German-speaking Switzerland you must pass an aptitude test.

73354.q: How many ECTS credits does a master's degree at a Swiss university involve?
73354.e: A university master's usually takes one and a half to two years full time. That equals 90 to 120 ECTS credits.
73354.m: A master's usually involves 90 to 120 ECTS credits.

73355.q: Which university is the largest in Switzerland by number of students (as of 2024)?
73355.e: About 28,000 students are enrolled at the University of Zurich. In 1833 it was the first university in Europe to be founded by a democratic state.
73355.m: The University of Zurich is the largest university in Switzerland.

73356.q: By when must you usually apply for a course starting in the autumn semester at a Swiss university?
73356.e: Most universities set 30 April as the application deadline for the autumn semester. For medicine an earlier deadline applies because of the aptitude test.
73356.m: If you want to start studying in autumn, you usually apply by the end of April.

73357.q: How can you prepare for the central Passerelle exam?
a: As you like, for example with a course or by self-study
Only with three years of grammar school
Not at all, the exam needs no preparation
73357.e: For the central exam you can choose how to prepare. Many attend a preparation course, others study on their own. The exam covers general subjects such as languages, maths, sciences, history and geography.
73357.m: You can prepare for the central Passerelle however you like.

73358.q: Why is the supplementary exam after the vocational baccalaureate called the Passerelle?
a: The French word means bridge or crossing
It is the name of its inventor
It is a town in the canton of Vaud
73358.e: “Passerelle” is French for footbridge. The exam builds a bridge from the vocational baccalaureate to university.
73358.m: The Passerelle is a bridge to university.

73359.q: Which certificates entitle you to register for the Passerelle supplementary exam?
a: A vocational baccalaureate or a recognised specialised baccalaureate
An EFZ without a vocational baccalaureate
73359.e: People with a federal vocational baccalaureate certificate or a nationally recognised specialised baccalaureate certificate are admitted. An EFZ alone is not enough.
73359.m: For the Passerelle you need a vocational or specialised baccalaureate.

73360.q: With a vocational baccalaureate, what applies to access to higher education?
a: Universities of applied sciences are open, for university you need the Passerelle
All universities are open without any further exam
Only university is open, not universities of applied sciences
73360.e: The vocational baccalaureate opens the way to a university of applied sciences, usually in a matching field. For university and ETH you also need the Passerelle supplementary exam.
73360.m: Vocational baccalaureate: straight to a university of applied sciences, to university with the Passerelle.

73361.q: Which subject is examined in the Passerelle supplementary exam?
73361.e: The exam covers the first language, a second national language or English, mathematics, sciences, and the humanities and social sciences. Business subjects from the vocational baccalaureate are not examined again.
73361.m: The Passerelle mainly examines general Matura subjects.

73362.q: Which subjects belong to the humanities and social sciences area of the Passerelle?
73362.e: The humanities and social sciences area covers history and geography. Candidates already know subjects such as economics and law from the vocational baccalaureate.
73362.m: History and geography are part of the Passerelle exam.

73363.q: How long is the preparation course required for a Passerelle exam taken at a school?
73363.e: Anyone taking the exam at a recognised Matura school must attend the one-year preparation course there. For the central exam, preparation is up to you.
73363.m: The preparation course for the Passerelle usually lasts one year.

73364.q: Which qualification is a vocational baccalaureate together with a passed Passerelle legally equal to?
a: A bachelor's from a university of applied sciences
73364.e: Together with the vocational or specialised baccalaureate certificate, the Passerelle counts in Switzerland as equivalent to the grammar school Matura. Universities abroad decide for themselves whether to recognise it.
73364.m: With the Passerelle you are on a par with the grammar school Matura for university access.
